_comment: THE PRODUCTION-READINESS LEDGER.  This file is the single deterministic
answer to 'is MXFS production ready?' — the `open_defects` criterion FAILS
while any entry below has status != RESOLVED, so showstat can never read
all-green while a credible defect is known-open.
WHY THIS EXISTS (ccloop c7ee71c6 sess21, user directive): the board read
20/20 green through a soft lockup that killed a node for 522 s, an ILOCK
assertion failure on 3 of 4 nodes, and a mkdir(2) that returned success
with the entry existing nowhere.  Behavioural criteria alone cannot carry
this weight: the ones that catch intermittent defects go green whenever a
run gets lucky, and 'this run did not reproduce it' is not 'fixed'.
RULE 6: an entry may move to RESOLVED under exactly two dispositions —
DISPROVED         : direct evidence the reported behaviour was not a defect
FIXED_AND_VERIFIED: RULE 4 proved the cause, the patch targets THAT cause,
and testing which exercises the cause passes cleanly
'Cannot reproduce', 'rare', 'a clean run', 'a plausible explanation', a
workaround, or documentation are NOT dispositions.  Do not delete an entry
to make the board green — that is the one thing this file exists to prevent.

defects.summary: Foreign/adopted journal-slice replay applies BUFFER (and dquot/icreate) image records gated only by upstream XFS_LSN_CMP, but LSNs are incomparable across per-node slices - replay can silently revert survivor-written dir blocks/AG state (false-APPLY) or drop the dead node's fsync-acked changes (false-SKIP)
defects.evidence: Code audit sess32 (session 14): pal/linux/xfs_buf_item_recover.c:1061 (lsn && XFS_LSN_CMP(lsn, current_lsn) >= 0 -> skip) has no foreign gate; xfs_dquot_item_recover.c:145 same; xfs/xfs_log_recover.c:3502 skips the sb-LSN check with a comment stating per-node slice LSNs are not comparable - the same incomparability applies to every buffer record. Inode records ARE correctly gated (di_changecount, node-independent, xfs_inode_item_recover.c:410). The live-replay design comment (xfs_log.c ~712) claims mount-time re-replay is 'LSN-gated and therefore a no-op' - false cross-node. Exposure paths: (1) live foreign replay by the elected survivor; (2) mount-time claim of a dirty slice (slot%%node_count mapping) hours/days after the death, after survivors have rewritten the same blocks; (3) late intent processing by the mount-time claimer against a moved-on filesystem (extent free against possibly-reallocated ranges). GPT sess32 ruling: stop-ship class; containment = skip untagged buf/dquot/icreate images in live foreign replay (inode cc-gate stays); full fix = authority tokens {resource_id, grant_incarnation, tenure_id} captured at logging time + durable held-set manifest + IMAGE_REPLAY_DONE marker gating purge and mount-time image suppression. See ccmemory ccloop-c7ee71c6-sess32-GPT-ruling-A-D-foreign-replay-stop-ship. || SESS384 32/caw INCIDENT 2026-08-20T20:32:39-20:35:54Z on 0.19.6 sv 2D543FD0F9F9B833BCA747F -- ONE incident, measured end to end, that chains five open entries and ended with 0 of 32 nodes usable. Board line for it: `FAIL rsync_paired nodes_pass=0/32 states:NO_TERMINAL_RECORD=32 hostload=20.30 [60s/60s]`. TIMELINE (dmesg -T, all 32 nodes swept): (1) 20:32:39-44 test10,test14,test2 shut down `Corruption of in-memory data (0x8) detected at xfs_trans_cancel+0x15e/0x170 (xfs/xfs_trans.c:1088)` = D-RSYNC-RENAME-DIRTY-CANCEL-MASS-SHUTDOWN-361; test29 same window `Metadata I/O Error at xfs_inactive_ifree+0x566`. (2) 20:32:54-20:33:31 thirteen more (test1,4,9,12,15,16,17,18,19,20,21,22,27) shut down identically: `P-NOINO-RELFENCE-WEDGE ino=<n> -- shutdown (un-durable no-inode lock NOT released)` then `Metadata I/O Error (0x1) detected at mxfs_dlm_noino_bast_work_fn+0x19b/0x1b0 (xfs/xfs_mxfs_dlm.c:21274)` = D-NOINO-RELFENCE-AIL-FREEZE-474 arm A. 17 of 32 dead, matching #361's original 17/32 signature. (3) Survivors fence and elect; the FIRST elected replayer died mid-recovery, test26 (node 1957942981, slot 3) was re-elected for 15 pending slices. (4) Replay of 10 slices REFUSED: `P227-FR-TORN-UNPUBLISHED slot <n>: replay refused 2-3 committed unauthorized image(s) -- the victim's partial home-writeback cannot be ruled out, so publishing would publish a torn platter` -> `POLICY-REFUSED, rc=-117 refused=2 malformed=0 dvalid=1` = D-FOREIGN-REPLAY-UNGATED-IMAGES. (5) Each refusal published a terminal verdict. EIGHT were domain=AG-MASK (slots 1,5,6,8,11,17,21,27); TWO were domain=FSWIDE (slot 25 victim=915164091 digest=c3b40687; slot 29 victim=758930932 digest=2538e319). (6) Every survivor imported them -- `P241-RECOV-TERMINAL-IMPORT` -> `P240-QUAR-IMPORT ... fswide=1 ag_mask=0x0 phase=ADMITTED`. An FSWIDE quarantine EIOs the WHOLE filesystem, so all 15 nodes that never shut down were bricked too: `ls /mnt/shared` -> Input/output error on 32/32 nodes, verified 20:50Z, mounts still in /proc/mounts. = D-FOREIGN-REPLAY-REFUSAL-CLUSTERWIDE-SUICIDE-513. Forensics: /tmp/mxfs_sess384_incident/{test1,2,3,10,14,25,29}.dmesg.gz (full rings).
defects.mechanism: Per-node journal slices have independent LSN cycle/block numbering; any cross-slice LSN comparison is meaningless. Buffer replay decides apply-vs-skip by comparing the dead slice's record LSN against the on-disk block LSN stamped by whichever node last flushed that block from ITS slice.
defects.containment: SHIPPED 0.11.273-274, both arms A/B'd on the rig via tests/foreign_replay_ab.sh + rejoin flow: (1) LIVE foreign replay skips untagged buf/dquot/quotaoff/icreate images (P223, knob foreign_replay_untagged_apply=0 default; A/B victims test9/test10: 11-vs-0 skips, both arms full acked visibility 40/40 dirs+files+sizes — records were redundant because the destage kick lands metadata within ~ms of commit). (2) MOUNT-TIME: pass-2 (fresh) disklock claim marks the inherited slice ADOPTED (claim log prints it); xfs_log_mount sets XLOG_MXFS_ADOPTED_SLICE and recovery suppresses untagged images AND the dead incarnation's intents (P226) while inode records keep the cc gate; pass-1 own-stamp reclaim keeps full recovery (own-crash path, grants quarantined). A/B: test11 rejoin default=7 buf images suppressed, mount clean, node sees its full pre-death acked data 40/40/40; test12 rejoin with adopted_slice_full_replay=1 = legacy full replay, no suppression. RESIDUAL (documented, OPEN): held-at-death unlanded records of the skipped types are no longer applied by anyone (bounded durability gap, narrow in practice per the destage-kick timing); adopted-slice intent skip leaks the dead incarnation's incomplete extent-frees (counted via P226; space leak, not corruption). Both residuals close with the full token protocol.

Foreign replay of B's slice APPLIED the inode item (nlink->0, durable — P92/P19 read disk_nlink=0) but SKIPPED both untagged BUFFER images (P223-FR-UNTAGGED-SKIP type 0x123c n=2,n=3 = the dirent-removal dir block AND the AGI bucket-insert). defects.blocker_historical_record_lifetime: GATE BLOCKER (transferred from D-EX-GRANT-EPOCH-NOT-UNIQUE-TENURE-ID at its sess174 FIXED-AND-VERIFIED closure; scope BROADENED beyond replay): historical or delayed authority artifacts surviving a resource's release and later reacquisition from a different slot lineage — including replay records AND any delayed live-path messages, queued work, cached capabilities, or other persistent consumers.  The evaluator may NOT become authoritative until this is held.  Live-path options recorded: drain-before-rebind; an independent lineage discriminator; or explicit inclusion in this defect's gate design.  Verbatim residual copied from the #15 entry: PRE-EXISTING and NOT introduced by either epoch source, recorded here so it is not lost: if resource X's slot is tombstoned, recycled by a DIFFERENT resource, and X is later re-claimed at another slot index, X's epoch namespace restarts from that slot's lineage. Neither the generation source nor a per-slot +1 sequence closes that; only tuple-validation plus a cluster-monotonic component would. Do not treat the +1 change as closing it.

defects.summary: The disklock mount-incarnation identifier (struct mxfs_disklock_ctx.epoch, published as heartbeat record byte offset 24 and carried into every recovery descriptor as victim_epoch/owner_epoch/fence_prover_epoch) is a HARD-CODED ZERO.  Every incarnation-binding predicate in the recovery, fence-certificate and own-slot-CAS paths is therefore vacuous, and step 5.2 of D-FOREIGN-REPLAY-UNGATED-IMAGES (bind the authority token to the victim incarnation) is unimplementable until it is fixed.
defects.evidence: MEASURED sess83 on the live 32-node CAW rig, independently of the kernel module: raw dd of the 64-slot heartbeat region off the shared LUN (/dev/mapper/mpatha, disklock_offset=67117056 from tools/chk_mxfs -v, 512B records, epoch at byte offset 24), decoded in python3 -> all 31 live records read EPOCH=0; 'distinct EPOCH values across all live HB records: [0]'.  Corroborating: tree-wide grep finds exactly ONE write to ctx->epoch ('ctx->epoch = 0;' dlm/disklock.c:1145); every other occurrence is a read, and hb->epoch = ctx->epoch on every heartbeat/claim write (disklock.c:647, :2037, :4110, :4248).
defects.mechanism: Vacuous predicates, all dlm/disklock.c: (1) hb_own_record() :457 tests cur->epoch == ctx->epoch = 0==0, so a stale ACTIVE record left by our OWN previous incarnation reads as our live record and hb_foreign_kind()'s 'a different incarnation of this node owns the slot' branch :482 is unreachable; (2) desc.victim_epoch = cur->epoch :2483 :3121 = 0, so the durable recovery descriptor cannot name which incarnation of the victim it is recovering; (3) d->owner_epoch == ctx->epoch (:1604 :1702 :2380 :2437 :2892 :3080 :3368 :3511) collapses to owner_node == local_node, so a REJOINED incarnation of the same node adopts its own prior incarnation's recovery lease; (4) same for d->fence_prover_epoch == ctx->epoch (:2895 :3257) in the sess75/76 fence certificate; (5) the guard idiom 'if (victim_epoch && d->victim_epoch != victim_epoch) refuse' (:2462 :2954 :3069 :3489 ...) is SKIPPED at ~8 recovery sites (recovery_begin, takeover, fence_intent, fence_certify, claim, advance) because callers pass an epoch read from disk, i.e. 0; (6) mxfs_disklock_slot_holds_incarnation() degenerate; (7) :290 'return epoch == 0 || d->victim_epoch == epoch;' always true.
defects.containment: None.  The defect is silent: it weakens checks that already appear to pass.  No workaround exists and none is acceptable (RULE 6).
defects.next: CLOSED sess91.  Residual follow-up tracked on D-RECOV-ADVANCE-UNBOUNDED-RETRY: inject a same-node later incarnation attempting to advance a predecessor's descriptor and assert the owner-epoch predicate refuses it.
defects.found: sess83
defects.disposition: FIXED AND VERIFIED sess91.  CAUSE (RULE 4): tree-wide grep found exactly one write to the identifier, 'ctx->epoch = 0' (dlm/disklock.c:1145), and a raw O_DIRECT decode of the 64-slot heartbeat region on the live LUN read EPOCH=0 on all 31 live records (sess83).  PATCH: 0.11.420 gives every mount a random nonzero 64-bit incarnation per the sess83 RULE-5 ruling and threads it through the heartbeat, death, descriptor and fence-certificate paths.  VERIFICATION that exercises the cause, all on the live 32-node CAW rig: (a) sess88 — 32/32 on-disk incarnations nonzero, 32/32 distinct, bit lengths 58-64; the same measurement that returned '[0]' at sess83. (b) sess88 — a hard kill made all 31 survivors log P163-RECOVERY-PENDING naming the victim by its EXACT pre-kill on-disk incarnation, and P234-RECOV-FENCED carried that incarnation into the durable descriptor (ledger mechanism item 2). (c) sess88 — the incarnation CHANGES across a remount of the same host, which is what makes it an incarnation rather than a node id. (d) sess91 — the decisive step, because (a)-(c) only prove the identifier is nonzero, not that the COMPARISONS became live.  tests/incarnation_mismatch_probe.sh reaches the refusal arms through the monitor's epoch-change path (disklock.c:1147) by rewriting only the 8-byte epoch field of a dead node's sector, with the feature CRC recomputed so the record stays valid.  ALL THREE arms that sess88 and sess89 recorded as never having executed on the rig fired, and each took the correct branch: arm=zero gave 'P237-RECOV-INC-MISMATCH slot=4 victim=4085327405 victim_inc=1634619062121349274 slot_inc=0 ... refusing to publish' plus P234-COMPLETE-FENCEFAIL rc=-116 and NO descriptor published (mechanism items 5 and 7 — zero is not a wildcard); arm=nonzero gave 'P237-RECOV-SUPERSEDED slot=29 victim_inc=383883444245855066 slot_inc=15952125467273129900 — retiring our pending recovery instead of guarding a LIVE member' plus P237-COMPLETE-SUPERSEDED, with no guard laid; and the follow-on round exercised P237-RECOV-INC-UNOBSERVED through to P163-RECOVERY-COMPLETE + P97-SWEEP-DONE.  The owner-incarnation predicates (mechanism items 3 and 4) are exercised POSITIVELY by every one of those completions: recov_auth_holds and recov_fence_auth_holds both require inc_eq(d->owner_epoch, ctx->epoch) and inc_eq(d->fence_prover_epoch, ctx->epoch) to hold on real nonzero values before a descriptor may be certified or advanced. (e) Regression gate: full 32/caw board GREEN on 0.11.420 (sess90) and again on 0.11.421 (sess91) — 27 of 27 functional criteria PASS, open_defects red by policy only. NOT CLAIMED, and carried forward as an explicit item on D-RECOV-AUTH-ZERO-VICTIM-EPOCH-WEDGE's successor entries: the NEGATIVE arm of the owner/prover-incarnation tests (a same-node LATER incarnation attempting to advance or certify a predecessor's descriptor — the 'A -> B -> A within a single session' case in disklock.h:261) was not injected.  Every arm that was injected refused or branched correctly, and no arm published against an incarnation the slot did not carry.

defects.summary: mkdir(2) returns success while the directory entry exists on no node
defects.evidence: TWO independent byte-exact captures, ccloop c7ee71c6 sess22: sfstorm_20260729_003736 r32 ino=44040321 test31 node31_1; sfstorm_20260729_005540 r39 ino=56623307 test27 node27_1. Both nlink=33 visible=31 expected=32 identical on ALL 32 nodes, zero nonzero mkdir(2) rc cluster-wide.
defects.mechanism: P65-EPOCH-CONVGATE requests reload+adopt (peer converted the dir). P34J-RELOAD-DEMOTE-BAIL abandons that reload whenever a release drain is concurrently active -- its own comment promises 'the caller retries once the demote completes', which NO caller implemented. i_dlm_dir_valid_epoch therefore stays behind the master dir_epoch, and P32E-DIREPOCH-FENCE then skips EVERY flush of whatever the operation goes on to commit (observed firing 3x for one inode: from mkdir, xfsaild and a kworker). The drain exits flushed=1 with pending!=durable (P196 cls=UNCOPIED: never copied into any outgoing image), hands off the grant (P188), and the next adopt discards the change (P177).
defects.detector: P32E-DIREPOCH-FENCE count tracks durable losses almost 1:1 (p32e=6/7/9 -> 3/4/4 losses). P195 is the state-reached precursor; dirent_durability the intermittent symptom.
defects.blocking_fix: Adopt at EX ACQUIRE, before the tenure is exposed to the operation, so P195 never fires at all. The sess22 fix (reload_demote_wait_ms) makes the adopt HAPPEN rather than never, but it still happens after the op gate has noticed -- P195 still fires 5-7x per POST run, i.e. a tenure still mutates an epoch-stale base and then recovers.
attempted_and_refuted: P193 epoch-override at the conversion gate — A/B measured A=0 B=0 failing rounds, no effect; the review showed it is at the wrong layer
dir_lookup_freshness_gate — measured to NEVER engage: dirty_here=1 in 100% of genuine forward-stale hits, so the tenure has always already mutated by the lookup
create_baseline_trackers — A/B was counter-directional (P195: 0 with fix off, 1 with fix on, n=1 per arm); principled and retained, but NOT validated

P197-P6-PREMISE (sess22) REFUTED the tenure-identity hypothesis: i_mxfs_ex_grant_seq IS correctly re-stamped. premise=ok in 60/60 and in both loss captures (dirty_age_ms=6, tenure_age_ms=6). Do not re-chase 'the tenure stamp was carried over'.

tests/creator_stale_base.sh (sess22): a designated-creator + quiet-window harness. Constructs the epoch-stale precondition en masse (3000+ P65 per run) but the adopt always succeeds and it NEVER loses an entry. The loss needs the CONCURRENT release drain that only the full 32-way race produces. Reproducing needs sf_mkdir_storm.sh at 60 rounds -- 30 is not enough on current builds; both captures were round >30.

progress_sess22.fix: v0.11.174 mxfs.reload_demote_wait_ms=50 -- mxfs_dlm_reload_inode now WAITS (bounded, 1ms steps) for an active release drain instead of abandoning the reload, implementing the contract P34J's comment already stated. Bounded so a drain blocked on a lock we hold costs only the bound, never a deadlock.

P195 (mutation on an epoch-stale base) still fires 5-7x per POST run, so the invariant is still violated and the state is still reachable; recovery-after-the-fact is not the same as prevention.

defects.NEW_SYMPTOM_SHAPE_sess25: A dirent_durability FAIL observed this session has a DIFFERENT shape from the captured single-name loss and should not be assumed to be the same defect. test22 reported r21 and r22 each missing 28 of 32 peers (everyone except node1/node2/node16/node22), for a CONTIGUOUS TAIL of rounds (8 of the 10 judged rounds, 21-28), while the other 31 nodes all reported durable_loss=0. 28 simultaneous losses agreed by nobody else is not 28 lost mkdirs -- it is ONE node's directory view going stale at a point in time and never converging. Contrast the captured D-SILENT-MKDIR-LOSS shape: nlink=33 visible=31 expected=32, i.e. exactly ONE name, agreed by ALL nodes. Also: on the reporting node P32E-DIREPOCH-FENCE, P195, P188 and P34J all read ZERO, so none of this defect's own detectors fired. Treat as a candidate SEPARATE read-side staleness defect until evidence ties them together.
defects.progress_sess26: MECHANISM FOUND AND FIXED; defect stays OPEN because the causal link to the observed losses is correlational, not a byte-exact chain. Method: every documented chain marker (P32E/P195/P188/P177/P146V/P51/P65/P194) read ZERO in a losing window (all 11 probes first confirmed present via strings mxfs.ko), so the producer had no probe. tests/dd_loss_differential.sh differenced per-token probe frequencies between the losing node and its 31 peers in one scoped window and nominated P6-MIDTENURE-RELOAD-SKIP: loser 661 vs peer median 37 (range 25-215), 3x above the highest peer, nothing else comparable. MECHANISM: that branch clears i_dlm_stale and returns WITHOUT reloading, premise 'dirtied under the current EX tenure so the platter has nothing to teach us'. P197 shows the premise is literally true; the INFERENCE is false when a peer published since. New P81-P6-SRC histogram shows the swallowed staleness comes from srcs 2/5/7/8, ALL peer-driven (2 = consuming a peer's DIR_MODIFY; 5 = set at release, a peer may have held EX throughout; 7 = the else-branch of dir_slow_skip, i.e. a peer handoff DID occur; 8 = MXFS_IF_DIR_RELOAD consumed on the EX-acquire fast path). At src=8 the flag is CLEARED before the reload is attempted, so skipping destroys the notification on both channels and the peer's entry is never observed. New per-inode i_dlm_p6skip_n shows this repeats: repeat_max 20-29 consecutive skips with no real reload. mxfs.p6_epoch_override could never help -- it honours only src==3, and losing windows show epoch == entry_epoch throughout. FIX: mxfs.p6_honor_src_mask (default 0x1A4 = srcs 2,5,7,8) in pal/linux/xfs_aops.c; the skip does not apply to staleness from those sources. 0 = pre-fix, same-build A/B. RULE 0 CONSTRAINT: the obvious fix (p6_midtenure_skip=0, always reload) takes dirent_durability from 120s to a 240s/240s TIMEOUT and is forbidden; the mask reloads only on peer notifications and costs nothing. PAIRED MEASUREMENT, one build (0.11.228, 8E827AAB556A0E21AF739C9), knob flipped at runtime -- swallowed notifications (hist 2+5+7+8) test1/test5/test19: 173/43/42 at mask=0 vs 0/0/0 at 0x1A4; repeat_ge8 86/36/44 -> 0/0/0; repeat_max 29/20/24 -> 0/0/0. dirent_durability PASS 124s, cache_coherency 654/654 26s, dir_reuse_coherency 65/65 102s. WHY STILL OPEN: observed loss rate is ~2 in 12 runs, so the 4 post-fix passes and 3 pre-fix passes accumulated so far cannot distinguish the arms on the LOSS itself. The swallowed-notification count is a far more sensitive proxy (~42/node/run -> 0) and it is eliminated, but RULE 6 defines this defect by the loss. Next: alternate p6_honor_src_mask 0x1A4/0 across many paired runs and compare durable_loss rates; also consider whether src=1 (readdir refresh, the largest bucket, no repeat streaks) needs honouring (mask 0x1A6).
defects.loss_rate_tally_sess26: RUN TALLY, one build (v0.11.223-0.11.228, p6_honor_src_mask flipped at runtime). Counting only GENUINE single-node durable losses (normal ~120s wall, late_ok>0, states:FAIL=1) and excluding rank1 240s truncations, which are a separate pace failure (see D-MOUNT-DEGRADES-WITH-USE) and occurred in BOTH arms: PRE-FIX (mask=0 or pre-fix builds): 2 genuine losses in ~12 runs -- test19 durable_loss=8 late_ok=4 at 119s, and test4 durable_loss=8 late_ok=14 at 120s. POST-FIX (mask=0x1A4): 0 genuine losses in ~16 runs. If the pre-fix rate (~0.17) were unchanged, 0 in 16 has probability ~0.05, so this is suggestive but at the edge of significance -- NOT a disposition on its own. The strong evidence remains the mechanism metric: swallowed peer notifications ~42/node/run -> 0, and consecutive-skip streaks (i_dlm_p6skip_n) max 29 -> 0. The rank1 240s truncations (3 observed: durable_loss 8/8/5, late_ok 0/10/14) are NOT this defect -- P6-MIDTENURE-RELOAD-SKIP is absent from their differentials and they occur pre- and post-fix alike.
defects.sess27_create_baseline_is_DEAD_CODE: PROVEN: mxfs.create_baseline_trackers (sess21) has NEVER EXECUTED ONCE. The block lives in mxfs_dlm_grant_local_new (xfs_mxfs_dlm.c ~27477) and is gated on S_ISDIR(VFS_I(ip)->i_mode), but its only caller is xfs_iget_cache_miss under XFS_IGET_CREATE (xfs_icache.c:1885) where the inode was just allocated and i_mode is still 0 -- the mode is set later by xfs_init_new_inode, and even the generation is only assigned at xfs_icache.c:1902. New probe P209-CREATE-BASELINE, placed INSIDE the block, read ZERO on every node across a full 32-node dirent_durability run. This explains the ledger note that sess21's paired A/B was 'counter-directional and never validated': the knob is a no-op, so both arms were the same code. DO NOT treat create_baseline_trackers as a live lever. SECOND, INDEPENDENT DEFECT in the same block: even if reached, it does `if (bgg) ... if (bep) ...` on values read from the DLM for a brand-new inode created WITHOUT a real acquire (deferred publish), so the DLM has no grant record and both read 0 -- the guards would skip and the sentinels would survive anyway. Fixing the S_ISDIR gate alone is therefore NOT sufficient; the stamp has to happen where the grant actually becomes real (the deferred publish), or the 'never set' sentinel 0 has to be replaced by a distinct 'self-created, coherent as of creation' value so the detectors gated on cached_grant_gen != 0 stop being inert for self-created directories.

THE IN-TREE PRECEDENT FOR THE FIX: dlm/dlm_caw.c ~1271 documents exactly this problem and its solution -- ctx->orphan_clock is 'a dedicated table with its own mxfs_pal_spinlock_t (never sleeps), because callers ... run with the caller's own xfs_inode spinlock held. defects.sess28_ROOT_PROVEN_cross_incarnation_epo: ROOT PROVEN BY TRACE AND FIXED (RULE 4 step 2b), build 0.11.242 C6D909C4133BA6731C55251. THE DEFECT: the CAW dir_epoch is a property of the inode NUMBER, not of an incarnation. caw_tombstone_slot() and caw_claim_inherit_epoch() (dlm/dlm_caw.c ~897/920) deliberately carry dir_epoch across an idle gap, and mxfs_v5_dlm_inode_dir_epoch() serves it out of a per-resource grant_meta cache that survives the inode being freed and re-created. So every consumer's `master_epoch > i_dlm_dir_valid_epoch` test compares a DEAD incarnation's handoff lineage against a LIVE incarnation's baseline -- the same invalid cross-incarnation comparison class sess27 proved for di_gen in RELOAD-TYPEFLIP-STALE-SKIP. TRACE (2/caw test2, one inode's full scoped window, ino 2099630): line 119 'P9-NLEDGE reset4create' = incarnation A created; line 126 'P210-CREATOR-BASELINE site=2 bep=0' = A published at epoch 0; A then handed off (P70-BP EXIT=full / P-DIRBAST) driving the SLOT epoch to 2; line 1363 'EVICT-RING-FLAG incore_gen=2916713347 freed_gen=2916713348' = A FREED; line 1383 'reset4create' = incarnation B created on the same number; line 1410 'P195-STALE-BASE-ALREADY-DIRTY grant_epoch=2 valid_epoch=0 self_created=1 baseline_unset=1 comm=mkdir'. defects.mechanism: No closed submission gate + drain-to-zero before handoff. Includes: a partial inode-cluster write whose buffer completion marks EVERY attached inode durable, including ones whose sectors were dropped; and no per-tenure in-flight write accounting, so a write submitted while ownership was valid can land after a later tenure's.
defects.detector: P188-REL-OBLIGATION-AT-UNLOCK plus P196-UNLOCK-OBLIGATION-CLASS (sess22), which names WHICH of four causes each occurrence is: NODRAIN / REDIRTY / INFLIGHT / UNCOPIED.
defects.blocking_fix: Close the tenure to new submissions, commit, publish, wait for every write attributed to the tenure, account completion only for bytes actually issued, verify pending==durable, THEN bump the published epoch and release. Infrastructure already half-exists: b_tenure_id (per-buffer tenure attribution) and i_mxfs_ex_grant_seq (live per-tenure counter for dirs, measured egseq!=0 in 7122/7122 P68-EVDECIDE).
attempted_and_refuted: pub_skip_rearm (re-arm the skipped inode as still-dirty) — MEASURED LIVELOCK: the skip happens precisely because publication authority is absent, so the retry can never succeed. The retry must happen BEFORE release, while the grant is still held.

progress_sess22.classified: Every P196 observed reads cls=UNCOPIED with drain_ran=1 drain_flushed=1 (e.g. dr_pend=17 dr_dur=12 dr_flush=12). progress_sess22.consequence_for_the_fix: Enforcing at the drain (mxfs.pub_obligation_enforce) CANNOT close this: the retry re-runs a flush that is fenced further down by P32E. gpt_detector_design_sess29.priority: GPT ranks this the highest-leverage remaining defect: it can invalidate the authority premise of the sess29 cluster fix, explain dirent_publish_integrity's unlanded_at_unlock=1, plausibly cause the silent mkdir loss, and contaminate several coherency/pace observations.
gpt_detector_design_sess29.do_not_infer_home_visibility_from: transaction commit; log force completion; AIL insertion; I/O submission; buffer dirty state transiently clearing. A log force makes a change durable in the JOURNAL, not visible at its HOME block, and peers do not replay another mounted node's log.
gpt_detector_design_sess29.cheapest_strong_primitive: an exact home-I/O COMPLETION CERTIFICATE attached to the change when it is made -- i.e. hook the real buffer/log-item iodone, not any earlier stage.
gpt_detector_design_sess29.scope_warning: the association must cover ALL peer-visible blocks, not just the inode core. For mkdir that includes parent dir DATA, parent inode, child inode, and the dir/free-space metadata lookup depends on. An inode-level release certificate is insufficient when the visible state lives in a directory data block.
gpt_detector_design_sess29.use_dlm_epochs_not_wall_clock: the sess29 cross-node merge technique is reusable but should key on causal identifiers -- DLM resource, authority epoch/grant sequence, local dirty generation, release sequence, home submission+completion sequence, next grant sequence -- rather than CLOCK_REALTIME.
gpt_detector_design_sess29.optional_strong_validation: sampled peer-side home read: before release, digest the authoritative home image and publish identity/generation/digest (an LVB is a natural carrier); on the next grant, invalidate the receiver's cached copy and read home directly, comparing incarnation/generation/CRC/digest. Diagnostic arm only. A buffered read may just return another stale cache image -- it must be a real post-invalidation read.
gpt_detector_design_sess29.the_barrier_itself: 1 stop new modifications under the current authority epoch; 2 identify every home obligation from that epoch; 3 journal ordering/durability; 4 push those exact items to home; 5 WAIT for real successful home-I/O completion; 6 publish the completed release generation; 7 end authority / permit the peer grant. A plain log force is only step 3. Keep the DLM grant blocked until completion -- do not release first and finish asynchronously. If lock ordering forbids waiting inside mxfs_dlm_ilock_end, use a prepare-release phase or workqueue state machine.

sess30_obligation_detector_at_unlock.what_the_ledger_asked_for: The standing complaint on this defect is that the pending-vs-durable predicate is evaluated on ONE early-exit branch (P176) and NEVER at the wire unlock. BUILT sess30.
sess30_obligation_detector_at_unlock.predicate: XFS's own per-inode flush flag. XFS_IFLUSHING (1<<7 in ip->i_flags) is set by xfs_iflush when it copies the in-core image into a cluster buffer and cleared only by that buffer's iodone. So `IFLUSHING at unlock` means verbatim: we are handing the tenure away while bytes produced under it are staged in a buffer that has not reached home.
sess30_obligation_detector_at_unlock.sites: mxfs_dlm_relbar_check() at BOTH bast_process release tails (arm=noanchor, arm=anchored), immediately before the wire unlock; PLUS mxfs_relbar_epoch_check() at ALL NINE i_dlm_epoch bump sites (every site that ENDS a tenure: bast_process x3, bast_notify, ilock_begin x2, evict x2, peer_joined_flush). Read with `echo 1 > /sys/module/mxfs/parameters/release_barrier_dump` -> P220-RELEASE-BARRIER-TOTAL unlocks/flushing/in_ail/pinned/epoch_ends/epoch_flushing. Probes P220-UNLOCK-OBLIGATION-OPEN and P220-EPOCH-OBLIGATION-OPEN (the latter carries epsrc = __LINE__ of the bump site, so the leaking path is NAMED).
sess30_obligation_detector_at_unlock.lockless_by_design: mxfs_relbar_epoch_check reads ip->i_flags directly rather than via xfs_iflags_test(), because several bump sites hold ip->i_dlm_lock and xfs_iflags_test takes ip->i_flags_lock -- nesting a second inode spinlock inside the DLM lock for a diagnostic is not worth the lock-order risk.
sess30_obligation_detector_at_unlock.first_readings: unlocks=9975/5224/9740 flushing=0 in_ail=0 pinned=0; epoch_ends=11204 epoch_flushing=0. SOLID NEGATIVE for the two bast_process tails: the existing release drain leaves nothing staged there.
sess30_obligation_detector_at_unlock.IMPORTANT_do_not_over_read: Those readings came from runs in which P219 stale_tenure was ALSO 0 -- i.e. the runs never exercised the condition (host contention truncated them). The hypothesis 'the tenure ends while a staged image is outstanding' is therefore UNTESTED, not refuted. It needs ONE clean run with a full workload and both detectors armed.

gpt_barrier_design_sess30.invariant: No write containing bytes produced under grant tenure A may remain queued or in flight when tenure A is handed to another node. Stronger than 'check authority at copy-in' and stronger than 'wait for the flush lock'.
gpt_barrier_design_sess30.iflock_is_only_a_proxy: It can be cleared by abort/error/shutdown without successful home publication; checking it ONCE is racy (clear -> local op stages -> unlock); it says nothing about dirty state that has not reached xfs_iflush yet. Prefer an explicit per-tenure outstanding-publication COUNT.
gpt_barrier_design_sess30.sequence: 1 BAST marks REVOKING and CLOSES ADMISSION (do not block in the AST); 2 drain active users; 3 force log to unpin; 4 flush dirty-but-not-staged while EX is still retained; 5 arrange submission of already-staged buffers; 6 WAIT for successful completion holding NO ILOCK / flush lock / buffer lock / AIL lock / transaction or AG lock / DLM internal lock; 7 recheck a generation counter for work that appeared during the drain; 8 only then downgrade/unlock.
gpt_barrier_design_sess30.admission_race: 'Wait if iflock held, else release' is NOT sufficient -- admission must be closed BEFORE examining state, or: worker sees iflock clear -> local op stages and takes iflock -> worker unlocks -> staged write lands later.
gpt_barrier_design_sess30.delwri_hazard: Do NOT steal or independently submit a buffer from a delwri list xfsaild currently owns: the buffer lock does not confer ownership of b_list. Correct shape is an ownership-aware rendezvous -- release worker sets an urgent-submit bit, the current list owner submits normally, iodone wakes the waiter.
gpt_barrier_design_sess30.clustering_warning: Avoid broad xfs_iflush_cluster from the release path: it stages neighbouring slots whose DLM authority and release state differ. In MXFS clustering is no longer merely a performance choice, it creates cross-authority coupling.
gpt_barrier_design_sess30.failure_policy: If the home write FAILS, 'unlock anyway' recreates the corruption window. Either retain the grant and retry, or fence. A timed-out write is especially dangerous: timed out does not mean it cannot complete later.
gpt_barrier_design_sess30.submit_time_check_role: Keep the submit-time epoch check as a PERMANENT INVARIANT ASSERTION / fail-stop, not as the recovery mechanism. Correct re-arming at submit time is far more invasive (undo flush state for every attached item, keep each in the AIL, restore watermarks, prevent buffer-wide iodone retiring them, distinguish retryable state from a peer-freed inode) and 'retry after reacquiring EX' is not universally valid -- reacquiring EX does not make an obsolete incarnation current again.
gpt_barrier_design_sess30.scope_warning: An inode-only barrier will NOT cover the authority domain. The same copy-in/submit-across-release window exists for directory and attribute blocks, bmap btree blocks, remote attr blocks, and (on the AG/global resources) AGI/AGF/AGFL, inode and free-space btrees, rmap/refcount, quota. Suggested general detector: per-buffer provenance (owning lock domain + resource tenure/epoch at last authoritative modification), and for inode clusters it must stay PER SLOT because one physical buffer spans multiple authority domains.

defects.summary: A workload that meets its budget on a fresh prep cannot finish after the same mount has been used
defects.evidence: 32/caw@0.11.163 rsync_paired: PASS 14s fresh vs 0/32 hung at 60s after prior work. 32/caw@0.11.163 crash_consistency: 32/32 fresh vs 31/32. 32/caw@0.11.167 crash_consistency: PASS 57s fresh vs 0/32 hung at 90s. The IDENTICAL 13-test sequence on a fresh prep passes every time, so it is accumulated mount state, not test ordering.
defects.mechanism: TWO components rooted. (1) sess28: xfs_dir2_readdir.c retried a reload 200x with msleep(1) while the caller held ILOCK_SHARED, so every round bailed -- 1210ms -> 5ms per getdents (242x). (2) sess29 ROOT PROVEN + FIXED: the demoter claim taken by mxfs_inode_dlm_defer_bast is deliberately RETAINED by mxfs_trans_drain_inode_unlocks' P152 punt (the only exit in the tree that skips its clear) so the committing task stays exempt across its post-commit xfs_iunlock -- and NOTHING ever ended that retention. The dwork that inherits the release lands in slot 2 and clears slot 2 only. mxfs_foreign_demoter() then stays true for the life of the in-core inode, so EVERY reload pays mxfs.reload_demote_wait_ms and abandons with i_dlm_stale set (224-354 bails on ONE inode vs 1 on healthy nodes). Second propagation step: the inode is freed still claimed, alloc_inode_sb does not zero the slab object, and the initializer's MXFS_CLEAR_DEMOTER refuses a non-owner clear -- so the NEXT inode on that memory is born stranded carrying a dead task's stamps. Decisive counter: P215-DEFER set=2 clear=0 retain=2 on four nodes, i.e. every deferral punted and the inline clear never ran.
defects.detector: Per-phase timers in tests/suite/sustained_load.sh (setup/rmrf/mkb/syn/bar1/mkd/bar2): compare rmrf on a fresh prep against the same mount after a full board. The aggregate per_op hides it -- sess28 measured ~97% of the criterion's wall outside the only thing it was timing. For the demoter component use tests/demoter_strand_census.sh.
defects.blocking_fix: unknown — suspects: DLM lock-table growth, AG grant-cache churn, inode cache/AIL growth, CAW slot-table pressure, per-AG counters that never reset

defects.REPRODUCED_sess25:
REPRODUCED ON THE CURRENT BUILD with a clean paired measurement, and the trigger is now NARROWED. Same build 0.11.210, same 32-node cluster, same criteria:
  fresh prep            : cache_coherency PASS 35s/60s   dlm_fairness PASS 26s/30s
  2nd run, same prep    : cache_coherency PASS 31s/60s
  after ONE dirent_durability storm on that mount:

                          dlm_fairness    FAIL 30s/30s NO_TERMINAL_RECORD=32
                          zero_silent_loss PASS but 50s vs 28s fresh
So it is NOT cumulative age and NOT 'any prior work' -- a second run on the same mount is still fast. It is a HEAVY STORM specifically. That also explains why sustained_load was refuted as the detector in sess22 (14 consecutive runs, no progressive decline): sustained_load is not a storm. IMPORTANT for future sessions: this confounds any regression test run on an aged mount. Two criteria were briefly suspected of being a regression from this session's demoter change and were exonerated by re-running on a fresh prep; P73-WAITSTALL was 0 throughout, so the slowdown is NOT demote-wait stalls.
defects.NARROWING_sess25:
tests/mount_degrade_probe.sh (new) times three primitives per node with NO barrier, so the per-node DISTRIBUTION is visible -- which the criteria cannot show, because one straggler holding a barrier reports as NO_TERMINAL_RECORD on ALL ranks and is indistinguishable from every node being slow. Paired FRESH vs POST_STORM, 32 nodes, same build 0.11.210:
  metric            FRESH(min/med/max)         POST_STORM(min/med/max)
  statfs            58.9 / 70.9 / 84.4 ms      58.4 / 73.1 / 96.4 ms
  shared-dir mkdir  18876 / 28208 / 29866 ms   481 / 26983 / 28901 ms
  private mkdir     846 / 2634 / 3957 ms       411 / 642 / 31752 ms
  private max/min   4.7x                       77.3x
THREE SOLID CONCLUSIONS:
  1. statfs is UNCHANGED (71 vs 73 ms median, 1.4-1.7x spread in both). The filesystem service      path does not degrade at all.
  2. Shared-directory mkdir costs the SAME fresh and post-storm (28208 vs 26983 ms median for 20      mkdir+rmdir = ~1.4 s/op). So the storm does NOT degrade shared-dir throughput; that ~1.4 s/op      is D-32NODE-SHARED-DIR-CREATE-PACE and is storm-INDEPENDENT.
  3. The post-storm signature is a SINGLE-NODE OUTLIER, not a uniform shift: private max/min goes      4.7x -> 77.3x, driven by one node (test25) at 31752 ms against a 642 ms median. That node was      NOT wedged -- load 0.45, no D-state, no P73-WAITSTALL -- but showed P34-ACQ-SLOW ino=137      isdir=1 req_mode=5 dur_ms=1056..2396, i.e. multi-second EX acquires on the shared directory.
REFRAME: 'the mount degrades' is probably the wrong model. The evidence says ONE NODE BECOMES A PERSISTENT STRAGGLER after a storm (slow, not stuck), and because every barrier criterion needs all N ranks, that one node fails the whole board. Same blast-radius shape as the two wedges fixed this session, but a slowdown rather than a deadlock.
PROBE LIMITATION, stated so the numbers are not over-read: the three phases are NOT synchronised across nodes, so a node lagging in its private phase overlaps its peers' shared phase. That makes the private MEDIANS non-comparable between runs (FRESH's 2634 ms median is higher than POST_STORM's 642 ms purely because all 32 nodes ran private simultaneously on the fresh run). The SPREAD and the statfs/shared columns are sound; the private median is not. Next session: add a coord barrier between phases, then re-run the pair.

defects.localised_sess26: CORRECTION OF AN EARLIER SESS26 CLAIM. Two independent 240s/240s dirent_durability truncations on an aged mount, BOTH on test1 (= rank 1), never any other node -- that part holds. The token differential vs the 31 peers showed test1 elevated on P1-AGWAIT (x25-28), P128-INACT-DEFER (x154-177), P-DIRFLUSH (x18-24) and doing none of the peers' eviction work, and I initially recorded those probes as naming the backlog. THEY DO NOT. Measured afterwards on a FRESH-PREP PASSING run (117s, 32/32, durable_loss=0) with tests/rank1_straggler_probe.sh: rank1 is ALREADY above every peer on exactly those probes, at the same magnitudes -- P128-INACT-DEFER 157 (peer max 2) vs 153-176 when failing; P-DIRFLUSH 800 (peer max 56) vs 615-773 when failing; P1-AGWAIT 92 (peer max 6) vs 110-200; P-BLOCK0-CONVGATE 62 (peers 0); P-IGET-ENOENT 40 (peers 0); EVICT-RING-FLAG 0 vs median 23. So the elevation is the COORDINATOR ROLE, present on healthy passing runs, and it does not discriminate failing from passing. METHOD LESSON: a loser-vs-peers differential is only valid when the losing node is an ordinary peer. If the loser is rank 1, the role asymmetry alone yields x20-x158 departures and swamps any real signal -- compare rank1-failing against rank1-PASSING instead. (The P6-MIDTENURE finding for D-SILENT-MKDIR-LOSS is unaffected: that loser was test4, an ordinary peer, and P6 sits at x1.6 on rank1 so the role does not explain it.) WHAT REMAINS ESTABLISHED: the 240s truncations happen only on an aged mount and only on rank1; a fresh prep on the same build/mask passes at 116-124s (11 runs). The CAUSE is not yet named. SECOND METHOD CORRECTION: 'diff rank1-failing against rank1-passing' is ALSO invalid as naively executed. Probe pr_warn counters are static atomic_t = PER MODULE LOAD and capped, so they never reset between runs on one mount. Diffing a late (failing) run against a fresh-prep (passing) run measures CAP EXHAUSTION: measured top rows were P170-CLWR 800->0 (its documented cap is exactly 800, see pal/linux/xfs_buf.c ~3747), P25-INSTR 600->0, P141-UNLK-EXCLR 500->0, P82-ADD/P19-B3DEC/P140-RECLAIM-COMMIT 300->0 -- round numbers to zero, entirely artifact. VALID DESIGN: match the ORDINAL run position after a fresh prep. The mount fails at iteration k; prep again, run k iterations (expected to pass at k), and diff the two iteration-k censuses -- same node, same role, same module age. Or get the failure to occur on the FIRST run after a prep, making any fresh-prep run a like-for-like control. REPRODUCTION RATE for that design: fresh prep then 1-2 passes at 116-124s, then a 240s rank1 truncation; observed 3 times (durable_loss=8, 8, 5; late_ok 10, 14, and one 0). See ccmemory probe-counts-are-per-module-load-and-capped.
defects.sess28_QUANTIFIED_DOSE_RESPONSE: sustained_load IS a detector at 32 nodes on the current build, contradicting sess22's refutation (which was 14 consecutive runs on ONE aged mount -- that measures run-to-run noise at a fixed dose, not a dose-response). Build 0.11.243 C3D864E1F8AB80753D23D6C, 32/caw, identical knobs, MONOTONE in mount age: (a) FRESH PREP -> sustained_load PASS 32/32, wall 4s/180s, per_op=106ms. (b) after the 5-test aging batch (crash_consistency dir_reuse_coherency fence_during_write fault_netpartition soak) -> PASS 32/32 but wall 44s/180s, per_op=179ms -- an 11x WALL increase for a 1.7x per-op increase. (c) after the FULL 32-node board -> FAIL 180s/180s TIMEOUT, NO_TERMINAL_RECORD=2 then =4 of 32 on consecutive runs, per_op=198ms. THE DECISIVE RATIO: 20 ops at ~198ms is ~4s of actual operations against a 180s wall, so ~97% of the aged wall is spent OUTSIDE the op loop. The degradation is NOT in per-op service time (which moves only 1.7x) -- it is in the criterion's per-node entry/setup path or in whatever the ranks wait on before it. That is a much narrower target than 'the mount is slower', and it is consistent with sess25's finding that statfs is UNCHANGED (71 vs 73 ms) while a single node becomes a 77x outlier. NOT CAUSED BY THE sess28 FIX: with mxfs.dir_epoch_incarn_gate flipped to 0 on the SAME aged mount and the same build, sustained_load failed WORSE (0/32 NO_TERMINAL_RECORD vs 28/32), so the fix reduces the degradation if anything. CHEAP REPRODUCER (~10 min at 32 nodes, no storm needed): prep 32 caw; run.sh 32 caw sustained_load (expect ~4s); run the full board; run.sh 32 caw sustained_load (expect a 180s timeout).

A SECOND COMPONENT REMAINS: the criterion still fails 180s/180s with bar2=121028ms NO_TERMINAL_RECORD=3, i.e. 3 of 32 nodes cannot finish a 20-op loop that the other 29 finish in ~2.5 s. defects.sess28_SECOND_COMPONENT_ROOT_PROVEN_leak: ROOT PROVEN (RULE 4 step 2b) for the component that remained after the readdir fix. THE DEMOTER CLAIM OUTLIVES ITS HOLDER. CAPTURE METHOD (the part that made it findable): a node that blows the budget produces NO terminal record, so the aggregate line describes only the healthy majority -- which is how this criterion reported per_op=198ms while nodes were stuck. tests/suite/sustained_load.sh now emits per-op progress to /dev/kmsg AS IT HAPPENS (MXFS_SL SLOW/HB/BEGIN/CREATED/READDIR/REMOVED/SYNCED), and tests/sl_straggler_capture.sh sweeps every node for non-heartbeat D-state stacks DURING the run (post-mortem is useless: run.sh kills the test at its budget and the state is gone; the only D-state left afterwards is the normal bounded disklock heartbeat, which must never be convicted). TRAIL: 30 of 32 nodes reach 'SYNCED elapsed=1638..4760'; test21 and test22 stop at 'SLOW phase=rmdir k=8 ms=801/803' and emit nothing further. Reproduced 3 times, SAME two nodes, SAME op index. LIVE STACKS, 5 samples over ~60 s: always msleep inside mxfs_dlm_reload_inode+0x127, but from DIFFERENT PIDs (210880, 210999, 211113) and DIFFERENT syscalls (83 mkdir, 217 getdents64, 257 openat, 262 newfstatat) and different callers (mxfs_dlm_dir_consumer_refresh->xfs_lookup, mxfs_dlm_ilock_begin->xfs_ilock_data_map_shared->xfs_dir_lookup, mxfs_dlm_dir_modify_reload_prelock->xfs_create->xfs_vn_mkdir). So it is NOT one stuck syscall and NOT a deadlock -- EVERY syscall on that node pays the wait. THE WAIT is the sess22 demote-wait at xfs_mxfs_dlm.c:19160: `while (mxfs_reload_demote_wait_ms && waited < ... && mxfs_foreign_demoter(ip)) msleep(1);` -- bounded at 50 ms, then P34J-RELOAD-DEMOTE-BAIL and the reload is abandoned with i_dlm_stale still set, so the next syscall repeats it. THE PROOF: test21 = 300 P34J bails, ALL on ONE inode (8926798) with ONE demoter_pid (208840). test22 = 290 bails, ALL on ONE inode (46675531) with ONE demoter_pid (17409). Healthy nodes test5/test13 = ZERO bails and 49 SUCCESSFUL P198 waits. AND BOTH DEMOTER PIDs NO LONGER EXIST -- /proc/<pid> is gone on both nodes while the claim is still set and still being observed. The claim LEAKED: some exit path in the release/BAST drain returned without MXFS_CLEAR_DEMOTER. mxfs_foreign_demoter() is then true for the life of the in-core inode, which is exactly the 'a mount that must be remounted to stay in budget' symptom this defect is named for. NOTE A LATENT HAZARD FOUND EN ROUTE: ip->i_dlm_demoter is a bare struct task_struct* held WITHOUT a reference, so once the holder exits it is a dangling pointer. mxfs_foreign_demoter() only compares it (safe), but MXFS_SET_DEMOTER's legacy-clobber A/B path dereferences it ((ip)->i_dlm_demoter->pid) -- a use-after-free, reachable only under mxfs.demoter_legacy_clobber=1. NEXT: P34J now prints demoter_comm / demoter_line / demoter_age_ms (build 0.11.246, 303E25202F73654C4F056E2). i_dlm_demoter_line is already stamped at every claim, so ONE reproduction names the exit path that failed to clear it. Then fix that path; a dead-holder reclaim is a safety net, not the root fix.
defects.sess28_LEAKING_SITE_NAMED: THE LEAKING CLAIM SITE IS NAMED, first reproduction on build 0.11.246 (303E25202F73654C4F056E2). P34J now prints demoter_comm/demoter_line/demoter_age_ms, and the two populations separate cleanly across 32 nodes: HEALTHY/TRANSIENT (test8, test20, test25, test30): exactly 1 bail each, demoter_line=16541, demoter_comm=kworker/u1x:x, demoter_age_ms=150-156 -- a live drain on a bast kworker, ~150 ms old, self-clearing. LEAKED (test23, the straggler): 224 bails on ONE inode 48234637, demoter_pid=216131, demoter_comm=mkdir, demoter_line=34955, demoter_age_ms=179907 -- a claim held by a SYSCALL context for the ENTIRE 180 s run. test15 showed 354 bails in the same run. LINE 34955 is MXFS_SET_DEMOTER(ip) in the trans deferred-unlock path (mxfs_trans_defer_inode_unlock, just after `if (!igrab(VFS_I(ip))) { mxfs_pal_free(pending); return false; }`). Its own comment says 'Cleared after bast_process completes in mxfs_trans_drain_inode_unlocks' -- so the claim is set in ONE function and cleared in ANOTHER, with the whole remainder of the transaction in between. That is the widest SET->CLEAR span in the file (34955 -> 35082, 127 lines, and across a function boundary); every other pair is 6-75 lines within one function. If the transaction is aborted/cancelled, or drain_inode_unlocks is not reached for that pending entry, the claim is never cleared and, because it was taken by a syscall thread that then exits, mxfs_foreign_demoter() stays true for the life of the in-core inode. NEXT: audit every path from mxfs_trans_defer_inode_unlock's success return to mxfs_trans_drain_inode_unlocks for exits that skip the drain (trans cancel/abort, error unwinds, shutdown), and make the clear unconditional on that path. A dead-holder reclaim is a SAFETY NET, not the root fix. Note ip->i_dlm_demoter is a bare task_struct* held with NO reference, so it dangles once the holder exits -- any fix must not dereference it (mxfs_foreign_demoter only compares, which is safe; MXFS_SET_DEMOTER's legacy-clobber A/B path derefs it and is a use-after-free under mxfs.demoter_legacy_clobber=1).

defects.ATTRIBUTED_sess25:
THE REFERENCE IS NOW NAMED. sess23's P202-REFEV ring never produced a capture because it is a fixed 10-entry HISTORY window and by unmount has wrapped many times: a leak is an OLD grab with no matching release, which a history window structurally cannot hold. Replaced with P203-GRABLEVELS, a GRAB-BY-REFCOUNT-LEVEL table -- the grab that took i_count to N is recorded in slot N, so with icount=1 slot 1 IS the outstanding reference. Self-correcting: it never has to observe a release, so untracked VFS iput()s cannot desynchronise it.
Captured on the reproducer:
  P203-GRABLEVELS ino=29360571 icount=1 over=0
    P203-LEVEL[1] xfs_lookup+0x16c        <- THE SURVIVOR
    P203-LEVEL[2] mxfs_dlm_bast_notify+0x6f
    P203-LEVEL[3] site=file1:line26265
    P203-LEVEL[4] site=file1:line26690
Levels 2-4 are the DLM machinery's own grabs and were all released; the surviving reference is the ordinary namespace lookup at level 1, on an inode with dentries=0 hashed=1 lru_linked=1.

The pre-existing comment's reasoning ('the dwork holds an iget ref that keeps the inode out of reclaim, so it has already run by the time we reach evict') is CORRECT. A repair knob mxfs.cancel_ref_release exists and ships OFF -- it repairs a case that does not occur.

Design around the gap that xfs_iget grabs and plain VFS iput releases are untracked, so count tracked-vs-untracked explicitly rather than inferring from an imbalance.
defects.sess26_attribution_attempt: RATE: 3 catches in 5 full reproducer cycles at 16/caw on builds 8E827AAB / 90C3AAA8 / C142E323, one node per catch (test10, test6, test1). Consistent signature across all three: DIRECTORY, icount=1, dentries=0, hashed=1, lru_linked=1, sblist_linked=1, dlm_mode=3(PR), dlm_state=1(CACHED), itemp=1, in_ail=0, bast/dwork/bwork all NOT pending, demoter=0, nlink 14-18, stale_src 2 or 8, bastq_src 1/9/14. ATTRIBUTION converges on xfs_lookup+0x16c from TWO independent fields (iget_caller and P203-LEVEL[1]) in the later captures; GRAB=file2:line1741/1742 is the ordinary xfs_iget_cache_hit igrab and names nothing. DISPROVEN INSTRUMENT (do not rebuild): a per-inode grab/release BALANCE, added as P205-REFBAL with fields i_mxfs_tgrabs/i_mxfs_tputs. First cut counted only the tracked igrab/iput wrappers and read tgrabs=61 tputs=1 net=60 against icount=1, because MXFS releases via xfs_irele() not iput(). Made symmetric by also counting the xfs_irele() chokepoint and the xfs_iget() hand-off: still tgrabs=161 tputs=83 net=78 against icount=1. The residue is VFS-side references (dput->iput, evict, d_splice_alias's own error-path iput) which cannot be hooked from the filesystem, and Linux has no reverse map from a refcount to its holders. The approach is unsound in principle. P205 is retained only for its honest 'UNEXPLAINED (VFS igrab/iput outside both chokepoints)' verdict. ALSO: P203-LEVEL is sound only under LIFO release order (if grab A takes 0->1 and B takes 1->2 and A releases first, the survivor is B's while LEVEL[1] still names A), so its attribution is PLAUSIBLE not PROVEN. P203-GRABSTACK does not exist in the module at all (strings mxfs.ko = 0 hits) although tests/unmount_leak_repro.sh grepped for it -- that harness has been corrected to grep P203-LEVEL/P202/P205. KEY CONTRADICTION TO RESOLVE: dentries=0 with icount=1 means no VFS dentry holds it, yet a lookup-obtained reference survives. xfs_lookup itself was verified to release on every internal path, and xfs_vn_lookup hands the ref to d_splice_alias which consumes it on success and error alike. NEXT (targeted, not global): count per inode how many times xfs_lookup returned 0 handing out a reference, and compare against the dentry count at unmount; lookup_handoffs>0 && dentries==0 && icount==1 shows a lookup reference no dentry ever took. Count d_splice_alias outcomes too, since its error path legitimately consumes the ref via iput without creating a dentry.
defects.arm_site_audit_sess26: ARM-SITE AUDIT, partial. The live hypothesis is that a bast arm igrabbed and the work owning that reference neither reached its trailing irele nor is still pending (every capture shows bast/bwork/dwork/timer all not pending, demoter=0). Arm sites are enumerable via i_dlm_bastq_src (21 assignment sites); captures show src 1, 9, 14. AUDITED AND CORRECT: src=1 (~27113, ilock-end) igrab + queue_work with xfs_irele on queue-false. src=9 at 16613 releases via mxfs_dlm_dwork_safe_irele(ip,3) on queue-false, and at 16866 via xfs_irele on queue-false. src=14 at 13867 and 17816 both pair igrab with queue and xfs_irele on queue-false. The shared PR-demote helper (~32320) also pairs correctly. Note mxfs_dlm_dwork_safe_irele REFUSES to release when i_count<1 or I_FREEING/I_CLEAR (printing P124-DWFN-BADREF) -- but P124 measured 0 on the leaking node, so that refusal did not occur. STILL TO AUDIT: the remaining bastq_src sites (2,3,4,5,6,7,10,11,12,13,15,16 at lines 16094, 16784, 17877, 17972, 18081, 18114, 18260, 25929, 26213, 26688, 26759, 27045, 34464) plus the two generic setters at 32327/32407. Also worth checking whether any site sets bastq_src WITHOUT an accompanying igrab, since the captures' bastq_src only records the LAST arm and may not be the leaking one -- the same last-writer weakness as grab_line.
defects.NEW_ANGLE_sess27_GPT: RULE-5 GPT consult. The load-bearing fact is NOT nlink/PR/CACHED but that the inode is ON THE INODE LRU and later has i_count==1. An inode joins the LRU after becoming unused, so the surviving reference belongs to a NEW BUSY TENURE that began AFTER the inode previously reached zero. That collapses the search to the FINAL 0->1 transition after the last LRU insertion, and needs neither a global lifetime balance nor LIFO pairing -- the two instruments already disproven here. Instrument via a TEMPORARY KERNEL PATCH (ihold() is inline, so module-side instrumentation cannot see it): inode_add_lru(), LRU removal/isolation, __iget(), igrab(), ihold(), iput(), and any direct atomic_long_*(&inode->i_count). Record inode addr/ino/gen, old+new i_count, ts, cpu, pid/comm, stack id, per-inode busy-tenure seq; ring buffer + stack depot, not printk. A kprobe/fentry on generic iput() DOES observe the VFS-side releases (dput->iput, d_splice_alias's internal iput) that are unhookable from the filesystem. A raw ihold()/direct increment from zero is the suspicious case; a normal igrab() of a cached zero-ref inode can be legitimate. FIRST: verify the unmount diagnostic itself does not igrab and manufacture the reported count of 1. SECOND TRACK: vmcore/drgn reverse-search of kernel memory for the inode pointer, classifying the containing object -- and given dlm_state=CACHED, inspect the MXFS DLM object and every reverse pointer from it: 'cached lock object keeps an inode pointer but is not considered pending work' is an ownership category distinct from the queue-arm sites already audited.
defects.sess27_final_tenure_instrument_NEGATIVE: BUILT AND MEASURED, RESULT NEGATIVE (build 0.11.236 8A3F18EEAA6BC0B9475F4C1). GPT's LRU premise was VERIFIED against the kernel source: /src/linux/fs/inode.c __inode_lru_list_add() returns early 'if (icount_read(inode))', so LRU membership proves the inode reached zero. xfs_fs_drop_inode() runs from iput_final() at that transition, so mxfs_inode_tenure_reset() (xfs_inode.h, called from pal/linux/xfs_super.c) now bumps i_mxfs_zero_seq and clears i_mxfs_grabst[] there, scoping the grab table to the final tenure. ALSO VERIFIED: the unmount diagnostic does NOT manufacture the count (mxfs_report_leaked_inodes only atomic_read()s i_count, takes no reference), and evict_inodes() (fs/inode.c:919) skips any inode with a nonzero count, so the survivor is a genuine unreleased ref. BUT the narrowing FAILED: reproduced first cycle at 16/caw (test9 ino 8391875) with 'zero_seq=1 tenure_grabs=499 tenure_age_ms=57533'. The inode hit zero exactly ONCE, 57.5s before unmount, then took 499 tracked grabs without returning to zero -- so the 'final tenure' is a huge busy window and the LIFO objection is fully back. tenure_grabs was added precisely so this failure is visible rather than being misread as an answer. Sites named were all REFUTED on inspection: LEVEL[1]/[2] = xfs_lookup+0x170 = xfs_inode.c:1229 (the xfs_iget return; already eliminated in sess26 because d_splice_alias consumes that ref on every path); LEVEL[4] = xfs_mxfs_dlm.c:27181, the ilock-end BAST arm setting bastq_src=1 -- which MATCHED the leaked inode's bastq_src=1 and looked like a hit, but line 27187 does xfs_irele(ip) on the queue_work-false path and pairs correctly. NOTE: 27181 is a DIFFERENT site from the ~27113 one sess26 audited as 'src=1'; there are at least two sites assigning bastq_src=1 (same one-of-two-variants trap sess26 caught with P142) and both are correct. CONCLUSION: every pairing-based instrument has now failed (global balance, refcount-level table, final-tenure scoping). Switch to the OWNERSHIP question per GPT: preserve a vmcore or run drgn against the LIVE kernel while the leak exists, reverse-search memory for the inode pointer, and classify the containing object. unmount_leak_check.sh must be SPLIT to leave that window -- it currently unmounts AND rmmods before reporting. Inspect the MXFS DLM object (dlm_state=CACHED) and the inode log item (itemp=1, in_ail=0) reverse pointers first.
defects.sess27_P206_OWNERS_all_zero: NEW EVIDENCE, build 0.11.237 EF6935F7BE9995D4AAEB942. Since drgn/crash/gdb and debug symbols are ALL ABSENT from the test nodes (checked), GPT's reverse-search track was done from inside the module for the VFS structures that pin an inode invisibly and that nothing had ruled out. New probe P206-OWNERS, printed beside P202 at unmount. Reproduced 2 of 2 cycles at 16/caw; second capture (test?, ino 29360571): 'P206-OWNERS fsnotify=0 flctx=0 iprivate=0 nrpages=0 readcount=0 dentry_count=0 i_state=0x100 i_opflags=0xb'. EVERY VFS OWNER CANDIDATE IS ZERO -- no fsnotify mark connector, no file_lock_context, no i_private, no page cache, no read-only opens, and a true dentry-alias COUNT of 0 (not just the old boolean). i_state=0x100 is I_REFERENCED, set by __inode_lru_list_add on rotate, consistent with lru_linked=1. CONSEQUENCE: nothing reachable FROM the inode holds the reference. The owner must hold a bare struct inode*/xfs_inode* elsewhere -- an MXFS structure, a work/timer payload (all measured not pending), or a leaked local in a path that igrab'd and returned without storing the pointer. That last category is now the leading hypothesis and is NOT addressable by pairing instruments. This capture also shows the signature varies in its DLM fields across reproductions: capture 1 stale_src=2 bastq_src=1 zero_seq=1 tenure_grabs=499; capture 2 stale_src=8 bastq_src=9 zero_seq=9 tenure_grabs=542. So no single arm site is implicated. GRAB= is the ordinary xfs_iget_cache_hit igrab in both (xfs_icache.c ~1768/1809 -- the SAME site, line numbers shifted by this session's edits; do not read the change as two different sites).
defects.sess27_resolver_drives_the_bast_arms: CONNECTION worth keeping: mxfs_dlm_force_peer_flush() (xfs_mxfs_dlm.c ~30400) is just mxfs_dlm_ilock_begin(ip, PR) + mxfs_dlm_ilock_end(ip, PR) -- and ilock_end is the site at xfs_mxfs_dlm.c:27181 that igrabs and queues the BAST work with bastq_src=1. The xfs_lookup type-flip machinery calls force_peer_flush from BOTH the INODE-REUSE-EVICT retry (xfs_inode.c ~1571, up to 4x) and the P95B resolver loop (every 16th round, up to 201 rounds). So the resolver is the GENERATOR of the bast arms seen on leaked inodes, which is why bastq_src keeps pointing there. The arm site itself is correct (line 27187 xfs_irele on the queue_work-false path) and the INODE-REUSE-EVICT retry is correct too (xfs_irele(*ipp); *ipp=NULL; goto retry_iget). Recorded so the next session does not re-derive the call chain, and so 'bastq_src points at the resolver' is not mistaken for a hit.
defects.disposition: FIXED AND VERIFIED (sess36, 0.11.307/308). ROOT (kernel-side kprobe ref-trace, per-inode running-count reconstruction with ZERO anomalies, correlated to module prints at ms precision): mxfs_dlm_bast_notify's four dispatch sites returned without xfs_irele on queue_work()==false, leaking this call's iget ref on every collision with an already-pending work (which owns only the first donor's ref). Live capture ino 8391890: EDEADLK-failed EX acquire -> synchronous deferred-BAST honor -> bast_notify iget -> queue collision (P70-BP starts 10us later) -> P76-QW-FALSE site=immediate -> ref stranded; unmount signature icount=1 dentry_count=0 nothing-pending == every historical capture; prior arm-site audits were clean because the arms ARE clean — the leak was the notify dispatch. FIX: xfs_irele on the queue-false branch at all four sites (the ilock-end arm's existing correct pattern); GPT design review passed (ownership model confirmed; keep-and-park rejected). VERIFIED: (a) deterministic branch-coverage via TEST-ONLY mxfs.bast_qfalse_inject — 126 forced collisions through the fixed branch in one storm, zero queue-false leaks; (b) 8 consecutive clean reproducer cycles on fixed builds (pre-fix catch rate ~0.45/cycle across 11 cycles => P(8 clean unchanged) ~0.8%); (c) kprobe traces armed throughout. RESIDUAL SCOPE NOTE: sites none-held-idle/orphan-release/phantom-reconcile carry the code-identical one-line fix but their triggering recovery scenarios did not occur in any capture or cycle; the only site ever observed firing (immediate) is the demonstrated one. The DISTINCT teardown-ordering leak observed once on an infra-aborted cycle (P142-DWORK-STALE pag=NULL last-ref refusal) is split to D-DWORK-TEARDOWN-LASTREF-LEAK.

defects.summary: A dirent naming a REGULAR FILE resolves to a DIRECTORY inode; the type-flip resolver gives up and the name is durably corrupt cluster-wide
defects.evidence: ccloop c7ee71c6 sess22, 32/caw, after a 20-round sf_mkdir_storm on the same mount. `echo "hello from node 5" > .cache_coherency/cross_visibility/node5.txt` left: stat -> type=directory ino=60823425 size=6 nlink=2 mode=755, while its neighbours node4.txt/node6.txt are correct 18-byte regular files. Every one of the 32 nodes reads node5.txt as empty/absent-as-a-file. MXFS's own probes name it exactly: 'P95B-TYPEFLIP-WAIT ino=60823425 resolved=0 rounds=201 final_ftype=2 dirent_ftype=1 name=node5.txt' and 'P-EVICT-RESULT ino=60823425 final_mode=040755 final_ftype=2 dirent_ftype=1 fop_dir=1 tries=5'. dirent_ftype=1 is XFS_DIR3_FT_REG_FILE, final_ftype=2 is XFS_DIR3_FT_DIR.
defects.scale: Cluster-wide census: 165 P95B-TYPEFLIP-WAIT events across all 32 nodes; 109 resolved, 56 GAVE UP (resolved=0). All 56 unresolved are the same inode and the same name, i.e. the resolver handles most flips but can fail permanently on one -- and when it does, the corruption is durable and agreed on by every node. Also 196 RELOAD-TYPEFLIP-STALE-SKIP in the same window.
defects.mechanism: The corruption is in whatever EMITTED the dirent: a name produced by rename_visibility's rename carries ftype=REG while the inode it points at is a live directory of the same incarnation. Likely vector is cross-node inode-number REUSE -- the renamed file's inode was freed and re-allocated as a DIRECTORY by a peer while this node's dirent still claims REG (a dangling dirent surviving a peer's free). Note the adjacent probe RELOAD-TYPEFLIP-STALE-SKIP fires with incore_mode=0100644 vs disk_mode=040755 and KEEPS the in-core regular-file view over the disk's directory -- i.e. another guard is also picking the wrong side. UNROOTED: find the path that lets a REG dirent survive (or be created) against a live DIR inode.
defects.detector: dirent_type_integrity (tests/suite/dirent_type_integrity.sh, P8, coord=barrier) -- counts unresolved flips in the MXFS_DIRENT_WINDOW scoped to the current workload; threshold 0. MUST run after dirent_durability (P6), which stamps the marker; with no marker it FAILs rather than judging stale evidence. cache_coherency catches the user-visible symptom.
defects.blocking_fix: Root the dirent side. The lookup resolver cannot fix this -- both of its outcomes are wrong (publish a mismatch, or ESTALE forever). Fixing it requires either (a) preventing a peer's inode free/realloc from leaving our dirent dangling, or (b) making the dirent's ftype reconcilable against the inode's real type with a defined winner.
defects.reproduction: RELIABLE REPRODUCER FOUND (sess22): 16/caw, criterion `cache_coherency`, rename_visibility subtest. With NO injection armed (typeflip_force_unresolved=0), P201-TYPEFLIP-UNRESOLVED-FAIL fired 154 times cluster-wide in one run, e.g. 'ino=17315221 incore_ftype=2 dirent_ftype=1 incore_mode=040755 name=node12_after_1 comm=ls'. cache_coherency FAILS 0/16 with 'rv new exists node12_after_1' and 'rv content node12_after_1(exp=content_12_1 got=)'. This is FAR more prevalent than the single node5.txt instance first captured, and it does NOT need an aged mount -- it needs the rename workload. Supersedes the earlier 'intermittent, needs storm + heavy tests' note.
defects.attempted_and_refuted: sess27: P206-RENAME-FTYPE-STALE / P206-LINK-FTYPE-STALE -- the hypothesis that xfs_vn_rename/xfs_vn_link snapshot the dirent ftype from i_mode BEFORE the ILOCK (which an MXFS reload can change) so the written ftype can be stale. MEASURED 0 on every node while P201 fired 4x: the written ftype always matched the inode's post-lock type. Probes kept; knob mxfs.rename_ftype_revalidate ships default 0.

sess22_fix_attempt.change: v0.11.183 mxfs.typeflip_fail_unresolved (default 1): when xfs_lookup's P95B type-flip resolver exhausts its 200 rounds without matching the dirent's ground-truth ftype, FAIL the lookup with -ESTALE (drop the ref, leave *ipp NULL) instead of falling through and handing the VFS an inode whose type contradicts the dirent. Probe P201-TYPEFLIP-UNRESOLVED-FAIL.
sess22_fix_attempt.rationale: The pre-existing comment called the fall-through 'no worse than the old single-shot behavior'. It is worse: publishing the mismatch is exactly how the corruption becomes durable and agreed by all 32 nodes. -ESTALE is the correct 'revalidate and retry' contract and a reported failure beats silent namespace corruption.
sess22_fix_attempt.exercised: YES. v0.11.184 added TEST-ONLY mxfs.typeflip_force_unresolved to make the resolver give up immediately. Armed cluster-wide + storm: P201 fired 208 times, cache_coherency correctly reported the failure (31/32) instead of silently accepting a wrong-type inode, and ZERO durable type mismatches resulted (all 32 cross_visibility entries regular files).
sess22_fix_attempt.NOT_VALIDATED: The CONTROL arm (force_unresolved=1, fail_unresolved=0, i.e. the pre-fix fall-through) also produced ZERO durable mismatches. So the injection reproduces the GIVE-UP but not the CORRUPTION -- it makes the resolver stop early on flips that would have resolved anyway, rather than recreating the genuine reuse race where the in-core inode really is the wrong incarnation. The fix is principled and its path is proven to run, but it is NOT proven to prevent this defect.
sess22_fix_attempt.no_regression: 32/caw on 0.11.183 with the fix on and no injection: cache_coherency, strong_consistency, posix_multi, mmap_coherency, zero_silent_loss, rsync_paired, dir_reuse_coherency all PASS 32/32; two further storm+heavy-test aging cycles all PASS.
sess22_fix_attempt.next_step: Reproduce the genuine unresolved flip. The natural occurrence needed a mount aged by a storm PLUS several heavy criteria; a single storm after a fresh prep does not do it. Either age harder, or inject at the reuse site (bind a REG dirent to a live DIR inode) rather than at the resolver.
sess22_fix_attempt.effect_measured: My P201 change does NOT create failures -- it makes pre-existing ones visible. P201 fires only after the resolver has ALREADY given up 201 rounds, so all 154 would previously have been published as wrong-type bindings. Before: stat reports 'directory' (silent). After: stat reports ESTALE (visible). BUT the ESTALE is PERMANENT, not transient -- the in-core inode never converges, so every subsequent lookup fails too. The name is unusable either way; the fix buys visibility, not correctness. It is NOT a fix for this defect.

defects.which_side_is_wrong: REFUTED (sess27) -- the PLATTER INODE is the corrupt side, not the dirent. sess22 read the child's 'disk' mode through the BUFFER CACHE, the same path under suspicion, so both sides agreed and the reasoning was circular. New probe P207-COHERENT-TRUTH reads the platter with a PLAIN BIO at the resolver give-up: coh_mode=040755 coh_gen==incore_gen, i.e. the platter itself held the PRE-FREE DIRECTORY image. A live inode can never carry a generation older than its own free (EVICT-RING-FLAG showed incore_gen=2697616535 -> freed_gen=2697616536), which is what proves the platter stale. CONSEQUENCE: sess22's blocking_fix 'root the dirent side' aimed at the wrong half, which is why typeflip_fail_unresolved could never fix it.
defects.CORRECTION_prevalence: RETRACTED (sess22, self-caught): the counts I reported as prevalence -- '154 P201 at 16/caw' and '338 P201 on a freshly prepped mount' -- came from UNSCOPED `dmesg | grep -c` runs. prep_cluster does NOT clear the kernel ring and dmesg survives a module reload, so those scans swept in hits from earlier runs on earlier builds. Proof: a standalone run on a freshly prepped cluster read 32 hits that were ALL leftovers (same ino 17315221, same name node12_after_1, OLD probe format from before that build was compiled) while the workload in that run produced zero. PROPERLY SCOPED measurement (dirent_durability stamps MXFS_DIRENT_WINDOW, then dirent_type_integrity scans only after it), 16/caw: total_flips=80, unresolved=0, failed_estale=0, stale_skips=57. So type flips are COMMON and are normally RESOLVED; the UNRESOLVED case that produces the corruption is RARE and its true frequency is NOT established. What remains solid is the captured instance itself: node5.txt durably a directory on all 32 nodes, with disk_mode=040755 and disk_gen==incore_gen. The defect is real; my frequency claims were not.

ROOT_CAUSE_sess27.root: RELOAD-TYPEFLIP-STALE-SKIP (xfs_mxfs_dlm.c ~20198) kept the in-core inode whenever disk_gen <= incore_gen. XFS generations are RANDOM, so on a genuine cross-node inode-number reuse that comparison is a COIN FLIP; when it lost, the node kept a DEAD incarnation and its release drain PUBLISHED that corpse over the peer's live inode. sess96's own comment two lines above already noted the gen test is unreliable but only patched the case where a lookup supplied a dirent ftype -- with expect_ftype==UNKNOWN (reload from a release/BAST path) the broken comparison was the ONLY discriminator.
ROOT_CAUSE_sess27.byte_exact_capture: 32/caw ino 10485888 name node15.txt: test15 creates dir gen 2697616535; test15 frees it (freed_gen=2697616536); test15 reuses the number for a REGULAR FILE with new random gen 2379993492; test30 logs RELOAD-TYPEFLIP-STALE-SKIP incore_mode=040755 disk_mode=0100644 incore_gen=2697616535 disk_gen=2379993492 expect_ft=0 -- reads the CORRECT image and rejects it; test30 then P170-CLWR publishes 10485888:40755:..6535 at realns ...79.98, 2.5s AFTER test15 published 10485888:100644:..3492 at realns ...77.48.
ROOT_CAUSE_sess27.fix: mxfs.typeflip_skip_same_incarn (default 1): the skip requires disk_gen == incore_gen (same incarnation) -- exactly what sess103 already did for the sibling RELOAD-SIZE-DROP-SKIP and what the guard's own documented target case (sess90 stale-cluster clobber) has. 0 = legacy <= as a same-build negative control. New probe P208-TYPEFLIP-REUSE counts the dangerous subset (different incarnation, lower random gen) in BOTH arms with action=keep|adopt.
ROOT_CAUSE_sess27.paired_AB_one_build: 0.11.234 EF05E2534A9855795A875F8, knob flipped at runtime, fresh mkfs per arm. A(=0): cache_coherency FAIL 1/32 failed=2; dirent_type_integrity FAIL 5/32 unresolved=4; P208=432 action=keep; STALE-SKIP=432; P201=165; P207=165.  B(=1): cache_coherency PASS 32/32 654/654 23s; dirent_type_integrity PASS 32/32 unresolved=0; P208=223 action=adopt; STALE-SKIP=0; P201=0; P207=0.
ROOT_CAUSE_sess27.causal_link: An earlier control iteration PASSED with P208=0 -- it never entered the state. The failure tracks the EXPOSURE, not the arm label: exposure>0 + keep = corruption, exposure>0 + adopt = clean.
ROOT_CAUSE_sess27.reproducer: prep -> dirent_durability -> cache_coherency (3 for 3 pre-fix). dirent_durability's 30-round mkdir/rmdir storm is the AGING pass driving cross-node inode-number reuse; cache_coherency then creates regular files onto the reused numbers. Running cache_coherency FIRST (manifest order, fresh mount) does NOT reproduce it -- which is why the board showed 654/654 green for many sessions. Harnesses: tests/typeflip_ab.sh, tests/inode_cluster_clobber_capture.sh.
ROOT_CAUSE_sess27.still_open_because: RULE 6 needs testing that exercises the cause to pass cleanly. One paired iteration each so far. Accumulating more paired iterations plus a full-board regression pass on the fix before any disposition.
ROOT_CAUSE_sess27.disposition: FIXED AND VERIFIED (RULE 6), ccloop c7ee71c6 sess27, build 0.11.234 EF05E2534A9855795A875F8.  (1) CAUSE PROVEN by RULE 4: byte-exact cross-node timeline for ino 10485888/node15.txt, the guard's own kernel line showing test30 reading the CORRECT new image (disk_mode=0100644 disk_gen=2379993492) and rejecting it, and P207-COHERENT-TRUTH proving via a PLAIN BIO that the platter itself carried the pre-free DIR image -- a generation older than that inode's own free, which no correct FS can expose.  (2) The patch targets exactly that comparison and nothing else, mirroring the sess103 same-incarnation gate already applied to the sibling RELOAD-SIZE-DROP-SKIP.  (3) TESTING THAT EXERCISES THE CAUSE PASSES CLEANLY under UNCHANGED acceptance criteria: the sess27 reproducer (prep -> dirent_durability -> cache_coherency) run 4 times on the fix arm, every run exercising the cause (P208 exposure 223/123/282/233, all action=adopt) and every run clean -- cache_coherency 32/32 654/654, dirent_type_integrity 32/32 unresolved=0, and P201=P207=RELOAD-TYPEFLIP-STALE-SKIP=0 in all four.  Same-build control arm (knob=0) FAILED 2 of 2 whenever exposure was nonzero (P208 432 and 552, action=keep; cache_coherency FAIL 1/32 and 3/32; dirent_type_integrity FAIL 5/32 and 8/32) and PASSED the one iteration where exposure was 0, i.e. the outcome tracks the EXPOSURE rather than the arm label.  (4) NO REGRESSION: full 32/caw board on the fix -- fio_perf, fio_perf_vs_xfs, cache_coherency, strong_consistency, posix_multi, mmap_coherency, zero_silent_loss, dlm_fairness, dlm_membership, scaling_curve, dlm_scaling, rsync_paired, crash_consistency, dir_reuse_coherency, fence_during_write, fault_netpartition, soak, dirent_durability, dirent_type_integrity, node_responsive, kernel_health, sustained_load, dlm_lock_correctness all PASS.  No acceptance threshold was widened; two criteria were made STRICTER this session.

defects.LIMIT_ON_THE_CLAIM: What is proven is that THIS defect -- a dirent whose ftype contradicts the inode it names, produced by RELOAD-TYPEFLIP-STALE-SKIP retaining a dead incarnation and publishing it -- was fixed under the stated verification.  It is NOT a claim that no untested workload can surface a different stale-image publish.  The knob-0 legacy path remains in the tree only as the negative control.

defects.summary: crash_consistency cannot finish inside its budget at 32 nodes
evidence: sess23 @32/caw on 0.11.194 (BDD132E1285CDEB945565F1): crash_consistency FAIL nodes_pass=0/32 states:NO_TERMINAL_RECORD=32 at exactly 90s/90s — every node failed to print a terminal RESULT line before the budget expired. defects.diagnosis_sess24: ATTRIBUTED BY PER-PHASE INSTRUMENTATION (mxfs-CCph stamps, now in the test). It is NOT a hang and NOT a correctness failure: zero checks fail. Per-phase means at 32 nodes: barrier_ready 0.16s, write 50 files oflag=sync 22.67s, write 50 md5 sidecars 19.50s, barrier_written 7.04s, drop_caches+sleep 3.96s, verify 200 cold files 8.69s => SUM OF MEANS 62.5s, which matches the clean 2x-per-doubling series (1n=2 2n=5 4n=8 8n=16 16n=32s) extrapolated to ~64s. But SUM OF MAX is 98.96s, so the slowest node exceeds the 90s budget; every node then blocks at the final barrier and is killed, producing states:NO_TERMINAL_RECORD=32 with no failed check. 68% of the wall (42.2s of 62.5s) is creating 100 small files per node (50 data + 50 .md5) into ONE shared directory — the same mechanism as D-DIR-REUSE-COHERENCY-32-FLAKY. MULTIPATH HYPOTHESIS REFUTED: the recorded 32/cawd=65s and 32/cawp=66s passes are from 2026-07-25/26 on OLDER builds, so the device attribution was confounded; and the CAW attempt census measures CAW service time at 1.5% of grant wait with ZERO io errors, so the dm-multipath command path is not the cost.
defects.disposition_sess24: NOT A PACE DEFECT. It was the wedged node. After recovering test27 (D-BAST-WRITEBACK-ABBA-DEADLOCK) and re-prepping, crash_consistency PASSES 32/32 at 64s of its 90s budget on the SAME build and SAME device (/dev/mapper/mpatha). 64s is exactly the value the clean 2x-per-doubling series predicts (1n=2 2n=5 4n=8 8n=16 16n=32) and it matches 32/cawd=65s and 32/cawp=66s. The earlier per-phase capture is consistent with this in hindsight: it reported only 27-30 of 32 ranks, and the sum-of-MAX that exceeded the budget (99s) was the sick node dragging the tail while sum-of-means was a healthy 62.5s. Reclassified rather than closed: the cause is now attributed to another OPEN defect, so it is resolved only when D-BAST-WRITEBACK-ABBA-DEADLOCK is fixed and verified.
