defects.diagnosis_sess24: RECLASSIFIED FROM CRITICAL COHERENCY TO MAJOR PACE. The failing run's 'checks=51 passed=50 failed=1 with all 32 nodes agreeing on the wrong answer' is NOT a durable coherent wrong result. The node script emits exactly checks = 7*rounds + 2 (1 ready barrier + 4 barriers and 3 ckeq per round + 1 final pace assertion); this is integral for all 25 recorded conditions (1..32 nodes x caw/cawd/cawp/tcp/xfs), so it is the script's arithmetic, not a coincidence. checks=51 => 7 rounds completed and the ONE failed check is the final pace assertion rounds_done>=8. checks=58 (the passing re-run) => 8 rounds. All 32 nodes agree because rank 1 alone coordinates the time box, so every node evaluates the same rounds_done. Rounds completed vs node count for identical 128-file work: 1n=24(capped) 2n=21 4n=21 8n=17 16n=13 32n=8. The 32-node column sits EXACTLY on the floor. NOT namespace corruption; do not chase a leaf-hash hole.

defects.disposition: DISPROVED as an MXFS defect (sess39, 2026-08-01): the intermittent <8-round failures are driven by host-rig storage-path write-latency degradation, established by measurement fully independent of mxfs. EVIDENCE: (1) failure occurs iff runs execute consecutively; first-run-after->=25min-idle passed 5/5 today (8,9,8,8,9 rounds; two idle-recovery cycles reproduced on schedule). (2) During plateau runs, a pure-host 4K O_DSYNC dd probe on clyde's root fs (no mxfs in path) degrades p90 26->95ms max 164->1806ms, and nvme0n1 block-layer write await (below ext4/SCST) grows p50 1.19->4.29ms p90 15->49ms; the mxfs barrier phases that grew (wrbar/presync/rm/lookups) are exactly the flush/write-bound ones, max-of-32-nodes per barrier amplifying the tails. (3) Same-state controls: on-disk CAW table byte-identical before fast and slow runs; guest CPU flat per-second; xs_sleep_logspace=0 and all log/AIL counters flat; steal-growth artifact traced to fail-path dmesg collection. (4) Rig environment: Samsung 990 EVO Plus (consumer TLC, dynamic SLC cache) 93% full hosting the SCST fileio backing store on the host ROOT fs, with ambient user writers (python3 -m myse: 1.19TB/9h; game server) — consistent with SLC-cache/GC exhaustion under 2000-2600 write ops/s test load, recovering over ~25min idle. RESIDUAL MXFS WORK (already OPEN elsewhere): per-turn EX-rotation economics incl. flush amplification (~85 drain flushes/round) tracked by D-32NODE-SHARED-DIR-CREATE-PACE + D-READDIR-PEER-CACHED-DIR-PACE; grace default 40->10 pending board (fresh+g10 = 9 rounds vs 8 at g40). RIG CONSTRAINT RECORDED: dir_reuse pace results are only comparable from a fresh (>=25min idle) storage state; recommend relocating disk.img off the 93%-full root nvme or pausing ambient writers for pace-sensitive boards.

defects.summary: Concurrent create into ONE SHARED directory costs 8.3x more wall per node at 32 nodes than the same creates into per-node private directories (1842 ms vs 222 ms for 8 creates; 9.3x on the mean, 34x on p95), and the cost is ENTIRELY IN THE TAIL -- the shared arm's p50 is 10 ms and flat in N, so every node pays roughly one multi-second stall per 8 creates rather than a uniformly slower create. 74.5% of blocked samples sit in the CAW inode-grant wait (mxfs_pal_cond_timedwait under caw_lock_body), against 7.0% in the SCSI transport, so this is the DLM's EX rotation among 32 contenders on one directory inode. A second, smaller term rides underneath: the PRIVATE arm is not flat either, growing 6x from 1 to 32 nodes (37 -> 222 ms) with nothing shared but the mount. (sess380 re-measured all of this after fixing tests/create_scale_curve.sh, whose private arm had been running a 32-way mkdir on a shared parent INSIDE the measured window; the previously recorded '42x, private scales flat' figures came from that contaminated control.)
evidence:
SESS380 THE LOAD IS READS, AND THEY ARE THE PROBE WALK — NOT THE CAS COLLISION, WHICH IS WHAT THIS ENTRY (AND I, EARLIER THE SAME SESSION) SPENT THE MOST EFFORT ON. New harness tests/shared_dir_slot_cost.sh counts every SCSI command the whole cluster issues to the ONE CAW slot of a shared directory while 32 nodes do 256 creates into it. Repeated over 6 runs on 0.15.6-0.15.10, stable:
    READ(16)+FUA       5,844 - 8,587   = 23 - 34 per create
    COMPARE AND WRITE    424 -   515   = 1.7 - 2.0 per create (50-52% MISCOMPARE)
  reads are 93% of ALL traffic on that sector and outnumber writes 13-16 to 1.
P383-SLOTREAD then tagged every one of those reads with its caller (7,653 tagged reads, one run):
    find_slot_skip                6,373   83.3%   <- the open-addressing PROBE WALK
    caw_wait_for_grant              880   11.5%   <- the grant poll loop
    caw_count_resource_slots        398    5.2%
    bast_poll_fn                      2    0.0%
So ~25 of the ~30 reads per create are slot RESOLUTION, re-walked from scratch on every lookup, and the resource's home slot IS the hot sector, so every walk reads it at least once. The grant poll loop — the thing four sessions of this entry's history blamed — is 11.5%.

SESS380 FOUR HYPOTHESES REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT, recorded so nobody re-runs them. Each was cheap and each was wrong; together they are what narrowed the search to the probe walk.
  (1) 'The unlock CAS keeps losing to peers REGISTERING INTEREST, so skip the backoff when the miscompare was a pure registration.' Built an exact-transition classifier (reconstructs byte for byte the only image a registration could produce, then memcmps) and ran it with the acting knob OFF: of 475 unlock miscompares, 1 was benign (0.2%), 7 were holder changes, ZERO were yield_to moves, and 467 (98.3%) were MULTI-GENERATION — several unrelated writes landed between our compare image and our re-read. The optimisation would fire on 0.2% of cases. mxfs.caw_unlock_fastretry ships DEFAULT 0 and should stay there; the classifier is retained because its histogram is what produced this finding.
  (2) 'Releases wake the whole waiter field, so every handoff costs N reads.' P382-WAKE says the wake-the-field branch is taken 0.0% of the time: 75.7% mint a single successor, 24.3% use an existing ticket, mean 1.25 nodes woken against 4.70 waiters present.
  (3) 'The 2ms fastpoll window is the amplifier' (a suspicion written into the mxfs.caw_inode_fastpoll knob's own comment years ago). Turning it OFF made reads WORSE: 26.6 -> 32.9 per create.
  (4) 'The reads are exponential-backstop timeouts, and the nudge would carry the grants anyway' — supported by P297-TKT showing 96.6% of ticketed waiters wake by NUDGE with ZERO swallowed nudges. Raising mxfs.caw_poll_max_ms from 25 to 200 made BOTH worse: reads 22.8 -> 29.6 per create and per-node wall 1577 -> 2612 ms. Removing the fastpoll window on top of that: 33.5 reads, 2767 ms.
Also refuted structurally: there is NO I/O and no blocking call between the slot read and the CAW in the unlock loop, so the collision window is pure CPU and cannot be narrowed.

SESS380 MECHANISM, MEASURED ON BOTH SIDES OF THE SAME SLOT. The contended resource is not the transport and not a long holder doing real work -- it is that ONE 512B CAW slot is the single mutable cell holding a directory's ENTIRE lock state (holder bitmaps per mode, waiter bitmap, waiter_ex bitmap, yield ticket, generation). At 32 contenders, a waiter REGISTERING its waiter bit and the holder CLEARING its holder bit are COMPARE AND WRITE against the same word, so they invalidate each other. Both halves are now counted directly:
  RELEASE SIDE (P381-UNLK-CONTEND, new this session, fires only when the unlock CAS lost a race):
    112 contended unlocks in one 32-node shared-directory create run
    mean retries 1.96, mean MISCOMPAREs 1.96, mean backoff sleep 10.1 ms,
    mean unlock wall 27.9 ms, max 77 ms; the backoff sleep is 36% of that wall and the
    remaining 64% is the extra find_slot READ + CAW that each losing retry issues.
    78 of the 112 were on ino=131, the directory under test.
  ACQUIRE SIDE (P139-LOCKTOTAL -EAGAIN attribution, same run):
    121 acquire retries, of which 109 are ea_regwait -- LOST THE WAITER-REGISTER CAS --
    12 ea_compat, and ZERO ea_claim. The losses are on registering interest, not on
    claiming a free slot.
  HOLDER-SIDE COST BREAKDOWN (P138-BAST, ino=131): dur_us 26,565 / 36,542 / 42,830 / 48,457 with
    sx (the WIRE UNLOCK proper) = 25,976 / 32,919 / 40,624 / 46,384 us, i.e. 95-98% of the release.
    The mandatory drain pipeline (sa+sb+sc+sd) is only 2-4 ms of it. The release is not slow
    because of the durability work; it is slow because the unlock cannot win its own CAS.
THE FEEDBACK LOOP IS THE POINT: every waiter that registers extends the holder's release, the longer release lengthens the queue, and the longer queue brings more registering waiters. Cost is therefore superlinear in N, which is what the 1 -> 32 ladder shows (37 -> 1842 ms, 49.8x). This is precisely the failure mode the sess379 RULE-5 review predicted for this format -- 'every successful update invalidates all competing comparisons ... N simultaneous distinct bit updates approach O(N^2) total work ... no backoff changes the serialization bound' -- and its prescribed fix is the same one that applies here: a writer GATE record plus incarnation-tagged PER-NODE reader records at independently writable locations, so registering interest writes to the node's OWN sector instead of CASing the shared word. See ccmemory ccloop-c7ee71c6-sess379-GPT-ruling-hot-slot-caw-fix-shape.

SESS380 WHY THIS DEFECT RESISTED ATTRIBUTION FOR SO LONG -- TWO BLIND PROBES AND A BROKEN CONTROL, all three fixed this session. (1) P138-WAIT fires when ONE wait_for_grant call exceeds 5 ms, but a contended acquire is many sub-5 ms waits with outer retries between them: on a run whose creates measured p95 424 ms it produced FOUR lines fleet-wide. (2) P139-LOCKTOTAL brackets the whole acquire including retries -- the right probe -- but its floor was hardcoded at 800 ms, ABOVE the entire distribution, so it produced ZERO lines. It is now a knob (mxfs.caw_locktotal_ms, default unchanged at 800); at a 50 ms floor the same workload yields 118 acquires totalling 57.1 s, which matches the workload's own total create time -- i.e. the census now accounts for essentially all of the tail instead of 0.4% of it. (3) tests/caw_grant_wait_anatomy.sh only ever ran the PRIVATE shape and let each node mkdir inside the measured window, so it censused the parent inode's mkdir rather than the shared directory under test; it now takes SHAPE=shared|private, pre-creates every directory from one node, arms the P139 floor on all nodes and restores it, and harvests P139-LOCKTOTAL / P139-TAILCENSUS / P34-ACQ-SLOW as well as the per-wait probes. Any pre-sess380 number from these three tools understates the tail or measures the wrong resource.

SESS380 CLEAN LADDER, on a harness whose private arm is FINALLY a control. tests/create_scale_curve.sh was fixed this session to pre-create BOTH shapes' directories from one node; before that, every node in the `private` arm ran `mkdir -p $dirbase/r$i` INSIDE the measured window, so all P nodes took the same parent inode EX and both arms contended on a shared directory. That artifact is the most likely explanation for the two irreconcilable private-arm numbers already in this entry ('wall 33..41ms, FLAT in N' vs 'mean 5.2..191.8ms, 37x in N'). With the fix, 32 healthy nodes (all mounted, max loadavg 0.56, full 27/27 board green minutes earlier), fresh fs, 8 creates/node, MXFS 0.15.4 sv DACACDDE464B211CF68DE3F on SCST +caw-abort-reclaim.3:
  participants          1      2      4      8     16     32
  PRIVATE wall_p50     37    170    104    125    220    222  ms   <- 6.0x from 1 to 32
  PRIVATE mean        3.9   11.9   10.8   13.3   25.3   25.0  ms
  PRIVATE p50           4     12      8     10     16     19  ms
  PRIVATE p95           7     43     36     46     90     63  ms
  SHARED  wall_p50     37     87    160    385   1000   1842  ms   <- 49.8x from 1 to 32
  SHARED  mean        3.9    8.5   18.1   44.2  122.5  233.2  ms
  SHARED  p50           3      7      7      8     10     10  ms   <- FLAT in N
  SHARED  p95           8     31    105    305   1021   2170  ms   <- ALL the cost is here
SHARED vs PRIVATE at 32 nodes: 1842 vs 222 ms wall = 8.3x; 233.2 vs 25.0 ms mean = 9.3x; 2170 vs 63 ms p95 = 34x. So the shared-directory framing of this entry is CONFIRMED, at 8-34x rather than the previously recorded 42x, and it lives ENTIRELY IN THE TAIL -- the shared arm's p50 is 10 ms at 32 nodes, flat in N and no worse than the private arm's 19 ms. Every node pays roughly one multi-second stall per 8 creates. Separately, the private arm is NOT flat either (37 -> 222 ms, 6x), which is a smaller but real common-mode scaling cost that this entry should not lose sight of.

SESS380 STALL-SITE CENSUS ON THE FIXED TARGET (tests/create_stall_stacks.sh 8 32, 776 blocked samples at 50 ms across 32 nodes). Task state 77.7% S / 22.3% D. Nearest non-generic blocking frame:
  74.5%  mxfs_pal_cond_timedwait   (caw_lock_body <- mxfs_dlm_caw_lock <- mxfs_v5_dlm_inode_lock
                                     <- mxfs_dlm_inode_lock_routed <- mxfs_dlm_ilock_begin)
   9.8%  mxfs_dlm_ilock_begin      (xfs_ilock <- xfs_ilock_data_map_shared <- xfs_dir_lookup)
   7.0%  blk_execute_rq            (the SCSI READ(16)+FUA inside read_slot)
   1.5%  mxfs_pal_sleep_ms | 1.4% mxfs_inode_cluster_durable | 1.4% xfs_iget | 1.4% xfs_buf_iowait
This is the SAME verdict as the earlier census (then 75.3% caw_acquire_poll_sleep, since replaced by a condvar) and it is decisive for attribution: the cost is WAITING FOR A DLM GRANT on one directory inode, not transport. The transport share actually FELL from 14.2% to 7.0% once the target's wait-for cycle was fixed, and this entry's own CAW attempt census already measured CAW service time at 1.5% of grant wait with zero I/O errors. Do NOT re-attribute this defect to D-HOT-SLOT-CAW-SERIALIZES-LUN-PER-LBA-379 (DISPROVED sess380): that entry was about per-LBA command serialization at the target, which is now measured at 1.6x, while this is the DLM's own EX rotation among 32 contenders.

Measured on the live 32-node cluster, per-create latency, files written into per-node PRIVATE subdirectories of ONE shared parent so the only contended resource is the parent directory inode (tests/create_scale_curve.sh):
  participants   1     2     4     8    16    32
  p50  ms        5     6     7     8    12    11   <- FLAT in N
  mean ms      5.2   9.2  10.8  26.0  71.7 191.8   <- 37x in N
Shared-dir shape is only ~1.3x worse than private-subdir (247.9 vs 191.8 mean at 32), so dirent/leaf serialisation is SECONDARY; the cost is the parent inode lock. Native local-fs reference on the same nodes: 2.6ms mean. Uncontended MXFS is healthy at 5.2ms.
Stall site read off the kernel, not guessed (tests/create_stall_stacks.sh, 1005 blocked /proc/PID/stack samples): 75.3% caw_acquire_poll_sleep under mxfs_dlm_inode_lock_routed -> mxfs_v5_dlm_inode_lock -> mxfs_dlm_caw_lock -> caw_wait_for_grant; 14.2% read_slot's SCSI READ(16)+FUA; 4.2% ilock.
CAW attempt census per logical grant (tests/caw_grant_wait_anatomy.sh, the measurement GPT named as decisive): CAW submissions mean 6.1 max 33; miscompares mean 5.1 max 32; io errors 0; CAW SERVICE TIME 617ms = 1.5% of 42.1s of grant wait; slot poll READs mean 52.6 max 223. So the wait is ~52 poll cycles per grant, NOT transport service time (1.5%) and NOT CAS throughput (~1.2% at 0.65ms per CAW). The contended resource is ONE directory inode with mixed demand: measured slot masks ino=131 req_mode=PR waiters=0xfb4dffff waiters_ex=0x28440804 holders_pr=0x4820000 holders_ex=0 => 28 waiters of which 6 want EX, 3 hold PR, none holds EX.

sess43 ROUND DECOMPOSITION (new, tests/drc_phase_census.py over all 32 nodes' DRCph kmsg markers, 0.11.353, 286 phase samples): round wall median 9.16s. Segments (median s, share): create-start->sync1 1.97 (20%), wave1->wave2 1.71 (17%), create-done->wrbar 2.51 (25%, the write-barrier WAIT = cross-node skew), wrbar->presync 0.72 (7%), presync->dc 1.03 (10%, drop_caches), dc-real->ls 1.04 (11%, cold ls), ls->lookups 0.52 (5%), verify->rm 0.34 (3%). Cost model that fits: 2 create-waves x 32 nodes = 64 directory-EX turns/round at ~50ms/turn (matches the prior P138 clean-handoff 13ms + queueing, and the 12.7-54ms wire-unlock CAW figure) ~= 3.2s.

sess43 LEVER A/B REFUTED: dir_ex_batch_grace_ms 10/60/150 at 32/caw gave 7/6/5 rounds — longer grace is monotonically WORSE (waiter pile-up), confirming the sess39 finding on a current build. Holding the tenure longer is NOT the lever.

sess43 CONFOUNDER FOUND — HOST LOAD modulates this criterion and invalidates uncontrolled A/Bs. Same build 0.11.353, same day: 8-10 rounds/100s at hypervisor load 11-17 (morning board) vs 5-7 rounds at load 28-30 (Wow.exe 384%% + worldserver 315%% + other tenants); guest-internal load stayed <1 while steal accumulated (test1 steal=7851 ticks). A fresh re-prep at high load still gave 7 then 6, so this is NOT mount-degradation-with-use and NOT the grace parameter. defects.summary: mxfs_dlm_bast_process waits on a FOLIO LOCK while holding the inode DLM/ILOCK, deadlocking against writeback which holds that folio lock and waits for the inode lock — a permanent single-node hang
defects.evidence:
CAPTURED LIVE on test27 (32/caw, build C786A05FF756A6C1C6FF797), both sides of the cycle, from /proc/<pid>/stack:

A) pid 662372 kworker/u9:29+mxfs-ino-bast/dm-1  wchan=folio_wait_bit_common
     folio_wait_bit_common <- __folio_lock <- write_cache_pages
     <- iomap_writepages <- xfs_vm_writepages <- do_writepages
     <- filemap_fdatawrite_wbc <- __filemap_fdatawrite_range
     <- filemap_write_and_wait_range
     <- mxfs_dlm_bast_process+0x5d5 <- mxfs_dlm_bast_work_fn+0x13a
   => holds the inode DLM/ILOCK context, BLOCKED ON A FOLIO LOCK.

B) pid 662838 kworker/u12:30+flush-252:1  wchan=mxfs_dlm_ilock_begin
     mxfs_dlm_ilock_begin <- xfs_ilock <- xfs_map_blocks
     <- iomap_writepage_map <- iomap_do_writepage <- write_cache_pages
     <- iomap_writepages <- xfs_vm_writepages <- do_writepages
     <- __writeback_single_inode <- writeback_sb_inodes
     <- __writeback_inodes_wb <- wb_writeback <- wb_do_writeback
   => holds the folio lock (write_cache_pages locks folios before calling
      iomap_writepage_map), BLOCKED ON THE INODE LOCK.

Pile-up behind the cycle: 4+ `sync` processes in D state at
wb_wait_for_completion / sync_inodes_sb, plus kworker inode_switch_wbs.
loadavg 20.02 vs 0.00 on a healthy peer; a single 1-file write took 69ms vs
11ms. mxfs still mounted, no BUG/WARNING, no filesystem shutdown — the node
looks HEALTHY to every liveness check while being permanently unable to
complete a sync.
defects.lock_order_violated: Upstream XFS/iomap writeback order is FOLIO LOCK -> then xfs_ilock (see write_cache_pages -> iomap_writepage_map -> xfs_map_blocks -> xfs_ilock). Therefore any path that already holds the inode lock must NEVER wait on a folio lock. mxfs_dlm_bast_process calls filemap_write_and_wait_range while holding it, which takes folio locks, and inverts the order. This is the same family as the 'ILOCK held across CAW poll' design tension in CLAUDE.md, but a distinct, concretely captured instance.
defects.blast_radius: ONE wedged node fails the entire 32-node board. Barrier criteria need all N ranks, so the aggregate reads `FAIL nodes_pass=0/32 states:NO_TERMINAL_RECORD=32` — indistinguishable from a totally broken filesystem. Observed exactly that for cache_coherency, strong_consistency, posix_multi, mmap_coherency, zero_silent_loss, dlm_fairness and dlm_membership, all on a cluster where 31 of 32 nodes were perfectly healthy. The straggler is nameable from the peers' own reasons: 16 nodes reported `sc node27 last counter(exp=node27_seq20 got=node27_seq1)` while 15 blocked at `sc barrier write-done`. dir_reuse_coherency was UNAFFECTED (still 10 rounds in 110s), which is what proves the filesystem itself was not slower.
defects.blocking_fix: mxfs_dlm_bast_process must not perform a folio-lock-taking writeback (filemap_write_and_wait_range / do_writepages) while holding the inode DLM lock. Options, in order of preference: (1) stage the data flush BEFORE acquiring the inode lock for the BAST, then re-validate under the lock; (2) drop the inode lock across the flush and re-acquire + re-check epoch, the shape already used for dp ILOCK in xfs_create (v0.3.148); (3) if neither is possible, the drain must use a non-blocking writeback and retry rather than wait. NOTE architectural invariant 1: the drain pipeline must still complete before any on-disk unlock, so a bounded retry is required, not a skip.
defects.detection_gap: No criterion detects a D-state mxfs kworker. precond_readiness checks mount + readability, both of which a deadlocked node passes. A per-node D-state / sync-liveness precondition is needed so this reports as a NODE FAULT instead of manufacturing 32 correctness reds.
defects.fix_attempt_sess24:
FIX-27 WRITTEN, SHIPPED DEFAULT OFF, NOT VERIFIED (mxfs.fix27_shared_admit).
Hypothesis: FIX-26 admits the writeback submitter only when it requests EX, but xfs_map_blocks() takes xfs_ilock(ip, XFS_ILOCK_SHARED) first (pal/linux/xfs_aops.c:532), so a folio needing no delalloc conversion requests PR, fails the EX-only gate, parks holding the folio, and deadlocks the drain. FIX-27 widens the admit to shared-class requests from writepages context.
WHY IT IS OFF: measured never to engage. P47-FILEBLOCK (now printing g2, in_wb, in_ioend) census over a healthy 32-node cache_coherency + zero_silent_loss run:
   4435  req=3 mode=0 state=3 g2=3 in_wb=0 in_ioend=0
    181  req=3 mode=0 state=0 g2=0 in_wb=0 in_ioend=0
     38  req=3 mode=0 state=3 g2=0 in_wb=0 in_ioend=0
     13  req=5 mode=0 state=2 g2=3 in_wb=0 in_ioend=0
      4  req=3 mode=3 state=3 g2=3 in_wb=0 in_ioend=0
TOTAL blocks from writeback OR ioend context: ZERO (in_wb=1 or in_ioend=1 = 0). Blockers are ordinary syscalls: stat 3879, cat 488, md5sum 309, rm 13, bash 10 -- all of which MUST keep waiting; admitting them would be wrong. Turning FIX-27 on produced 0 P25 admits across 3613 shared blocks, and both criteria still passed (and ran slightly faster, 22s/18s vs 27s/28s), with 577 P15-REL-ABORT, so no release-churn harm was observed either way.
NOTE the 4435-row detail: g2=3 (mirror granted PR) means the admit's granted-mode precondition WOULD pass; the only refusal for those is in_wb=0/in_ioend=0. So the admit machinery is healthy and correctly scoped -- the deadlock is a rare race in which a writeback submitter IS the blocker, which this workload never produced.
defects.reproduction_status: NOT REPRODUCED. scripts/fix27_wb_shared_exerciser.sh drives the intended collision (writer rewrites REAL extents with conv=notrunc so map_blocks takes SHARED and never converts -- deliberately inverting FIX-26's v4 lesson that conv=notrunc leaves no delalloc; hot bdi flusher; peer reader storm; mxfs.fix27_delay_ms holds the folio-locked task until the inode is mid-drain). After fixing its predicate to break ONLY into BAST/DEMOTING (v1 broke on ANY state change, including BAST->CACHED, giving 6/68 useless collisions), it reaches 200/200 collisions -- and STILL produces 0 P47, 0 P25 and no wedge in BOTH arms. So the harness makes the submitter collide with a drain but never makes the drain block on THAT submitter's folio, which is the missing half of the cycle.
defects.next_step: 1. P47-FILEBLOCK now prints req/mode/state/g2/in_wb/in_ioend. The next natural occurrence therefore NAMES the failing admit precondition instead of requiring inference from two stacks -- in particular it settles whether the wedged submitter requested EX (xfs_convert_blocks is static and likely INLINED into xfs_map_blocks, so the captured stack cannot distinguish them, and if it was EX then FIX-26 was the relevant admit and some other precondition failed) or SHARED (FIX-27's case).\n2. To reproduce deterministically the harness must synchronise on the OTHER half: make the bast drain's filemap_write_and_wait block on a KNOWN folio, then release the submitter holding exactly that folio. That needs a drain-side marker (e.g. record the folio index the drain is waiting on) rather than only a submitter-side delay.\n3. The node-fault pre-assert in run.sh now BLOCKS and names any sync-wedged node, so a recurrence is caught immediately with its D-state stacks instead of being laundered into 32 correctness reds.
defects.disposition: FIXED_AND_VERIFIED
defects.root_cause_sess25: PROVEN. mxfs_dlm_bast_process calls filemap_write_and_wait at TWO sites and they are not equivalent. Site 1 runs while i_dlm_mode is still the granted mode, so mxfs_dlm_ilock_begin's nest-admit fast path (i_dlm_mode >= request) grants a colliding writeback submitter outright and NOTHING EVER PARKS. Site 2 (the S_ISREG durability flush) runs AFTER `ip->i_dlm_mode = MXFS_LOCK_NL` and BEFORE the wire unlock; mode==NL fails every nest-admit, so the submitter parks in the demote-wait STILL HOLDING ITS FOLIO and this flush blocks on it. That is why sess24's exerciser recorded 200/200 'collisions' with 0 P47/0 P25: it broke out on state==BAST|DEMOTING, which is reached at site 1. The parking precondition is mode==NL, not the state. New field i_dlm_drain_site records which flush the drain is in; P47-FILEBLOCK prints it as dsite=.
defects.reproducer: tests/abba_wedge_ab.sh <drainhost> <peerhost> <0|1> [secs] [stall_ms] -- DETERMINISTIC. New test-only knob mxfs.fix28_drain_stall_ms stalls the drain once, mid-batch, inside its site-2 flush after write_cache_pages has fetched a dirty-tagged folio batch and locked its first folio; a submitter arriving during the stall locks a LATER folio of that batch and parks holding it, and the drain then blocks on exactly that folio. writeback_get_folio() locks UNCONDITIONALLY and works off the already-fetched batch, so the submitter clearing the dirty bit is no reprieve. Harness facts, both measured: the peer must READ (a peer WRITE loop gave 2572 P7B-BASTNOTIFY and ZERO site-2 entries -- EX ping-pong keeps the node re-acquiring so the release never gets that far), and it needs N independent files (one file reached site 2 in only 3 of 4 runs). The script exits 3 INCONCLUSIVE when the hazard was not built, rather than scoring an absent hazard as a pass.
defects.paired_ab_sess25: SAME BUILD 0.11.207 (A797C0480729E0D96999C88), 2/caw, no re-prep between arms. EXPOSURE IDENTICAL: P28-DRAINSITE2 21 vs 21, dirty=1 17 vs 16, P28-DRAINHOLD 17 vs 16, P47-FILEBLOCK 10 vs 10. OUTCOME OPPOSITE: arm0 (fix off) SYNC_WEDGED with both legs captured from /proc/<pid>/stack byte-identical to the test27 live capture and 1 P73-WAITSTALL and 0 admits; arm1 (fix on) SYNC_OK, 0 P73-WAITSTALL, 2 P25-IOEND-ADMIT src=writepages.
defects.single_event_causal_proof: Writing 1 to /sys/module/mxfs/parameters/fix27_shared_admit UN-WEDGED an already-deadlocked node (the demote-wait re-evaluates mxfs_ilock_admit_ioend every 3s), producing EXACTLY ONE probe line: P25-IOEND-ADMIT ino=132 state=3 g2=5 req=3 src=writepages -- state=3 DEMOTING, g2=5 mirror still EX, req=3 SHARED, i.e. precisely the case FIX-26's EX-only gate cannot cover and FIX-27 can.
defects.fix: mxfs.fix27_shared_admit default flipped 0 -> 1 (v0.11.207). sess24 shipped it off because it 'never engaged' under a healthy workload -- a correct measurement answering the wrong question: those 4380 blocks are stat/cat/md5sum which MUST keep waiting, and not firing under health is what a rare-cycle deadlock breaker is supposed to look like. Also added wake_up_all(&ip->i_dlm_wait) before the site-2 flush so a submitter that parked earlier (captured at state=4 ACQUIRING g2=0, when the admit had to refuse) re-evaluates immediately instead of after up to 3s. That wake ALONE IS NOT THE FIX: arm 0 on the build containing it still wedged with 17 hazards built.
defects.safety: Structural, not merely argued: the admit sets i_dlm_mode=EX when the mirror is EX, and the release pipeline's pre-unlock check treats i_dlm_mode != MXFS_LOCK_NL as `stranded` and SKIPS the wire unlock, so an admitted submitter cannot have the grant released out from under it. The anchored release path is protected by its own gen-anchored unlock returning -ESTALE.
defects.verification: 32/caw on the fix, fresh prep: the SEVEN criteria that read nodes_pass=0/32 during the original test27 wedge all PASS -- cache_coherency 654 checks, strong_consistency, posix_multi, mmap_coherency, zero_silent_loss 644, dlm_fairness, dlm_membership. Plus crash_consistency 32/32 at 64s/90s, rsync_paired 32/32, dir_reuse_coherency 32/32, kernel_health hits=0. 2/caw full regression all PASS.

defects.summary: mxfs_dlm_bast_work_fn's own trailing xfs_irele cascades into inactivation and parks PERMANENTLY in the demote-wait, despite the demoter exemption that exists to cover exactly this
defects.evidence:
ccloop c7ee71c6 sess25, 32/caw on 0.11.207 (A797C0480729E0D96999C88), THREE nodes at once (test7 test8 test13), byte-identical /proc/<pid>/stack, etime 619-839s and MONOTONICALLY CLIMBING on an otherwise QUIESCED cluster:
  mxfs_dlm_ilock_begin+0xf9c <- xfs_ilock+0x198 <- xfs_attr_inactive+0xcd
  <- xfs_inactive+0x59c <- xfs_inode_mark_reclaimable+0x3b0
  <- xfs_fs_destroy_inode+0xf5 <- destroy_inode <- evict <- iput
  <- xfs_irele+0xa6 <- mxfs_dlm_bast_work_fn+0x1a1
The node's own probe names the state, printed every 30s for the whole wedge:
  P73-WAITSTALL ino=31470439 req=5 mode=3 state=3 ex=0 pr=0 pin=0 bast_pend=0 work_busy=2 relflush=1 comm=kworker/u12:9
req=5 EX (xfs_attr_inactive wants ILOCK_EXCL), mode=3 PR held, state=3 DEMOTING, NO holders, and work_busy=2 = the only running bast work IS this worker.
defects.mechanism:
PROVEN by the demoter claim ring (new this session), replayed off a live 32/caw wedge on test16. The ring reads the culprit off directly, no inference:
  P73-DEMEV[8]  SET   line=15980 pid=59368 cookie=446  <- mxfs_dlm_bast_work_fn claims
  P73-DEMEV[9]  SET   line=16280 pid=56068 cookie=449  <- mxfs_dlm_bast_dwork_fn OVERWRITES it
  P73-DEMEV[10] CLEAR line=16292 pid=56068 cookie=450  <- and unconditionally CLEARS it
  P73-DEMEV[11] WAIT  line=25206 pid=59368 cookie=451  <- 59368 parks; demoter_pid=0
i_dlm_demoter was an unqualified single-slot `task_struct *` shared by every release path. The delayed-work drain stored itself over the work drain's LIVE claim and then cleared the slot to NULL. pid 59368's trailing xfs_irele then cascaded into evict -> xfs_inactive -> xfs_attr_inactive -> xfs_ilock, found the slot NULL instead of itself, lost the 'demoter is exempt (it must re-enter during its own drain)' exemption, and parked in the demote-wait forever waiting on a release only it could drive.
defects.detector: node_responsive (tests/suite/node_responsive.sh) -- but ONLY after the sess25 correction below; the pre-sess25 single-sample form could not tell this from ordinary load.
defects.blast_radius: Same as D-BAST-WRITEBACK-ABBA-DEADLOCK: one permanently-stuck kworker holds the inode tenure, so peers wait on a grant that is never released, and any barrier criterion reports NO_TERMINAL_RECORD on ALL ranks. THREE nodes were in this state simultaneously while every other criterion at 32/caw passed, i.e. it is invisible to correctness tests.
defects.blocking_fix: Root WHO clears the demoter. P73-WAITSTALL now prints demoter_pid / demoter_comm / demoter_line / demoter_age_ms / me= (sess25), so the next occurrence names the clobberer instead of requiring inference. Then either make the claim un-clobberable for the duration of the drain (it is a single-slot field shared by bast_work_fn, bast_dwork_fn and the orphan reclaim), or make the inactivation cascade not need the exemption at all.
defects.detector_correction_sess25: node_responsive's D-state check WAS a single instantaneous `ps` snapshot, which measures LOAD not a wedge -- and the script manufactures that load itself (all N ranks mkdir+rmdir into ONE shared mount immediately before sampling). Measured: 20 of 32 nodes FAILed with dstate=1 right after a dirent_durability storm, 3 of 32 still did on a quiesced cluster, and a manual re-sample 25s later found ZERO D-state tasks anywhere. Corrected to sample twice and convict only a task STILL in D state BY PID after a 10s dwell, reporting pid:comm:wchan. This is strictly MORE specific, not a lower bar: an unchanged-PID wedge trivially survives a 10s dwell (this one had been stuck 600s+), while healthy concurrent I/O does not. The corrected check found this defect on its FIRST run.
defects.note_not_the_abba_defect: DISTINCT from D-BAST-WRITEBACK-ABBA-DEADLOCK, which was root-caused, reproduced deterministically and fixed in this same session. That one is drain-blocks-on-folio vs writeback-blocks-on-inode, at drain site 2. This one has no folio in it at all: it is the drain worker's own post-drain reference drop re-entering the inode lock. Both present as 'one node cannot finish, board reads 0/N'.
defects.disposition: FIXED_AND_VERIFIED
defects.hypotheses_refuted_by_measurement: Two candidate clobberers were eliminated BEFORE the ring was built, each by its own probe firing ZERO times on all wedged nodes: (1) the P72 orphan reclaim's 10s 'leaked demoter' override (P72-DEMOTER-OVERRIDE = 0) -- attractive because it is a heuristic that could create the state it claims to detect; (2) the EDEADLK-freeing self-clobber, where the same task does SET_DEMOTER / drain / demoter=NULL and then retries into the demote-wait (P60-EDEADLK-FREEING = 0). Do not re-chase either.
defects.fix: v0.11.210: the claim is now OWNED and NESTABLE. MXFS_SET_DEMOTER claims via cmpxchg only an unowned slot or re-claims its own (depth++), and NEVER overwrites a foreign live claim; MXFS_CLEAR_DEMOTER releases only if current is the owner, and only the outermost nesting level clears. cmpxchg rather than i_dlm_lock because the call sites disagree about whether that spinlock is held, so taking it inside the macro would deadlock some callers. New probe P74-DEMOTER-CONTEST names a refused steal.
defects.verification: sess26 v0.11.223 srcver 1F788B1214DA3B702B8B67A (SHIPPING build). The sess25 single-slot fix was reverted because it regressed crash_consistency (PASS 74s -> FAIL@90s) by denying the second drain its demote-wait exemption. The two-slot revision left by sess25 was UNDEPLOYABLE: mxfs_is_demoter() was infinitely self-recursive (objdump: 'call' to its own entry, no base case) at 16 hot-path sites = kernel stack overflow. Fixed, plus 6 'is a foreign drain live?' sites that still used the one-slot spelling and were blind to a slot-2-only drain (new mxfs_foreign_demoter()). VERIFIED WITH MEASURED EXPOSURE via tests/demoter_claim_census.sh + mxfs.demoter_dump (P75): per 32-node dirent_durability+node_responsive run the second concurrent drain is admitted 30-37 times on 21-23 nodes with contest=0 and foreign_clear=0, i.e. the contended path runs constantly and no claim is ever stolen. NEGATIVE CONTROL on the SAME build (mxfs.demoter_legacy_clobber=1): legacy_steal=30, legacy_clear_live=19 -- the theft genuinely occurs pre-fix and is impossible post-fix. crash_consistency PASS 61s/90s (regression gone), dirent_durability + node_responsive PASS 32/32 dstate=0. Re-taken on the shipping build across a full 32/caw board pass: slot2=152 second-drain admissions on ALL 32 nodes, contest=0, foreign_clear=0. Board green with no regression: precond_readiness, cache_coherency 654/654 26s, strong_consistency 4s, posix_multi 80/80, mmap_coherency 35/35, zero_silent_loss 644/644, dlm_fairness, dlm_membership, crash_consistency 204/204 66s/90s, dir_reuse_coherency 72/72 110s, dirent_durability durable_loss=0, node_responsive dstate=0, kernel_health hits=0 -- all PASS 32/32. NOTE a self-inflicted regression was caught and fixed en route: the first cut of mxfs_foreign_demoter() dropped the original predicate's self-exemption for the case 'slot 1 foreign, slot 2 == me', so a live drain abandoned its own reload. Cost: cache_coherency 0/32 (60s timeout, from 25s passing), strong_consistency 25/32, posix_multi 1/32. The predicate now checks self-ownership FIRST.
defects.related: ccloop 703f15c3 fixed a DIFFERENT bug with this SAME stack (clearing the claim before the trailing irele) and its handoff warned the fix 'may be necessary-but-not-sufficient'. This was that second bug. GPT (RULE 5) independently ranked cross-path claim corruption as the leading hypothesis and recommended exactly the cookie/ring instrument that proved it.
defects.residual_structural_note: NOT closed by this fix and worth a future pass: two release drains still run CONCURRENTLY on one inode (72 contests in one run) -- the fix makes that survivable rather than impossible. GPT's structural recommendation stands: the potentially-final xfs_irele should be handed to a worker holding no DLM state, after the release pipeline completes and state has left DEMOTING, instead of being performed by the release executor itself. Also note `xfs_irele(ip)` followed by touching `ip` is a lifetime hazard in its own right.
defects.REGRESSION_AND_REVISION_sess25:
STATUS REVERTED FROM RESOLVED, self-caught. The v0.11.210 fix (single un-stealable claim slot) eliminated the wedge but introduced a RULE 0 PACE REGRESSION, proven by a same-build A/B using the negative control mxfs.demoter_legacy_clobber, back to back on one fresh prep at 32/caw:
  demoter_legacy_clobber=1 (pre-fix claim): crash_consistency PASS 32/32  [74s/90s]
  demoter_legacy_clobber=0 (v0.11.210 fix): crash_consistency FAIL  0/32  [90s/90s] NO_TERMINAL_RECORD
CAUSE: refusing a foreign claim protects the owner, but the refused claimant STILL RUNS ITS DRAIN, now without the demote-wait exemption, so every nested xfs_ilock it takes parks for the 3s poll.
MY EARLIER REFUTATION OF THIS WAS WRONG AND THE REASON MATTERS: I dismissed it because P73-WAITSTALL read 0. P73 only prints every 10th wait (~30s), so it STRUCTURALLY CANNOT SEE individual 3s stalls. A probe that cannot detect the effect is not evidence of its absence.
REVISED FIX (v0.11.215): TWO claim slots (i_dlm_demoter + i_dlm_demoter2) with a shared mxfs_is_demoter(ip) exemption test. Two concurrent drains on one inode is the measured reality (72 P74-DEMOTER-CONTEST in one 32-node run, bast_work_fn vs bast_dwork_fn), so BOTH stay exempt -- no stall -- while each clears only its OWN slot, so neither can strand the other. The 14 '!=' and 2 '==' exemption comparisons in xfs_mxfs_dlm.c plus the reads in pal/linux/xfs_aops.c were routed through the helper. Also converted xfs_inode.c's raw `i_dlm_demoter = current` / `= NULL` pair (inactivation upgrade path) to the new exported mxfs_dlm_claim_demoter/mxfs_dlm_release_demoter helpers -- it was a third instance of the exact clobber shape, bypassing the macros entirely.
NOT YET RE-VERIFIED. Required before this may return to RESOLVED, all on v0.11.215+:
  (a) crash_consistency PASS at 32/caw on a FRESH prep (the regression gate);
  (b) the wedge reproducer still clean (dirent_durability + node_responsive 32/32);
  (c) P74-DEMOTER-CONTEST should now be RARE — with two slots, a contest means THREE concurrent       drains on one inode, which is itself worth investigating if it occurs.
defects.residual: Two release drains still run concurrently on one inode; the fix makes that survivable, not impossible. contest=0 across every run measured, so two slots suffice for observed workloads -- but a THIRD concurrent drain would be refused a slot and would lose its exemption. contest>0 in the census is the standing alarm for that. Separately measured: the wedge SYMPTOM needs three conditions, not one -- (a) no claim at the trailing irele, (b) i_count==1 so it cascades into inactivation, (c) i_dlm_state != NONE so the demote-wait parks. TEST-ONLY mxfs.bast_irele_unclaim_inject forces (a) and fired 646+ times on 4 nodes without wedging, because every i_count==1 sample had state==NONE. A pre-fix arm therefore cannot be expected to reproduce the wedge on demand in this workload; that is why closure rests on the claim-theft census rather than on symptom reproduction.

defects.summary: A node writes the whole 16KB inode CLUSTER to its home location carrying stale images of slots it has no write tenure for
defects.evidence: Captured 32/caw while rooting D-DIRENT-INODE-TYPE-MISMATCH. test30 held ino 10485888 in PR (P71-HOLD mode=3) and its writeback published P170-CLWR 10485888:40755:..6535 -- the PRE-FREE DIRECTORY image -- at realns 1785413079984065412, 2.5s AFTER test15 published the correct new REG incarnation 10485888:100644:..3492 at realns 1785413077486480010. A plain-bio read (P207-COHERENT-TRUTH) then showed the platter holding the pre-free image, i.e. a generation older than that inode's own free. Every P170-CLWR line shows the write unit is the whole cluster: 21+ ino:mode:gen triples per write.
defects.mechanism: The PHYSICAL WRITE UNIT is the 16KB inode cluster, but the coherency protocol locks at INODE granularity. So a node writing one slot it does own republishes whatever it has cached for every neighbouring slot in the same cluster, including inodes a peer owns and has since modified or reallocated. Per the RULE-5 GPT consult (ccmemory ccloop-c7ee71c6-sess27-GPT-verdict-publication-authority-and-lru-tenure): protection must be at least as coarse as the physical write unit, and a compare-and-write used only to manipulate the DLM record does not fence a subsequent ordinary metadata write. Checking ownership only at dirty/queue time is also insufficient -- already-submitted I/O must be drained before an EX downgrade, since an in-flight write can land after another node's commit.
defects.relationship_to_typeflip_fix: mxfs.typeflip_skip_same_incarn (sess27, RESOLVED D-DIRENT-INODE-TYPE-MISMATCH) removes the mechanism that made this node RETAIN a dead incarnation to publish. It does NOT establish write authority, so the class of defect -- publishing an image the node has no tenure for -- remains. GPT's verdict was explicit: keep the equality fix, but classify this separately and deeper.
defects.detector: BUILT sess29 (0.11.253). Site: pal/linux/xfs_buf.c, the held-non-dir branch of the per-slot masking loop -- the `continue` commented 'held non-dir inode -> write it'. That branch is THE GAP: FREE and NL slots are skipped, and a DIRECTORY slot is never written unless logged this round (P56-CORESIDENT-DIR-SKIP), but a non-dir slot is written unconditionally from whatever the cached cluster buffer holds. Probes: P218-CLUSTER-PASSENGER (per slot), P218-CLUSTER-AUTHORITY (per write, carries the denominator), P218-CLUSTER-AUTHORITY-TOTAL via `echo 1 > /sys/module/mxfs/parameters/cluster_authority_dump`. Census: tests/cluster_authority_census.sh. Detection only -- no knob, no behaviour change.
defects.blocking_fix: One of: cluster-block exclusive ownership; validated read/merge/write under a block lock; or storage compare-and-write over the actual block plus an expected block version. Plus the ordering rules: dirty only while owning the write tenure, drain in-flight I/O before downgrade, and make every publication carry its incarnation + content epoch so a stale publication FAILS rather than overwrites.
defects.detector_design_sess27: NOT BUILT YET -- design plus the primitives that already exist, so the next session does not re-derive them.  SITE: pal/linux/xfs_buf.c ~8223, the P170-CLWR block, which already walks every dinode slot of the cluster buffer being submitted (b_ops == &xfs_inode_buf_ops).  PRIMITIVES: (1) mxfs_v5_dlm_inode_held_nb(dlm, ino) is a NON-BLOCKING held-query already used from a context holding pag_ici_lock (see xfs_buf.c ~3349) -- usable per slot here.  (2) struct xfs_buf has b_mxfs_grant_gen (xfs_buf.h:283), 'the owning dir inode's i_dlm_cached_grant_gen at the last COHERENT read of this block; 0 = never stamped', built for exactly this freshness question but currently only for DIR blocks.  (3) P56-CORESIDENT-DIR-SKIP already masks un-logged DIRECTORY slots out of a cluster write ('dir slot not logged this round; skip') -- precedent for the masking approach AND evidence that the general (non-directory) case is unguarded.  THE COUNTING TRAP: do NOT simply count slots the node does not hold EX for.  Roughly 20 of the 21 slots in every cluster write are bytes preserved from whenever the buffer was last read, so that predicate fires on essentially every write and measures nothing.  The meaningful condition is a slot whose bytes could be STALE: the buffer was last read under an OLDER grant than the current one for that slot's inode (the b_mxfs_grant_gen question, generalised from dir blocks to inode clusters), or this node holds an in-core inode for the slot that it has no write tenure for.  Establish the denominator before believing any numerator -- see the sess27 lesson about P208 having to be knob-independent to make an A/B interpretable.

first_measurement_sess29.reading: unlogged_written is the DENOMINATOR and is not itself a defect (ordinary preserved bytes; ~20 of 21 slots qualify on every write -- the sess27 counting trap). no_write_tenure=2970 IS the defect statement verbatim: this node published those slots' bytes while holding them only in PR, i.e. with no write authority. no_incore=68277 is the class P56's directory rationale calls the worst case -- the flushing node holds the cluster cached for a churned child while the slot's own inode is not in core at all, so the bytes are a stale prior-tenure image and no tenure can even be consulted. Writer is xfsaild in every sample.
first_measurement_sess29.honest_limit: The detector measures AUTHORITY, not DIVERGENCE. It proves the node had no write tenure for those bytes; it does NOT prove each one differed from the platter (rewriting identical bytes is harmless). The next step is to pair a nonzero numerator with a plain-bio platter read (the P207-COHERENT-TRUTH primitive) so divergence is measured, not assumed.

divergence_proven_sess29.method: Cross-node timeline merge. P170-CLWR carries every slot of every inode-cluster write as ino:mode:gen-tail:changecount-tail with a CLOCK_REALTIME realns; P218-CLUSTER-PASSENGER names the slots a node wrote WITHOUT write tenure. For each passenger, find the last publish of that ino by a DIFFERENT node at least skew_ms earlier and compare. di_changecount is monotone per incarnation, so the merge catches a revert WITHIN an incarnation as well as an incarnation revert -- the first version compared mode+gen only and reported DIVERGENT=0 on 2130 passengers, which was true but blind to the common case.
divergence_proven_sess29.result: 2308 passenger writes, 2306 comparable, 0 blind, DIVERGENT=6. Every one the same shape: a peer published the inode as mode=0 (FREED), and 3.9-4.1 SECONDS later this node published a pre-free mode=100644 image of it with a different generation, from its cached cluster buffer, holding no write tenure. Gap is ~78x the 50ms skew guard, so clock skew cannot manufacture it.
divergence_proven_sess29.why_it_matters: The run that produced this had dir_reuse_coherency PASS 32/32 and dirent_durability PASS 32/32. The corruption is SILENT to the current criteria. sess29_fix.bug_in_the_fix_found_by_gpt_review: nskip counted only the OLD skip rules, so a buffer whose only skips were AUTHORITY skips hit `if (nskip == 0) return false` -- which tells the caller 'not a partial write' and sends the WHOLE buffer, every unauthorised passenger included. The mask was computed and thrown away. The per-slot probe stamped skipped= from the mask at consideration time, so it reported INTENT not OUTCOME and the A/B's '2241 dropped' was an overstatement: after the fix (nskip == 0 && n_pr_skip == 0) the same workload drops 6187, ~2.8x more. sess29_fix.declined_fallback_replaced: GPT item 1 DONE. The mask is now ALWAYS applied; an empty result is left empty and resolved by obligation state, per GPT's split. empty + nothing owed -> refuse the write outright and complete the buffer with no I/O (P218-WRITE-REFUSED); the no-obligation proof is (logged|bli_dirty)==0, and since `logged` is every inode log item attached to THIS buffer, that PROVES completion cannot satisfy an unsent item. empty + an obligation -> keep the whole write so a committed change is not lost, and shout (P218-SKIP-DECLINED). Measured over a 32-node board: skipped=158218, refused=0, declined=1 occurrence.

defects.why_still_open: Verified at 8/caw and 32/caw. Held OPEN pending the two honest limits stated below, not for lack of node-count coverage. (1) The merge can only judge a passenger that has a prior PEER publish of the same inode inside the max-gap window -- 2 of 2242 at 32 nodes and 2 of 1446 at 8 nodes had none, so a small unjudgeable remainder exists in every run. (2) The fix establishes safety by NOT WRITING bytes it does not own, rather than by acquiring authority over the physical write unit. That is exactly what the pre-existing directory skip already does, and no lost write has been observed (logged and buf-logged slots are never skipped, and `declined` measured 0), but the deeper repair -- write authority at least as coarse as the write unit -- is still the stated blocking_fix and D-RELEASE-BARRIER-OPEN needs it too.
gpt_remaining_work_sess29: 1. REMOVE the `declined` fallback: it reinstates skipped slots when the mask would empty the write -- 'nothing legal to write, so write the illegal bytes'. dirty==0 after the mask implies no logged items and no bli_dirty, so refusing loses nothing, and the helper already owns submission (return true = 'I submitted it').

2. LOGGED SLOTS NEED AN AUTHORITY CHECK. 'Logged this round' proves a JOURNAL representation, not authority to publish to HOME. With D-RELEASE-BARRIER-OPEN: A logs X, releases, B publishes X, A then writes its logged image over B. The DIRECTORY case is already guarded (P56-NL-LOGGED-DIR-SKIP); non-dir is the same asymmetry one level up.

3. Verify storage-granule alignment / lower-layer RMW safety. Per-inode v5 CRCs detect torn images but do NOT make concurrent sub-block writes safe (512-byte inode writes to a 4Kn device are not independent).

4. Audit EVERY path that publishes an inode-cluster buffer -- log recovery, inode alloc/free, reclaim, unmount flush, error/retry. A recovery path that reconstructs one inode and writes the whole cached cluster reproduces this defect.
5. Split-I/O error handling: one flush becoming several range writes -- decide what stays in the AIL when one range fails.
6. STALE-READ MIRROR: skipped bytes remain in the local cached buffer; a later DLM acquisition must not consume them as authoritative without reload, or a stale-write bug becomes a stale-read bug.
defects.lost_write_safety: STRUCTURAL, not observational: `logged` is built by walking bp->b_li_list -- every inode log item attached to THIS BUFFER -- and a logged or buf-logged slot is never skipped. So a skipped slot provably has no log item for the buffer's iodone to complete; no AIL item is wrongly removed and no dirty state wrongly cleared.

new_finding_sess29_declined.what_it_is: A cluster write where the authority mask empties the write but an obligation exists: ONE logged slot (sector 14) plus 14 unauthorised passengers. dirty==0 means that logged slot is itself inside `skip` -- almost certainly P56-NL-LOGGED-DIR-SKIP, which deliberately refuses to publish a logged DIRECTORY slot sitting at NL without a RELFLUSH token. So every slot in the buffer is unpublishable, and the pre-existing code whole-writes ALL of them: the dir slot it just decided not to publish AND every unauthorised passenger. This is 'we owe bytes we do not own', exactly the hole GPT named in item 2, seen from the other side.
new_finding_sess29_declined.the_refinement_identified: APPLIED and VALIDATED in 0.11.260. The refusal test is now ((logged|bli_dirty) & ~skip) == 0 -- 'nothing we both OWE and were going to WRITE'. Verified safe by reading the sess19/sess20 chain at P56-NL-LOGGED-DIR-SKIP: discharging a skipped logged item without its bytes landing is the EXISTING shipped contract for this buffer (i_mxfs_pub_flush_seq is rolled back so the completion's discharge is a no-op, and MXFS_IF_PUB_SKIPPED re-arms it), so refusing adds no new hazard. The old fallback was actively WRONG here: it whole-wrote the very prior-tenure dir slot P56 had just refused to publish, with the ledger already recording that it had not been published. Measured on 32/caw: slots_skipped=71255 writes_refused=18 declined=0 -- the declined branch is now provably unreachable (an owed sector outside `skip` would have to be in `pr_skip`, and pr_skip never takes a logged or buf-logged slot), and it is retained as an assertion. Correctness green: cache_coherency 654/654, dir_reuse_coherency 32/32, dirent_durability 32/32.
new_finding_sess29_declined.rate: 1 occurrence per 32-node board run; loud and always-on, so it cannot regress silently.

sess30_logged_class.detector: P219-LOGGED-NO-AUTHORITY (pal/linux/xfs_buf.c, at the write path of the logged branch, immediately before its trailing `continue`). Counters via `echo 1 > /sys/module/mxfs/parameters/cluster_authority_dump` -> P219-LOGGED-AUTHORITY-TOTAL written/staged/noauth/noauth_dir/stale_tenure/nocore.
sess30_logged_class.primitive: STAGING TENURE STAMP. xfs_iflush stamps i_mxfs_pub_stage_epoch = i_dlm_epoch, i_mxfs_pub_stage_mode, i_mxfs_pub_stage_ns at copy-in (success path only). The cluster-write site compares stage_epoch to the live epoch. i_dlm_epoch is bumped on every grant loss / stale mark, so a mismatch means the tenure that authorized these bytes ENDED before they were published. One 64-bit compare -- no DLM query, no I/O, safe under pag_ici_lock (sess20: the blocking held-query sleeps there).
sess30_logged_class.staged_gate: The comparison is gated on (logged & slotbits), i.e. an inode log item for this slot attached to THIS buffer -- verified: `logged` is built by walking bp->b_li_list. That gate also makes it structurally immune to inode RECYCLING, since a flush-locked inode with an item on a live buffer cannot be reclaimed.
sess30_logged_class.instrument_bug_found_and_fixed: xfs_inode_alloc uses kmem_cache_alloc, NOT zalloc, so a recycled xfs_inode carries any field the mxfs init does not clear. The FIRST measurement read stage_epoch=2 now_epoch=1 on 18 of 22 hits -- an epoch that went DOWN, which a monotonic counter cannot do. Those were recycled inodes whose i_dlm_epoch had been re-initialised to 1 while the stale stamp survived. Fixed by resetting i_mxfs_pub_stage_* in the mxfs inode init. defects.summary: readdir of a directory a peer created costs ~1.2 s per directory; every other syscall on the same inode costs milliseconds
defects.evidence: MEASURED 32/caw, build 0.11.243 C3D864E1F8AB80753D23D6C, tests/shared_unlink_pace.sh. 32 empty directories in one shared parent, each created by a different node which still holds it cached; then one pass from test1, one syscall class per fresh tree so nothing is confounded: stat 133 ms total (4 ms/op) | open(O_RDONLY|O_DIRECTORY) 1463 ms (45 ms/op) | rmdir 3846 ms (120 ms/op) | opendir+getdents (`ls -f`) 39701 ms (1240 ms/op). Independently reproduced standalone: 32 dirs, readdir-only pass = 37495 ms (1172 ms/op). CONTROL: the identical 32 children created LOCALLY by the same node and removed by it = 152 ms total (4 ms/op) -- so the shared parent is not the bottleneck and neither is the removal. RULE 0: native XFS readdir of an empty directory is microseconds; this is ~10^5x over the ceiling.
defects.mechanism: ROOT PROVEN (RULE 4 step 2b), build 0.11.245 6764F19681F7272375144DA. xfs/xfs_dir2_readdir.c:1005 -- `for (p48_try = 0; p48_try < 200 && dp->i_dlm_stale && !shutdown; p48_try++) { msleep(1); dp->i_dlm_stale = true; mxfs_dlm_reload_inode(dp, ..., true); }`. 200 x msleep(1) is ~1.2 s at this kernel's timer granularity, which is EXACTLY the observed cost and explains its stability (1201-1215 ms on every sample: the loop always runs its full bound). IT CAN NEVER SUCCEED ON THIS PATH: xfs_readdir holds ILOCK_SHARED across iteration, so the reload's write acquire is blocked by THIS task -- sess14 proved that and made mxfs_dlm_reload_inode bail immediately with P173-RELOAD-SELFREAD. It returns with i_dlm_stale still set, and the loop body re-arms the flag before each attempt, so all 200 rounds bail. P173 was the top probe in the capture (110 lines over 32 dirs = the ratelimited count of 200/dir). The loop's own comment ("ILOCK holds here are sub-ms so waiting is safe") is about OTHER holders; it does not cover the caller being the blocker, which is the case that actually occurs. SUPPORTING MEASUREMENTS: a phase-split probe on P62 showed mxfs_dlm_reload_inode itself costs tot_ms=0/pre_ms=0/bp_ms=0, so the cost is the sleeping, not the reload. Timed per syscall from python (a real open, not bash's `exec 9<` which returns EISDIR on a directory and made an earlier 45 ms 'open' row meaningless): stat=4ms open=0ms getdents=1202ms close=0ms. REFUTED en route: the pre-readdir wait loop at pal/linux/xfs_file.c:1888 -- its probe P95D-READDIR-WAIT is present in the module (strings) and fired ZERO times.
defects.detector: tests/shared_unlink_pace.sh (~60 s at 32 nodes, no aging needed) -- its phase C prints the four syscall classes side by side and FAILs over a 2x-native ceiling. Also visible as sustained_load's setup phase after tests/suite/sustained_load.sh gained phase timers this session (rmrf=38379 ms of a 38402 ms setup).
defects.blocking_fix: unknown. The shape suggests readdir needs a reload path that can run WITHOUT the caller's ILOCK_SHARED (revalidate before taking the read lock, the way i_mxfs_rd_vgg's 'validate once per grant episode' design intends) rather than one that is structurally guaranteed to bail. Do NOT simply widen the P173 spin: sess14 measured that as a guaranteed livelock for long readers and 350 CPU-seconds per lap.
attempted_and_refuted: FIRST ATTRIBUTION WAS WRONG, and the correction is the method lesson. A batch `rm -rf` of the same 32 peer-created dirs measured 38344 ms and I recorded it as ~1.2 s per REMOVAL. Replacing the batch with an explicit per-op rmdir loop over the identical shape gave 993-1052 ms TOTAL (31 ms/op) -- a 37x difference for the same removals. The 1.2 s belongs to the readdir that `rm -rf` performs on each child, not to the unlink. Never attribute a batch wall to the operation the batch is named after; split it per syscall.
Peer-side release latency: REFUTED, drain_ms = 0,0,1 on the creators.
Requester poll quantization: REFUTED by construction, MXFS_CAW_POLL_MAX_MS = 25 ms and the inode fastpoll window is 2 ms for the first 64 ms.
defects.sess28_TIMELINE_NARROWED_TO_PARENT_RELOA: NARROWED FURTHER by an inter-probe delta timeline on the reader (dmesg timestamps, scoped to a fresh marker, 3 children under one shared parent, ~1210 ms per `ls -f` child). THE COST IS NOT ON THE CHILD. Each readdir of a CHILD triggers TWO reloads of the SHARED PARENT (ino 2461, size=36, disk=[n3 n4 n2]), ~600 ms apart, and EVERY ONE IS A NO-OP: 'P62-RELOAD-FORK-SHRINK incore_fmt=1 incore_nx=0 incore_size=36 disk_fmt=1 disk_nx=0 disk_size=36 shrink=0' followed immediately by 'P-RELOAD-IDENTICAL cc=5 gen=1236381809 -- disk == in-core, keeping loaded fork (no destroy/adopt)' and 'P56-RELOAD-MERGE merged=0 clean=1 disk=[n3 n4 n2] ours=[n3 n4 n2]'. Measured gap 48453.955377 -> 48454.561680 = 606 ms between two identical parent reloads that both found nothing. The CHILD's own reload lands 2 ms later. Immediately before each one, P173-RELOAD-SELFREAD fires ~3 times at 3 ms intervals (rd_last=xfs_file_readdir, comm=bash) and bails. THE SUSPECTED LOOP: xfs_dir2_readdir's grant-episode gate (rd_gg != dp->i_mxfs_rd_vgg, xfs_dir2_readdir.c:914) triggers a reload; if the reload BAILS, i_mxfs_rd_vgg is deliberately NOT latched (xfs_dir2_readdir.c:1074) so the trigger re-fires on the next access -- and with 32 peers touching the shared parent, rd_gg keeps moving, so the parent is reloaded again and again, each time discovering it is identical. THE ONE MEASUREMENT THAT CLOSES IT: bracket mxfs_dlm_reload_inode with entry/exit timestamps and split the ~600 ms into (a) the coherent grant/verify, (b) the FUA dinode read, (c) the fork rebuild. 600 ms is far too long for a 16 KB FUA read, so the prime suspect is a grant round trip on the hot shared parent -- which would also tie this defect to D-32NODE-SHARED-DIR-CREATE-PACE. Secondary: count reloads per readdir syscall and confirm the no-op repeat is unbounded rather than 2.

defects.summary: CAW yield_to deference starves compatible fresh acquires; retry-budget exhaustion returns -ETIMEDOUT and mxfs_dlm_ilock_begin force-shuts-down the FS — 10 of 32 nodes committed simultaneous voluntary shutdown under dirent_durability
defects.evidence: sess31 (ccloop c7ee71c6), build 0.11.267 srcversion 54BE75FB3219A5A723884FB, QUIET host (load 13/56 cores, NVMe <10%util): run 20260731T042501Z dirent_durability 32/caw FAIL. 10 nodes (test3,5,7,11,20,22,23,25,27,29) each: 'DLM inode lock unrecoverable: ino=139 mode=3(PR) rc=-110 comm=mkdir' within 1.8s (04:28:08.569-04:28:10.337Z). Uniform P-CAWEXH: req=3 our_mode=0 yield_bo=100(or 99) ea_claim=0 ea_compat=0 ea_regwait=0 last_hex=0 last_hpr=0x2088082d. 20/32 nodes logged >=1 full 100-retry exhaustion; every node with 3 consecutive died (P34-ACQ-SLOW attempts=4 dur_ms=7577 rc=-110). Evidence dir: tests/evidence/sess31_dd_shutdown_043430/ (full dmesg all 32 nodes + btime).
defects.mechanism: dlm_caw.c acquire loop: a mode-COMPATIBLE fresh acquire (our_mode=NL) that finds yield_to nonzero and not naming it sleeps and retries (yield_bo path, dlm_caw.c~3392) WITHOUT ever CAS-registering into slot->waiters (registration happens only on the INCOMPATIBLE path ~3619). Releases rebuild the batch ticket as yield_to = cur_slot->waiters (~3971), so the deferrer is invisible to the rotation it defers to; under continuous handoff (~13 rel/s on shared parent ino=139: 32-node mkdir+readdir storm) the ticket never empties and never names it. 100 retries x ~25ms = 2.6s per acquire attempt, x4 ilock_begin attempts = 7.6s, then rc=-ETIMEDOUT which ilock_begin punishes with xfs_force_shutdown (policy: proceeding without grant = uncoordinated metadata corruption). Same rc=-110 signature class as the PREVIOUSLY fixed sess130 (conversion priority) and v0.10.41 (upgrader-yields-to-PR-batch) carve-outs; the fresh-acquire case was never covered.
defects.notes: FIX SHIPPED 0.11.269 (GPT-reviewed option C): (A) mxfs.caw_fresh_register=1 — compatible-yield fresh INODE acquires CAS-register their waiter bit so release tickets (yield_to=waiters) include them; claim CAS clears waiter bits + recomputes waiter_mode atomically (UNCONDITIONAL — also drains pre-existing ghost waiter bits). (B) mxfs.caw_fresh_yield_bound=16 — a registered fresh acquire stops deferring after 16 consecutive yield-only laps and takes the compatible claim (P221-YIELD-BOUND). Verification: pre-fix 3 collapses in 4 same-day sequences; post-fix 5/5 dirent_durability PASS 65-66s, 0 exhaustions (scoped grep P-CAWEXH yreg=), 0 shutdowns, pace unchanged, including at loadavg 22 (worse than the failing era). STILL OPEN: terminal-event paired A/B incomplete — the regime is contention-marginal and did not reproduce post-fix even in control arm (register=0), partly because the unconditional ghost-clear is active in both arms. Complete opportunistically with tests/ysr_dd_ab.sh when the rig next enters the failing regime; tests/yield_starvation_repro.sh is the synthetic (needs barrier-aligned waves to bite). Sess31 note: ccloop-c7ee71c6-sess31-ROOT-FIXED-caw-yield-starvation-shutdown.
defects.disposition: FIXED AND VERIFIED (sess36, GPT-ruled). Cause proven sess31 (yield_to deference excluded compatible fresh acquires from release tickets -> 100-retry exhaustion -> ilock_begin forced shutdown; 10-node simultaneous collapse captured). Composite patch 0.11.269 targets the mechanism: fresh-acquire CAS waiter registration, atomic claim-CAS waiter-bit clear + waiter_mode recompute (drains ghost bits), 16-lap yield bound (P221 tracer). Exercised clean since: 5/5 collapse-workload passes at ship, every board green, sess36 +9 aged laps at 2/8 nodes + 32 board with P-CAWEXH=0 on every node; mechanism ENGAGEMENT observed sess36 (P221-YIELD-BOUND fired on test6 — the starvation condition arose, the bound broke it, no exhaustion followed). Paired A/B WAIVED for closure (GPT ruling): the control arm cannot isolate the variable without reverting the foundational claim-CAS change active in both arms — sub-change attribution is optional engineering analysis, not a FIXED AND VERIFIED gate.

defects.summary: crash_consistency cold-read verify: 5/32 observer nodes read IDENTICAL STALE content for two peer-rewritten files (md5 split vs the 27 correct readers) despite sync+drop_caches — a cross-node stale-read coherency failure, cross_write_read family.
defects.evidence: 0.11.292 knob=0 (shipped config), 32/caw, run_id 20260731T131837Z. 5/32 nodes FAILed their durable check: node5_f1 exp=2b88b319... got=38c22ec5... (identical wrong value seen by observers in r2,r3,r4,r5) and node6_f1 exp=175003ea... got=510bde72... (r3,r4,r5,r6). Same got-value across independent observers and rounds = the on-LUN content settled to a stable OLD image, not a torn/flapping read. Extracts: tests/logs/sess33_crash_md5_mismatch/ (all_results.txt, failing_checks.txt, pr_fail_counts.txt); full 3.8G run dir preserved this boot at /tmp/run_crash_consistency_20260731T131837Z (and scratchpad bulk_crash_run). CORRECTED INTERPRETATION (harness read, sess33): crash_consistency KILLS NO NODES (kill coverage lives in the separate real-kill harness); it is write+fsync -> barrier -> drop_caches -> every node cold-verifies every file. 'cc rN' = RANK N (the observer), not a round. So the five FAILing results are observers rank2..rank6 each reading the SAME wrong md5 for node5_f1 (got=38c22ec5) and node6_f1 (got=510bde72) while rank1 and ranks7-32 read the correct fresh values. The test dir persists across laps and files are truncate+rewritten each lap, so got= is almost certainly the PREVIOUS lap's content: a stale extent map / stale cached pages surviving the coherency protocol on exactly those 5 nodes. NOT an on-platter rollback (27 nodes read fresh).
defects.environment_caveats: Host loadavg ~35 during the lap (external game-server burst) — but a wrong md5 is not manufacturable by load; load may have widened the producing race. Multiple nodes logged 'sd 4:0:0:0: PR command failed: 2' during the kill cycles (SCSI persistent-reservation/fence failures under load); test15 also logged P13-SFPARENT-DURABLE-FAIL ino=128 and DLM rc=-35 storms in the window.
mechanism_candidates: 0. COLD-IGET-LAGGING-HOME (now primary): the fs was FRESH this boot — node5_f1 had no prior incarnation, so got= cannot be a previous lap's f1. The 5 observers cold-igot node5_f1's dinode from the LUN while its IN-PLACE image lagged its journal commit (oflag=sync makes data+journal durable, not the home dinode); a lagging dinode = old size/extents = reads of recycled-daddr bytes with a stable wrong checksum. The .md5 companion read fresh on the same nodes (33B file, different path/timing) which is why exp= was correct. The 27 correct readers' PR acquires BASTed the writer and waited out the release drain; the mechanism by which 5 readers bypassed that wait (adjacent ranks 2-6 = a shared window) is the open question — candidates: shared PR grant piggyback where the FIRST reader's drain-wait outcome was consumed pre-landing by the others, or an iget-time read that precedes the DLM acquire entirely.

1. STALE EXTENT MAP: the observers cached node5_f1's inode/extents from the PREVIOUS lap; the truncate+rewrite by node5 moved size/extents; the 5 nodes' revalidation (PR acquire + reload / i_mxfs_rd_vgg-style grant-gen gate for files) did not fire -> they read old blocks. The adjacent-rank clustering (2..6) suggests a shared timing window in the barrier.
2. FUA-READ GATE MISS: reads served from target/page cache without the _XBF_FUA_FRESH platter read where the protocol required one (load-35 widened timing).
3. drop_caches-surviving pages: clean pages pinned/referenced surviving echo-3 while the coherency layer assumed cold. (Would still require the stale-map hazard to matter.)

4. PR-failure lines ('sd 4:0:0:0 PR command failed: 2', multiple nodes, in-window) — crash_consistency does not fence, so these come from lease/heartbeat-adjacent PR activity or residue; treat as environmental until correlated.
5. 291/292 regression unlikely (neither touches read/coherency paths) but a 290 paired lap discriminates cheaply.

The rotation math (K=3 reader set) shows the 'five nodes' are EXACTLY the complete remote-reader set of node5_f1/node6_f1: 100% of remote readers were stale for the entire verify (persisting across repeated drop_caches), so the PLATTER dinode itself lagged at the 4096 state throughout. CONVERGENT THEORY: f1 = each rank's OLDEST write -> its EX tenure went quiet during f2..f50 -> MHT-expiry release mid-write-phase should have landed size (sess79 guarantee) and closed the core ledger (relbar obligation=0 held all session) -- both can be true with the platter still lagging if the release's durable pass satisfied itself against the TARGET CACHE (LIO drops write-FUA) and the release-time blkdev_flush failed or was skipped: FUA-readers then honestly read the lagging platter. The in-window 'sd 4:0:0:0: PR command failed: 2' storm marks the SCSI path degrading at exactly that time. defects.sess33_final_timeline_decode: ARCHIVE DECODE (kernlog_test5 13:19:06, the 14-write burst second): (1) dd was STILL WRITING f1 (P2G-LOGWHO flags=0x5 comm=dd mid-burst) — cc=2..4 images in the burst were CURRENT progressive flushes, not stale; (2) 'mxfs_submit_partial_inode_write: 35 callbacks suppressed' — MANY OVERLAPPING partial submits of the SAME 16KB buffer within ~1s (14 P170 prints are the ratelimited subset); (3) neighbor slots progressed across the burst (18876679 cc2->8, 18876680 0->4) — ALL RANKS' f1 files are co-resident in this ONE recycled cluster, which is why every failure landed here; (4) P-CLMERGE restored slot 6 mid-burst; (5) the LAST cluster write is 13:19:06, the release 13:19:13, and the cc=6 state was logged in between or during — with obligation=0 at release. No dual buffer instance required. defects.summary: A bast dwork can fire after per-AG teardown (ident check fails, pag=NULL) while holding the LAST inode ref; the P142 guard then intentionally leaks the ref rather than risk iput of a mid-teardown inode — one leaked mxfs_inode at module unload
defects.evidence: Observed once, 0.11.308, test3, infra-aborted cycle (typeflip harness killed mid-run; two peer nodes umount-busy; fs shutdown mid-teardown): ino=31457413 P6G-REL-STALE (release deferred to dwork) -> P142-DWORK-STALE ip=.. pag=0000000000000000 src=10 i_count=1 -> P142-DWORK-LASTREF 'ref intentionally leaked' -> P202-LEAKED-INODE-AT-UNLOAD icount=1 bast_pending=1 bastq_src=10 dlm_mode=0. The guard's rationale (uninserted pre-insert placeholders must not be iput) is sound for its original class; this instance is a real inserted inode caught by teardown ordering: the dwork outlived pag teardown because the inode's only ref WAS the dwork's own (circular — evict never ran, so the P204 cancel path never engaged).
defects.mechanism: Teardown ordering: unmount/shutdown path tears down per-AG structures while a deferred-release dwork holding the last inode ref is still queued; ident_ok then fails and the last-ref guard chooses leak over UAF.
defects.next_step: (1) Reproduce deliberately: shutdown injection + deferred release + immediate unmount. defects.mechanism_sess385: sess385 ROOT PROVEN, both sides measured, one incident. THE AG RELEASE PATH HAS NO INODE-LOG-ITEM -> HOME-BLOCK CONVERSION STAGE. The two halves of xfs_iunlink reach the medium by DIFFERENT mechanisms: agi_unlinked[bucket] and the victim's di_next_unlinked are BUFFER-logged (covered by the existing drains), but di_nlink=0 from xfs_droplink dirties the INODE LOG ITEM and reaches the cluster buffer only when xfs_iflush runs -- normally from xfsaild, asynchronously. xfs_log_force(SYNC) at release makes it durable in OUR journal, which no peer ever replays because peers read only HOME BLOCKS. So the AGI (the pointer) was published while the dinode (the pointee) still read LINKED. MEASURED at the publication point (probe P86, fires immediately before mxfs_v5_dlm_ag_unlock, FUA-reads each non-null AGI unlinked bucket head off the shared LUN): on ALL-PASS laps, 11 of 65 and later 15 of 72 published heads were bad. FULL CHAIN, one incident: test17 published ag=4 bucket=29 agino=0x82275 ino=17310325 disk_nlink=1 core_nlink=0; 3.2s later test24 logged 'Found unrecovered unlinked inode 0x82275 in AG 0x4' -> P217-RENAME-FAILSITE site=droplink_tgt rc=-117 -> P217-RENAME-DIRTYCANCEL -> 'Corruption of in-memory data (0x8) at xfs_trans_cancel' -> shutdown -> #474A cascade, 10 nodes down. Same AG, same agino, publisher and victim both instrumented. The acquirer is NOT corrupt and the AGI is NOT corrupt -- the transition was published in halves. SECOND, INDEPENDENT DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED en route (HOLE 1): mxfs_dlm_ag_drain_inode_buffers never received the three hardenings the AG-META drain got years ago -- it skipped any buffer with _XBF_DELWRI_Q (the v0.3.31 bug), skipped on a failed trylock instead of waiting (the v0.3.27 bug), and had no pinned/BLI fallthrough (sess77 / 4dd7-sess4). Those mattered MORE here because the normal route by which a dinode reaches its cluster buffer IS xfsaild (xfs_inode_item_push -> xfs_iflush -> xfs_buf_delwri_queue), so the skipped buffer was the COMMON case; and nothing else waited for it, because Phase 3 waits only on pag_dlm_meta_pending, which counts AG-META buffers only. MEASURED before the fix: 34 dirty inode-cluster buffers skipped in one all-PASS lap, 10 of the 23 checkable still differing from in-core at the instant of release -- Architectural Invariant 1 violated on a green board.
defects.fix_sess385: sess385 FIX LANDED 0.19.20 sv 50B07EF2D616706B3733F34, per the RULE-5 ruling (ccmemory ccloop-c7ee71c6-sess385-GPT-ruling-inode-publication-hole), three parts: (A) HOLE 2 / the missing stage: mxfs_dlm_ag_drain_inode_buffers now calls xfs_iflush_cluster(bp) on any inode-cluster buffer with a non-empty b_li_list before writing it. xfs_trans_log_inode attaches every dirty inode's log item to its cluster buffer at first dirty, so b_li_list IS exactly the set needing conversion -- no radix-tree walk. xfs_iflush_cluster is the non-blocking converter (ILOCK_SHARED nowait, skips what it cannot get), which is what keeps this OUT of the whole-AG ail_push deadlock that killed the two previous attempts; skipped inodes are retried by the enclosing pass-until-quiescent loop. Its failure path has already unlocked+released the buffer and shut the fs down, so that path must not touch bp again -- handled. Gated by mxfs.publish_inodes (default 1) for A/B. (B) HOLE 1: the drain now matches the meta drain -- no _XBF_DELWRI_Q skip, blocking xfs_buf_lock, pinned/BLI fallthrough, synchronous xfs_bwrite (which already forces SHUTDOWN_META_IO_ERROR on write failure, so a write we cannot complete can no longer be followed by an unlock that publishes stale metadata -- the fail-closed property xfs_buf_delwri_submit did not have). _XBF_MXFS_ALLOC_QUEUED buffers are left to drain_alloc_buflist per ruling item 2c (ownership asserted by the mxfs flag, never inferred from _XBF_DELWRI_Q). (C) ORDERING, pointee before pointer: drain_alloc_buflist + drain_inode_buffers now run BEFORE the first drain_meta_buffers, with a blkdev flush between, so the AGI is written AFTER the dinodes it points at. The old order published and flushed the pointer first, maximising the crash/forced-takeover window. TRAP FOUND AND FIXED IN THE FIX ITSELF: copying the meta drain's write predicate was wrong. For an AG-META buffer b_li_list carries the buf log item, which iodone releases, so that predicate self-clears; for an INODE cluster buffer b_li_list carries the INODE log items, which SURVIVE the write. The predicate was therefore permanently true -- the drain rewrote the same buffer every pass and hit the pass cap on 133 of 423 releases while the meta drain hit it 0 times (probe P85-LATEPASS: all 423 late writes reported the identical post-write state pin=0 bip=0 inail=0 li_empty=0). Correct predicate is _XBF_DELWRI_Q || pinned || b_log_item, re-evaluated UNDER the buffer lock. After: PASSCAP 141 -> 0, quiesces in 1-2 passes, writes 1095 -> 19 with nothing skipped. sess385 PART D, landed 0.19.20 sv 50B07EF2D616706B3733F34 -- PUBLICATION ENFORCEMENT, closing the residual the RULE-5 ruling flagged. The conversion stage uses xfs_iflush_cluster, which is deliberately NON-blocking (xfs_ilock_nowait) so it cannot re-enter the whole-AG ail_push deadlock; that leaves an inode whose ILOCK is held by another thread unconverted, and if it is still unconverted when the pass-until-quiescent loop hits its cap we would have unlocked and published a split anyway. Invariant 1 and the ruling both say a drain that did not complete must NEVER be followed by an on-disk unlock. So the P86 audit immediately before mxfs_v5_dlm_ag_unlock is now VERIFY -> REPAIR -> RE-VERIFY: for a head whose home dinode reads LINKED, look the inode up in this node's cache; if i_nlink==0 (SPLIT -- we unlinked it, it is ours to fix) retry a TARGETED conversion for that one inode up to mxfs.publish_retries (default 3): log_force(SYNC) -> xfs_imap -> xfs_buf_incore(BLOCKING, INCORE-only) -> xfs_iflush_cluster -> xfs_bwrite -> blkdev_flush -> re-FUA-read. Success logs P87-PUBLISH-REPAIRED. If core_nlink==-1 (BADHEAD) we have NO authority to repair -- most likely another node created that head -- so it is reported (P86-AGI-UNLINKED-BADHEAD) and left alone. A split surviving repair logs P86-AGI-UNLINKED-PUBLISH and, when mxfs.publish_refuse_unlock=1, forces SHUTDOWN_META_IO_ERROR rather than handing a peer metadata that will make it call this AGI corruption. That param DEFAULTS TO 0 (warn only) deliberately: shipping an unmeasured cluster-wide shutdown path would be a RULE 4 violation, and #474 shows what an uncontained shutdown costs. Measure the repair rate first, then flip it. LOCK-ORDER HAZARD FOUND AND FIXED IN SELF-REVIEW BEFORE ANY RIG RUN: the first cut ran the repair while still holding the AGI buffer locked. With flags=0 xfs_imap still falls through to xfs_imap_lookup -- an inobt btree read that reads the AGI -- whenever blocks_per_cluster > 1 AND inoalign_mask == 0, and xfs_log_force can drive an AIL push that also wants the AGI. Either would have self-deadlocked the release worker. The audit now SNAPSHOTS all 64 bucket heads into a local array and DROPS the AGI buffer before doing anything else; nothing can change the list underneath it because we still hold the AG DLM EX and pag_dlm_demoting is set.
