defects.summary: The durable write-authority token ex_grant_epoch is documented and consumed as a uint64 that uniquely names one exclusive tenure, but it is assigned from the uint32 slot generation (dlm/dlm_caw.c:956, the single assignment site in the tree). It is therefore a zero-extended 32-bit CYCLIC token, not a unique identity: after 2^32 successful CASes on a slot the token REPEATS, and at the wrap point generation==0 mints the value the protocol defines as invalid. generation advances on EVERY successful CAS of the slot — waiter registration included, not just grants — so a hot resource reaches wrap far sooner than a count of exclusive tenures would suggest.
defects.mechanism: dlm/dlm_caw.c:956 caw_grant_epoch_update(): `s->ex_grant_epoch = s->generation;` with `uint32_t generation` and `uint64_t ex_grant_epoch`. Two distinct failures: (1) TOKEN REUSE — a crash-recovery replayer validating a logged image by epoch equality can match a record written under an EARLIER tenure that happened to carry the same post-wrap value, and accept a foreign image as authorized; (2) ZERO MINT — at the wrap the granting CAS stamps 0, which caw_grant_result_fill classifies as MXFS_GAUTH_WRITE_ZERO_EPOCH, i.e. the fail-closed 'slot was tombstoned and the namespace restarted' signal. A live, legitimately-granted EX tenure then reports itself as having no authority.
defects.evidence: grep -rn 'ex_grant_epoch *=' --include=*.c --include=*.h over the whole tree returns exactly ONE assignment, dlm/dlm_caw.c:956, inside caw_grant_epoch_update. Field declarations: dlm/dlm_caw.h:274 `uint64_t ex_grant_epoch` vs the slot's `uint32_t generation`. The uniqueness claim the consumers rely on is stated in the sess48 comment at dlm/dlm_caw.c:950-955 ('uniquely names this exclusive acquisition ... new on EVERY reacquire') and in include/mxfs/mxfs_dlm.h:96-121. RULE-5 ruling sess107 (ccmemory ccloop-c7ee71c6-sess107-GPT-ruling-direct-handoff-mint-10-blockers) ruled the current token unsound and the wrap/zero handling release-blocking.
defects.blast_radius: Every consumer of durable write authority: the per-inode install path (xfs/xfs_mxfs_dlm.c, mxfs_grant_result.grant_epoch), the AG token stamped lock-free into every buffer-log record via pag->pag_mxfs_grant_epoch, and the foreign-slice replay gate that D-FOREIGN-REPLAY-UNGATED-IMAGES exists to build. A reused token defeats the gate in the accept direction (false authority); a zero token defeats it in the refuse direction (a legitimate tenure reports none).
defects.next: 1) Replace the epoch SOURCE with a durable per-resource 64-bit sequence minted in the granting CAS (`next = s->ex_grant_epoch + 1; if (next == 0) next = 1;`), which is serialized by the slot C&W and need not equal the CAS generation. 2) MANDATORY companion, or the change regresses: caw_tombstone_slot() currently PRESERVES generation but ZEROES ex_grant_epoch, so a naive +1 sequence RESTARTS at 1 after every tombstone+reclaim of the same resource and reintroduces the exact false match the sess97 zero-rule prevents — the tombstone must PRESERVE ex_grant_epoch alongside dir_epoch/last_ex_slot/open_holders. 3) Audit that replay validates the TUPLE (resource identity, ex_grant_epoch), never a globally unique scalar — independent slots legitimately issue the same numbers. 4) Land with the direct-handoff mint (same helper, same CAS) so the tree has one mint point. 5) Verification must exercise the cause, not just the happy path: drive a single slot's epoch to the wrap boundary (or inject the boundary value) and assert no grant mints 0 and no two live tenures share a token.
defects.residual_note: TRANSFERRED sess174 to D-FOREIGN-REPLAY-UNGATED-IMAGES as the 'historical-record-lifetime' gate blocker (copied verbatim there; scope broadened to all persistent consumers).  Original text: PRE-EXISTING and NOT introduced by either epoch source, recorded here so it is not lost: if resource X's slot is tombstoned, recycled by a DIFFERENT resource, and X is later re-claimed at another slot index, X's epoch namespace restarts from that slot's lineage. Neither the generation source nor a per-slot +1 sequence closes that; only tuple-validation plus a cluster-monotonic component would. Do not treat the +1 change as closing it.
defects.disposition: FIXED AND VERIFIED sess174 (RULE-5 ratified; closure build 0.11.462, srcversion F185ED4495CCC5DCEED0914).  CAUSE (proven sess107/108): the single assignment site copied the uint32 slot generation into the uint64 ex_grant_epoch, making the durable write-authority token a zero-extended cyclic value that repeats after 2^32 slot CASes and mints the fail-closed 0 at the wrap.  FIX: (1) caw_next_grant_epoch (dlm/dlm_caw.c:1102) mints a durable per-resource 64-bit sequence `next = s->ex_grant_epoch + 1; if (!next) next = 1;` serialized by the granting CAS — the epoch source is now independent of generation; (2) caw_tombstone_slot PRESERVES ex_grant_epoch (~dlm_caw.c:1273) so the sequence survives tombstone+reclaim instead of restarting at 1; (3) ONE mint point — caw_grant_epoch_update called at all 5 grant sites (dlm_caw.c 6253/7006/7868/8651/9921); (4) edge-triggered mint (0.11.461, sess169 RULE-5 ruling): mint iff can_write(new) && !can_write(prior from cur_slot), so a PW->EX upgrade does not re-mint mid-tenure; (5) test-only wrap-injection knob caw_inject_gep_wrap for boundary verification.  VERIFIED (exercises the cause): sess172 kernel-hook PW selftest on the 32/caw rig — basic: 1..9 strictly monotonic across 3 runs; wrap: injected prev=~UINT64_MAX -> next tenure mints 1, never 0; kill: t1=1699 -> ~3473, virsh destroy mid-hold, rejoin -> 3474 — the sequence survives node death + purge with no restart. sess174: FULL BOARD 27/27 applicable PASS at 32/caw on 0.11.462, all within RULE-0 budget.  CONSUMER TUPLE AUDIT: the shadow evaluator (xfs/xfs_log_recover.c:2370-2456) validates class+resource(daddr)+owner-slot+incarnation+per-resource-epoch — tuple validation, never a globally-unique scalar; uncapable_match quarantine cites this defect ID.  WRAP POLICY (RULE-5 Q4, sess174): (a) zero-skip prevents minting the fail-closed 0 token but does NOT preserve uniqueness after true 2^64 exhaustion — UINT64_MAX -> 1 can reuse values; the acceptance basis is exhaustion outside any deployment lifetime (1M tenure-starts/s against ONE resource ~= 584,542 years; 10k/s ~= 58.45M years), NOT collision-free wrap.  (b) True 2^64 wrap is NOT empirically verified; it is covered by the lifetime policy plus the injected boundary behavior verified in the selftest.  (c) caw_inject_gep_wrap is test-only and must never become an ordinary production control path.  TRANSFER: the remaining cross-slot resource-lineage restart risk is transferred to D-FOREIGN-REPLAY-UNGATED-IMAGES (#1) as its historical-record-lifetime gate blocker and is NOT claimed fixed by this closure.

defects.summary: The CAW slot records lock requests as ONE BIT PER NODE, but a node can have more than one local acquire attempt outstanding for the same resource. The bit therefore cannot say WHICH local request it represents. An attempt that gives up clears `waiters`/`waiters_ex` (and its giveup-mode holder bit) on behalf of the whole node, destroying the on-disk request of a DIFFERENT, still-live local attempt — and the same ambiguity misdirects direct-handoff nomination, which can only name 'node N'.
defects.mechanism: dlm/dlm_caw.c:2318 caw_drop_own_waiter() CASes `waiters &= ~node_bit; waiters_ex &= ~node_bit;` plus `holders[giveup_mode] &= ~node_bit`, keyed on ctx->node_bit alone — there is no attempt identity anywhere in the slot format or in the call. Three call sites, all post-giveup: grant-wait timeout (dlm_caw.c:3346), claim-exhaustion (4990), convert-exhaustion (6479). Concurrent same-node attempts on ONE resource are possible by design: AG acquires are serialized by pag->pag_dlm_acquire_lock and inode acquires by the MXFS_DLM_ISTATE_ACQUIRING park in mxfs_dlm_ilock_begin (xfs/xfs_mxfs_dlm.c:28138), but the demoter is EXEMPT from that park (!mxfs_is_demoter(ip) at xfs_mxfs_dlm.c:28141 and 28415) because the BAST drain's trailing xfs_irele must self-reenter. The tree already carries the probe P3A-DEMOTER-SLOWACQ (xfs_mxfs_dlm.c:28433) labelled in-source as 'the prime suspect for the same-node concurrent-request collision'.
defects.evidence: 32/caw census on 0.11.440 (tests/census_p.sh, 27 of 32 nodes reporting, sess110 board still in the ring buffer): P3A-DEMOTER-SLOWACQ = 0, P6H-ABORT-RECONCILE = 0, 'disk lock acquisition timed out' = 0, P-CAWEXH = 0, P91-CLAIMEXH = 0 on EVERY node, against ~970 P6H-ADOPT per node. So the reconcile arm is never entered under a healthy board and the collision is unobserved — reachable by construction, not by measurement. RULE 6 forbids closing on rarity. GPT (sess111) named this independently as a defect distinct from the holder-adoption race of blocker 6: 'A single waiter bit cannot represent two concurrent local requests, and reg_gen/reg_epoch do not identify which request a handoff satisfies.'
defects.blast_radius: Liveness and correctness. Clearing a live attempt's waiter bit strands that attempt (it polls for a grant that will never be nominated) until its own timeout, and a leaked-or-destroyed waiter bit is the exact shape of the measured 16-node reader-starvation wedge. Clearing a giveup-mode HOLDER bit that a concurrently adopted live tenure depends on is worse: the peer then mints the next epoch and writes while this node still believes it holds the tenure — dual writer.

See ccmemory ccloop-c7ee71c6-sess113-GPT-ruling-lreq-registry-STOP-SHIP. DO NOT DEPLOY 0.11.441 as it stands. defects.found: Code/design proof from a line-level audit, corroborated by a RULE-5 consult. SHIPPED since sess48 (0.11.398), which replaced a bounded 10-retry loop with this bounded 1000-retry loop.
defects.summary: caw_drop_own_waiter() gives up after 1000 CAS attempts (or on the first hard I/O error, or on a slot read error) and RETURNS NORMALLY. Its callers then return -ETIMEDOUT to the filesystem and the mount continues in normal service with a possibly-leaked waiter or holder bit on the shared LUN. A leaked EX waiter bit has ALREADY caused a measured cluster-wide wedge, so silent exhaustion cannot be treated as successful cleanup.
defects.mechanism: dlm/dlm_caw.c:2318 caw_drop_own_waiter(): `for (attempt = 0; attempt < 1000; attempt++)` with backoff capped at 8 ms; `break` on read error, on magic mismatch, on any non-EAGAIN caw_slot() error, and on loop exhaustion. The function is `void` — no caller can tell cleanup succeeded from cleanup abandoned. The in-source comment argues the loop is 'generously bounded so a genuinely wedged slot cannot pin this thread', which trades a thread stall for an unbounded cluster-wide liveness hazard without saying so.
defects.evidence: The sess48 comment block on the same function records the failure this loop exists to prevent: a 16-node barrier-directory wedge where the slot froze at waiter_mode=EX with two orphaned EX waiter bits, every blocked thread across all 16 nodes was a SHARED reader, no thread anywhere was requesting EX, defer_for_waiter starved all readers, cluster phase >600s, posix_semantics_multi16 FAIL. 32/caw census on 0.11.440: the reconcile arm was not entered at all (see D-SAMENODE-WAITER-CANCEL-COLLISION), so exhaustion is unobserved.
defects.blast_radius: Cluster-wide liveness. One orphaned EX waiter bit on a hot shared resource starves every reader on every node via defer_for_waiter.
defects.next: sess112 landed -EBUSY + P245-RECONCILE-EXHAUST + requeue-as-owed on 0.11.441.  sess113 RULE-5: THAT IS NOT ESCALATION and does not satisfy the requirement.  'A warning, counter and owed flag are not sufficient escalation': the deferred path ignores caw_drop_own_waiter's return value, passes e=NULL so a retry failure is not re-recorded at all, and lreq_gc can then delete the only evidence that cleanup failed.  Even with e passed, re-recording debt does not GUARANTEE another retry -- if no future local attempt on that resource ever finishes, the debt is never retried, and a leaked EX-waiter bit is the measured 16-node >600s wedge.  NEXT: a guaranteed mechanism -- a persistent reconciliation worker with a bounded retry policy, refusal of further acquisition of that (node,resource) while unresolved (poisoned state), and escalation to withdrawal/fencing if safety-critical cleanup cannot be confirmed.  Also: checked counter arithmetic (attempts/writers/tenure/pin overflow -- an attempts wrap makes live users look quiescent and AUTHORIZES the cleanup), BUILD_BUG_ON(MXFS_LOCK_MODE_COUNT <= 32) before using a u32 mode mask, and treat `if (e->attempts) e->attempts--;` underflow as an invariant violation rather than silently absorbing it.

defects.found: Code/design proof from a line-level audit, corroborated by a RULE-5 consult.
defects.summary: The node-local record of which locks this mount holds (ctx->held) is published AFTER a grant has already been recognised and removed BEFORE a release is known to have landed, and it carries no mode, no attempt identity and no conversion state. Every correctness decision that reads it as 'not tracked therefore not held' can therefore act on a live tenure. The direct-handoff adopt arm makes this concrete: it validates the slot image, then calls track_held() — an observe-to-track window in which a concurrent cleanup sees nothing tracked and clears the very holder bit being adopted.
defects.mechanism: dlm/dlm_caw.c:1982 track_held() records a SLOT INDEX only (no mode), scanning ctx->held.slots[] under ctx->held.lock; dlm_caw.c:2120 untrack_held() removes it. Six track sites (2102, 2915, 3204, 4110, 4727, 7953/7979) and seven untrack sites (4211, 4326, 5184, 5556, 6233, 6250, 6625). In the adopt arm (dlm_caw.c:2823) validation happens against cur_slot and track_held() is called at 2915, with no lock held across the pair. ctx->held additionally has a STICKY overflow latch (dlm_caw.h:453 held_overflow) which, once set, leaves tracking permanently incomplete for the mount's life and today only disables one consumer (the post-recovery settle purge, MXFS_CAW_PURGE_SKIP_TRACKED).
defects.evidence: The in-source doc for is_tracked_held() (dlm_caw.c:2016) itself states the property is only 'in steady state ctx->held mirrors our on-disk holder bits exactly'. GPT sess111: 'A flat slot/mode array documented as matching disk state in steady state is tracking or telemetry, not necessarily authoritative synchronization' — it has an observe-to-track window, track/untrack ordering windows, no attempt identity, no local reference count, no conversion-transition representation, and incomplete state after overflow. The overflow direction is already documented as asymmetric at dlm_caw.h:450: 'Declining to reclaim leaks slots; purging a live hold corrupts.'
defects.blast_radius: Any decision that treats untracked as unheld. Today: the post-recovery settle purge. Proposed and REJECTED this session as a blocker-6 fix precisely because of these windows. Under overflow the mount is unsound for every such decision, not just the settle purge.
defects.next: sess112 moved tenure publication into the same critical section that ends the acquiring attempt (0.11.441), closing the observe-to-track window for the publish side.  sess113 RULE-5: necessary but NOT sufficient, and three adjacent invariants are still unproven.  (1) tenure[] IS NECESSARILY ZERO for the whole adoption window -- the gap between the holder bit appearing on disk and lreq_finish publishing -- so tenure[]==0 is not a sufficient negative-ownership predicate; the registry also has NO observed write-grant epoch, so it cannot distinguish a delayed grant for an ABANDONED request from a grant for the CURRENT one, nor from a bit left by an earlier tenure (one node bit is reused across successive attempts, so temporal ownership needs an epoch/incarnation or an equally strong serialized transition).  (2) THE EXACT-MODE TENURE GUARD IS TOO WEAK UNDER CONVERSION: if a convert moves this node's on-disk representation PR->EX and then gives up before publishing, tenure[EX]==0 so cleanup clears EX and the surviving local PR tenure is left with NO on-disk holder bit at all.  Cancellation may need to DOWNGRADE to the strongest remaining locally required mode rather than clear.  AUDIT FIRST: does the convert CAS clear the old mode bit in the same image that sets the new one?  If it keeps both, the invariant differs and must be proven either way.  (3) lreq_release_all memsets the WHOLE tenure vector while tenure[m]>1 is representable; that is safe only if a higher local layer guarantees the disk unlock CAS happens exclusively on the FINAL local reference.  That invariant is neither enforced nor asserted -- make it explicit and mechanically checked.  Also make lreq_gc require pin==0 and no live op, and make lreq_release_all respect pin.

defects.opened: 2026-08-04 sess112 (ccloop c7ee71c6) — found by line audit while building the local request registry for D-SAMENODE-WAITER-CANCEL-COLLISION
defects.found: Code proof from reading caw_drop_own_waiter() against its three call sites. Not yet exercised by a test. SHIPPED behaviour since sess48 (0.11.398), when the function was introduced.
defects.summary: The give-up reconcile clears this node's waiter/holder bits at a REMEMBERED slot index without ever checking that the slot still holds the resource it was remembered for. A slot that was tombstoned and re-claimed for a DIFFERENT resource in the meantime carries our node bit as a live registration for THAT resource — and the reconcile cancels it.
defects.mechanism: dlm/dlm_caw.c caw_drop_own_waiter(ctx, slot_idx, giveup_mode) validated only `cur_slot->magic == MXFS_CAW_MAGIC` before CASing `waiters &= ~node_bit; waiters_ex &= ~node_bit; holders[giveup_mode] &= ~node_bit`. Live magic is satisfied by ANY live slot, including one now owned by an unrelated resource. Two of the three call sites make this reachable: the grant-wait timeout passes a slot index captured up to a full acquire timeout earlier (MXFS_CAW_WAIT_TIMEOUT_MS, liveness-extended), and the claim-exhaustion site passes whatever index the last retry happened to leave in slot_idx — an index the acquire may never have registered on at all. CAW slots are recycled through the tombstone path, so the index is not a stable identity for the resource.
defects.evidence: Line-level: the pre-sess112 function body read the slot, tested magic, and went straight to the bit clears with no memcmp against `resource` — and the function did not even take a resource argument, so the check was not merely omitted, it was unrepresentable. The three call sites are the grant-wait timeout, claim-retry exhaustion and convert exhaustion.
defects.blast_radius: Correctness and liveness on an UNRELATED resource. Clearing a holder bit strips a live local tenure's on-disk write authority (unfenced writer — the same corruption class as D-SAMENODE-WAITER-CANCEL-COLLISION, but reaching a resource the abandoning thread never touched). Clearing a waiter bit strands an unrelated acquire until its own timeout. Both are silent: no probe fired on the wrong-resource path because nothing looked.
defects.next: sess112 landed the resource memcmp at the remembered slot on 0.11.441 (the check was previously UNREPRESENTABLE -- the function took no resource argument).  That direction is right but sess113 RULE-5 found the disposition wrong and the debt model structurally broken.  (1) IDENTITY MISMATCH IS NOT DISCHARGE: `if (resource mismatch) { rc = 0; break; }` means 'the remembered location is stale', NOT 'the obligation is complete'.  Recorded debt must survive a mismatch, retarget via a canonical lookup, or escalate.  (2) A SINGLE owed_slot is structurally wrong: several give-ups on one resource can remember DIFFERENT slot indices (the resource moves after a tombstone+reclaim; the claim-exhaustion caller's index is a probe position it may never have registered on), so a later debt silently overwrites an earlier one -- and losing an old waiters_ex clear recreates the measured 16-node wedge.  Model debt as a COLLECTION of exact obligations (resource incarnation, slot index, stable slot-claim cookie, bit classes/modes); note slot->generation is NOT a stable claim identifier because any write bumps it, so this needs a claim epoch that changes only on tombstone/reassign.  (3) A blind re-scan by resource is NOT a safe substitute: ABA on resource reuse, same resource in a NEW slot incarnation, movement during the scan, duplicate claims, and 65536 slots per debt.  (4) A claim-exhaustion probe position the node never registered on should not become HOLDER debt at all. (5) memcmp on struct mxfs_resource_id is only safe if it has no padding and is canonically initialised -- verify, else compare fieldwise.
defects.why_still_open: Fix written but NOT verified. RULE 6: FIXED AND VERIFIED requires testing that exercises the cause; nothing has run on 0.11.441 yet.

defects.summary: Unmounting a forced-shutdown (dirty-log) mxfs releases the heartbeat slot as 'clean teardown' even though the log slice still holds unreplayed fsync-acknowledged content. The next mount of that slot is a pass-2 fresh claim (slice ADOPTED) whose gate skips the images, and because the node never DIED no survivor is ever elected to foreign-replay the slice. The fsync'd data is silently and permanently lost.
defects.evidence: sess179, 0.11.464 (sv 66F51D070BC971F72E39387), test32 loop repro via tests/vergate.sh mixed_build arm: mount loop7, fsync file /b4/marker, XFS_IOC_GOINGDOWN NOLOGFLUSH(2), umount rc=0 -> dmesg 'disklock: released heartbeat slot 0 (clean teardown)' DESPITE dirty slice; remount -> 'fresh claim — slice ADOPTED' + 'Starting recovery' + P227-TOKENSUM buf_items=7 tokened=0 untagged=7 wskip=7 + P227-FR-ATOMIC-SKIP whole txn (items=10) + P273-SHADOW-EVAL WOULD_APPLY=0; file GONE (arm reports file=0, FAIL). The refusal legs of the same arm (future-gen refusal before recovery) PASS; only the durability leg fails.
defects.mechanism: The clean-teardown slot release path does not verify the slice is clean before producing a CONSUMABLE sector. A shutdown fs cannot write its unmount record, so its slice stays dirty; releasing the slot as clean violates the adopted-slice design invariant that ONLY completed recovery produces a consumable sector (xfs_log.c sess32/sess165 comments). Trigger is any forced shutdown (I/O error, ENOSPC shutdown, admin goingdown) followed by umount+remount — no crash needed. Distinct from D-OWN-CRASH-RECLAIM-PATH-UNREACHABLE (pass-1 unreachable): even a working pass-1 would not match here because the clean release consumed the stamp.
defects.containment: None. Loss is silent (no error at umount or remount; probes P227/P273 record the skip but nothing alerts). True-crash path differs: ACTIVE stamp remains, peer-death machinery can elect replay.

defects.disposition: FIXED AND VERIFIED sess191 (closure build 0.11.465, srcversion 4DB2D8A8247E6DF80AE6F2F). CAUSE (proven sess179-180, DIAG-DSR-1/2): the clean-teardown slot release ran unconditionally at umount of a shutdown fs — umount cancelled the queued withdraw work before it ran, so a DIRTY slice was released as a CONSUMABLE 'clean teardown' sector; the next mount fresh-claimed it (slice ADOPTED, images skipped) and the fsync'd data was silently lost. FIX (RULE-5 rulings sess180/184/188/189, landed sess183-190): (a) shutdown umount now stamps WITHDRAWN durably (P163-WITHDRAW-STAMP) instead of releasing clean — voluntary death, slice stays unconsumable; (b) write-time snlocal marker at claim under single_node_exclusive=1 + kind-17 recheck legs so a single-node dirty slice can be fence-certified (SINGLE_NODE_EXCLUSIVE) and its untagged records replayed (P227-SNLOCAL-ACCEPT); (c) sess190 mount ADMISSION barrier: top-of-pass late-death drain + on-disk pending-descriptor sweep (mxfs_disklock_get_recovery_pending_slots), inline replay rounds, 30s admission wait then mount -EBUSY — no mount goes live over an unrecovered dirty slice, fail-closed. VERIFIED sess191 on the rig, all under unchanged acceptance criteria: (1) tests/dirty_slice_release_repro.sh test32 all — race, delay AND remount arms PASS in 8.8s (<60s budget); remount shows P274-CLAIM-WITHDRAWN-SKIP -> P236-FENCE-CERTIFIED kind=SINGLE_NODE_EXCLUSIVE -> recovery lease -> foreign replay P227-SNLOCAL-ACCEPT -> barrier 'cohort=0x0 late=0x1 replayed=1', marker B4-dirty-slice intact. (2) tests/vergate.sh test32 mixed_build — the discovering criterion, file=1 leg now content-checked (B4-mixed-build): PASS; refusal legs unchanged (refuse=1 line, recovery lines=0). (3) FULL BOARD 32/caw on 0.11.465: 27/27 PASS including fence_during_write and crash_consistency (teardown-change regression check per ledger item 4); prep/mount convergence 72s — no mount-time regression from the admission sweep. Harness notes sess191: vergate mixed_build now sets single_node_exclusive=1 for the whole arm (host-private loop device — operator assertion TRUE, same convention as the repro since sess187) and uses unique per-run dmesg tags (ring buffer keeps prior runs' tags).
defects.residual_note: The unfenceable-residue behavior change (mount now FAILS -EBUSY after 30s admission wait when a dirty descriptor-bearing slice cannot be certified, instead of going live owns-nothing) is intended per the sess189 ruling. Multi-node voluntary-withdraw replay (survivor election path, peers live) is exercised by the repro's remount arm acting as the surviving claimer and by the 32-node board's fence/crash cells; no separate multi-node arm was required by this entry's closure criterion. P-IUNLSTORE-PENDGRAFT fired once (test24 15:09:45): cert {0xf5->0xffffffff} explained the skew and the committed value was GRAFTED - the exact repair this fix exists to perform. defects.mechanism: iup->old_agino is captured at item creation and the caller advances in-core i_next_unlinked immediately; the BUFFER only catches up at precommit. In that window incore legitimately disagrees with the iunl-store's committed value. LIVESKEW (added sess48-v5 per GPT c3-391 ruling to stop grafts against live divergent inodes) compared incore against the record and refused, leaving the CLMERGE-restored fossil (0x101, the pre-0x100 value whose home write was lost) in the buffer for precommit to trip over.

defects.evidence: sess202, 0.11.471, laps 2-4 of `./run.sh 32 caw rsync_paired` on the same fs: lap2 12:36Z test16+test22 FAIL (rsync rc!=0, leftover temp dotfile, 401 files, zero kernel probes); lap4 12:55Z 3 nodes FAIL (test4 among them, 2 failed checks each, no shutdown). run.sh's /tmp collect dir is deleted before the per-node rsync stderr can be read. || SESS384 -- THE ERRNO IS NO LONGER UNKNOWN. Captured verbatim at 32/caw on 0.19.6 the moment the terminal-record guarantee (D-CRASH-CONSISTENCY-NO-TERMINAL-RECORD-CAPTURE-374) let the row report itself. Board cell: `FAIL rsync_paired nodes_pass=0/32 states:BUDGET_EXHAUSTED=9,FAIL=23 hostload=21.24 first_fail[test1:checks=6 passed=2 failed=4] faildist[0x9,1x15,4x8] steps[rsync barrier ready=9]` [60s/60s]. rank1's own reason, straight from rsync's stderr: `rsync: [receiver] mkstemp "/mnt/shared/.rsync_paired/node1/d1/.file40.ibjm7M" failed: Invalid exchange (52)` and `rsync: [receiver] mkstemp "/mnt/shared/.rsync_paired/node1/d1/.file5.y8aWuq" failed: Input/output error (5)`, with rc=23, file count exp=400 got=0, content sum exp=23a2d8970f1d3bfae523c69a993401ca got=d41d8cd98f00b204e9800998ecf8427e (i.e. NOTHING transferred). errno 52 on Linux is EBADE, and in this tree -EBADE has exactly ONE meaning: SCSI RESERVATION CONFLICT (dlm/disklock.h:926 'CAS bounces with SCSI RESERVATION CONFLICT (-EBADE)', dlm/v5_mount.h:748, dlm/scsipr.c:569 'D1 (EBADE on write = fencing event)', pal/linux/kern.c:4322 'ret = -EBADE'). So the user-visible failure of a file creation is a RAW FENCING ERRNO leaked to userspace: this node was fenced mid-write and the application was told 'Invalid exchange' rather than the mount being shut down and returning EIO. The second errno, EIO(5), is the same node after its shutdown completed -- which is what the application should have seen from the start. Distribution across the fleet in the same run: 15 nodes failed 1 check, 8 failed 4, 9 never produced a verdict at all (parked at `rsync barrier ready`).

defects.next: 1) DONE sess384: the errno is EBADE(52), a raw SCSI RESERVATION CONFLICT reaching userspace from mkstemp, followed by EIO(5) once the mount finished shutting down. The 'errno unknown' blocker this entry was named for is CLOSED. 2) THE DEFECT IS NOW SHARPER, not smaller: a fenced node must never return -EBADE to a syscall. Audit every path that can propagate the PAL/scsipr -EBADE into a VFS return (pal/linux/kern.c:4322 is the origin; dlm/v5_mount.c:5941 and :7585 both branch on it) and convert it at the boundary -- the correct user-visible behaviour on a fence is filesystem shutdown then EIO, which is what the SECOND error line shows the same node producing moments later. 3) Then re-decide whether what remains is a distinct defect from D-FENCED-VICTIM-NONCONTAINMENT-498 or a symptom of it.

defects.summary: incident474 arm B: the 8-node arm-A wedge was NOT contained - it cascaded to total 32-node fleet collapse within ~7 minutes (last survivor test1 withdrew 15:56:19Z). Survivors correctly fenced/replayed/purged the victims, but (1) victim-held EX inode locks stayed unreclaimable after purge, (2) withdrawn victims KEPT SENDING network announces - test21's retired identity was still heartbeating 6 minutes after being purged, and (3) the 'holders alive' liveness extension used those announces to stretch survivor lock waits to the 480s cap on locks whose holders were dead filesystems - so replayers died one by one until none remained.

defects.mechanism: Three cooperating non-containment holes, all evidence-backed: (a) purge of a dead node does not reclaim/invalidate the EX inode locks it held (or reclamation is gated on a drain the dead holder can never complete); (b) a withdrawn node's network announce path keeps running after withdraw - shutdown does not stop the announcer, so its identity stays 'alive' to peers; (c) the liveness extension trusts announces alone ('holder is alive') without checking the holder's fs is still mounted/serviceable, converting a dead holder into a 480s wait instead of an immediate reclaim.
defects.containment: None. Any multi-node wedge that triggers shutdown becomes a fleet-wide outage; defeats the purpose of per-node fencing/recovery.

defects.sess382_measured_cascade_and_unreprepabl: SESS382 — CORRECTED BY MY OWN IMMEDIATE RE-RUN; READ THE WHOLE ENTRY, NOT THE HEADLINE. Both runs used the same recipe (32/caw, MXFS 0.19.4, natural workload dirent_durability + ag_strand_repair, NO fault injection, the three sess382 fix levers disabled — mxfs.reldefer_reload=0, mxfs.relog_holds_obligation=0, mxfs.relog_holds_version=0 — and mxfs.reldefer_noprogress_ms=2000 to bring the wedge inside the test window). RUN 1: P-INODE-WEDGE=1, ag_strand_repair FAIL at its full 240s/240s budget with only 18/32 nodes passing (8 FAIL, 6 NO_TERMINAL_RECORD), and ALL 32 NODES LEFT NOMOUNT. RUN 2 (rings cleared, immediately after, identical recipe): P-INODE-WEDGE=1 on test9, test9 NOMOUNT, and ALL 31 SURVIVORS STAYED MOUNTED. Recovery ran CORRECTLY and in the right order — P163-RECOVERY-COMPLETE=1 with P97-SWEEP=2 strictly after it, which is exactly the sess215 b2/b3 containment behaving as designed. So on this build the single-victim wedge IS contained, and run 1's fleet-wide NOMOUNT is unexplained. ag_strand_repair.sh contains no umount/rmmod/virsh/destroy, so the test does not unmount nodes itself; whether run 1 was a genuine cascade or a harness/teardown artifact is UNDETERMINED and is the thing to settle next. Do not treat 1-wedge-to-32-down as established. SEPARATE AND MORE SERIOUS, from run 2 and worth its own attention: dirent_durability FAILED with durable_loss=3 (nodes_pass=0/32, 'rounds=30 durable_loss=3 late_ok=12 mkdir_err=0') — under this pre-fix emulation a wedge coincided with the loss of THREE dirents that had already been acknowledged durable. The configuration is deliberately degraded and is NOT a shipping configuration (shipping defaults give a green board), so this is evidence about what the pre-sess382 code did when it wedged, not a new shipping defect. It does mean the pre-fix wedge was not merely an availability event: when it fired it could take acknowledged-durable directory entries with it. Cross-reference D-RELOG-BEHIND-DISK-OBLIGATION-DEADLOCK-WEDGE-380 (CLOSED sess382), whose fixes eliminate the obligation/deferral that leads here. RIG NOTE from run 1's recovery: two nodes (test4, test5) could not be recovered by prep_cluster at all — three attempts ended 'ABORT: cluster prep failed' converging at active_count=30, with mxfs.ko LOADED but unmounted and P265-BASTQ-STATS counters byte-frozen across samples 12s apart (submitted=24038 dispatched=19354 merged=3241 rearmed=2548). Recovery needed a VM destroy/start. The live libvirt domains for those two hosts are test4r/test5r (clone replacements from the sess377 host-corruption recovery); the original test4/test5 domains are stuck 'in shutdown'. An un-reprepable survivor is a containment concern in its own right and is reproducible-adjacent to run 1.

defects.sess382_hole_c_CONFIRMED_reproducibly: SESS382 — HOLE (c) IS NOW DIRECTLY DEMONSTRATED AND REPRODUCIBLE ON DEMAND. MXFS 0.19.5 sv 453E3385BB93079744E6677, 32/caw. WHY A NEW FAULT WAS NEEDED: sess382's inode-wedge injection (mxfs.iflush_fence_fault_ino) cannot exercise this hole, and I measured that rather than assuming it. A wedge there makes the victim force-shutdown and WITHDRAW immediately, and withdraw STOPS the disklock heartbeat (sess213's finding), so the holder stops looking alive: single-victim wedge on test1 left 31 survivors MOUNTED, recovery ran in the correct order (P163-RECOVERY-COMPLETE then P97-SWEEP), and the fleet logged ZERO P-WAIT-EXTEND. Hole (c) needs the arm-A shape — a holder that is UNSERVICEABLE BUT STILL BEATING — which nothing in the tree could produce. THE SWITCH: mxfs.hold_grant_fault_ino makes mxfs_dlm_bast_process refuse to release a chosen inode's grant while the node stays mounted and its HB thread keeps beating (the sleep is in the drain, not the HB thread, and it is INTERRUPTIBLE — mxfs_pal_sleep_ms() is msleep()/TASK_UNINTERRUPTIBLE and would have added a permanent D-state task per node, the exact regression sess381 shipped once already). Harness: tests/hold_grant_liveness.sh <holder> <waiter> <window>. THE MEASUREMENT, verbatim: holder test1 held ino=132 for ~120s with MOUNT=UP throughout (P384-HOLD-GRANT-FAULT x14 samples). Waiter test2 logged 'P-WAIT-EXTEND type=1 ino=132 ag=0 want=3 el_ms=120159 blockers=1 - holders alive; extending past base timeout' and then 'P34-ACQ-SLOW ino=132 isdir=1 req_mode=3 dur_ms=129588 attempts=1 rc=0'. The acquire took 129.6 SECONDS and completed only because the fault was disarmed; left armed it would have run to the 480s liveness-extended cap (dlm_caw.c:6449). That is precisely the entry's hole (c): v5_caw_holders_alive -> mxfs_disklock_slot_live consults ONLY ctx->node_track[slot].live, i.e. whether the heartbeat thread is beating, and P-WAIT-EXTEND extends the wait on that basis alone. The oracle has no way to ask whether the holder's filesystem is serviceable or whether that specific grant is making any progress. VERDICT: hole (c) CONFIRMED. This is the first reproducible demonstration; previously it rested on the sess208 incident forensics alone. The fix per the sess214 RULE-5 ruling is c1 (advisory serviceability states in the HB record) + c2 (grant-bound progress cookies; an HB beat is NOT progress), rolled out telemetry-first, with escalation aimed at the NONPROGRESSING HOLDER and never at the waiter. Note for the implementer: struct mxfs_hb_feature.feat_flags (uint16, 'compatible advertisements; 0', CRC-protected, old nodes wrote 0) is the natural carrier for c1's states with no on-disk layout change.
defects.sess382_plan_of_record_hole_c: SESS382 PLAN OF RECORD for hole (c), per RULE-5 ruling 3 (ccmemory ccloop-c7ee71c6-sess382-GPT-ruling3-grant-progress-publication). PRIORITY CHANGED by this session's reproduction: c2 (grant-bound progress) is the LOAD-BEARING half, not c1. In the reproduction the holder's filesystem was fully SERVICEABLE and only one grant was stuck, so serviceability states cannot catch it. RULED PLACEMENT: NOT the CAW slot and NOT slot pad0 — a per-progress-event CAW on a contended slot reproduces the hot-LBA serialization already measured elsewhere (59,742ms on a contended root slot vs 3ms). Also explicitly REJECTED: deriving progress from slot generation, holder bitmaps, timestamps or HB beats — a frozen generation is equally consistent with 'useful off-slot AIL/log work' and 'infinite retry loop', and generation moves for unrelated waiter activity. PREFERRED: a dedicated per-node SINGLE-WRITER progress page/table (A/B pair, whole-page CRC, monotonic publication_seq, node_boot_epoch), written at HB cadence plus at transitions, with NO write per AIL item or retry; the HB record advertises support and the latest publication_seq. LAYOUT BLOCKER, established sess382 by reading tools/mkfs_mxfs.c:1631-1633 — THE ENVELOPE HAS NO RESERVED SLACK. The regions are packed: journal_offset = MXFS_SUPER_SIZE, disklock_offset = ALIGN_UP_4K(journal_offset + journal_size), xfs_data_offset = ALIGN_UP_4K(disklock_offset + disklock_size). So a NEW region means an mkfs layout change (every existing filesystem needs re-mkfs) plus an MXFS_PROTO_GEN bump. The alternative the ruling calls 'acceptable for an initial bounded implementation' is carving the HB record — but note the HB body is a UNION (evict ring OR recovery descriptor), so anything carved from INSIDE the union DISAPPEARS during RECOVERY_GUARD, which is exactly when progress evidence matters most. A carve must therefore move the union boundary and live OUTSIDE it, alongside prov(32B)/mepoch(44B)/feat(12B) — and the 512B sector is already fully packed (prov@424, mepoch@456, feat@500), so it can only come out of the evict ring (already carved twice, 28->25->23). That yields room for very few entries, while the ruling requires ONE ENTRY PER OUTSTANDING BAST with explicit OVERFLOW handling. DECIDE THIS FIRST — it is the gate on everything else. BINDING (minimum): node/mount epoch + the SAME canonical 32B resource id the CAW slot uses + holder grant_cookie (never reused within the boot/mount epoch) + acquire_slot_generation (evidence only, it wraps) + bast_request_id {requester_node, requester_boot_epoch, request_seq} + drain_epoch. A descriptor found WITHOUT acknowledgement of the current BAST must NOT authorize an extension; RELEASED/RETIRED must be published durably BEFORE the grant incarnation can be reused. PROGRESS DEFINITION: monotonic closure of a FIXED obligation ledger snapshotted at BAST accept — NOT execution events. txn commit / log force / AIL op / iflush attempt / re-log / retry counter can all tick forever in a loop. Work does NOT count if it replaces an old obligation with a new equivalent one. (Note the sess382 fix to D-RELOG-BEHIND-DISK-...-380 already implements this rule for the re-log: the drain's gated re-log no longer creates obligations.) ESCALATION: there is NO safe 'revoke just this grant' while the holder can still issue I/O. Ladder = verify+re-challenge (bounded) -> targeted local intervention on the holder -> quarantine the resource or quiesce the mount (publish WITHDRAWING) -> holder self-withdrawal / mount force-shutdown (sacrifice the affected MOUNT before the whole node) -> external SCSI-PR fencing only if withdrawal is unacknowledged or I/O cessation cannot be proven. Expiry does NOT let the waiter assume ownership, and the waiter is never the thing killed. Keep an absolute deadline or the ladder becomes the new 480s loop. ROLLOUT: publish-only -> shadow gate -> enforce on injected faults -> subset -> cluster-wide. DECISIVE FALSIFIER: a material population of shadow denials followed by ordinary completion of the SAME grant incarnation with no intervention, withdrawal, fault disarm or newly observed qualifying advance. Completion after disarming a deliberate fault must be classified separately.

defects.summary: Every filesystem formatted by the rig (mkfs_mxfs default log_node_count=4, prep_fs.sh passes no -n) gives the 32-node cluster only 4 XFS log slices; mount maps node_slot % log_node_count (xfs_mount.c ~1040) so 8 nodes journal CONCURRENTLY into each slice. Slice content is an interleaved soup of up to 8 self-consistent log streams (same uuid, same cycle). Foreign crash recovery of any slice (xfs_log.c:811, v5_mount.c:1072 use the same modulo) parses the soup and fails find_tail with -EIO -- the incident474 slot-30 forever-retry. Worse: EVERY node's own journal is co-written by 7 peers, so ANY crash recovery (own or foreign) on this rig replays corrupt data; weeks of crash_consistency PASSes on 32/caw are suspect. Also xlog_clear_stale_blocks (xfs_log_recover.c:1391) writes filler into the slice during foreign replay attempts, actively corrupting co-tenants' LIVE logs.

defects.mechanism: mkfs_mxfs.c:1479 default log_node_count=4 (-n flag line 1490, max 64); tests/setup/prep_fs.sh:74 runs 'mkfs_mxfs -f $DEV' with no -n. xfs_mount.c:1039-1044 own-slice = node_slot % m_mxfs_log_node_count; xfs_log.c:811 and dlm/v5_mount.c:1072 foreign-slice = dead_slot % count. No guard anywhere refuses a mount whose slot >= log_node_count, so slice sharing is silently permitted. Additional mkfs hazard: the AG-fit clamp (mkfs_mxfs.c ~1186) SILENTLY shrinks logblocks below log_node_count*16384, so a large -n can silently produce slices under the empirically-required 64MB minimum (sess36 wedge).

defects.summary: During foreign-slice recovery the recovery owner holds the disklock ctx->lock for ~35s (recovery stage 3->5 window), starving its OWN heartbeat thread: hb write waited lockwait_ms=34978 (write_ms=0) and only completed the same millisecond P163-RECOVERY-COMPLETE logged. That is >half the 62s lease. If replay+purge ever exceeds the lease (bigger logs, slower LUN, more victims), the recovery owner gets fenced BY ITS PEERS mid-recovery -> new owner restarts recovery -> potential fence cascade among recovery owners. Also delayed the withdraw stamp 16s in the same window (287.1 P-WITHDRAW -> 303.7 STAMP).

evidence:
SESS380 ROOT CAUSE, IN THIRD-PARTY CODE, WITH THE TRACE THAT PROVES IT. The 60 s quantum is a wait-for CYCLE in the SCST target's SCSI-atomic (COMPARE AND WRITE overlap) blocker graph. scst_check_scsi_atomicity() (scst/src/scst_targ.c) walked the WHOLE dev_exec_cmd_list and skipped only the command itself (`continue`, not `break`), so a command whose FIRST atomicity check is DEFERRED installs wait edges back to commands already blocked ON IT. The deferral is routine: scst_do_check_blocked_dev() appends the cmd to dev_exec_cmd_list BEFORE the atomicity check, and skips that check entirely when the cmd is not SCSI-atomic AND dev_scsi_atomic_cmd_active == 0 (leaving scsi_atomicity_checked == 0); if the cmd is then parked by a DEVICE block it STAYS on dev_exec_cmd_list, collects every overlapping CAW as a waiter, and runs its first check only on re-entry after the device unblocks -- at which point it blocks on its own waiters. Captured verbatim with TRACE_BLOCK on lba 155671 (the root inode's CAW slot):
  536846.409771  Device BLOCK (new count 1)
  536846.409778  Delaying cmd 48a9c59d due to blocking (tag 119, op READ(16))
  536846.409819  Delaying CAW 1d61a266 (blockers 1) due to overlap with 48a9c59d
  ... 5 more CAWs block on 48a9c59d ...
  536846.419048  Device UNBLOCK (new 0)
  536846.419053  Adding blocked cmd 48a9c59d to active cmd list
  536846.419087  Delaying cmd 48a9c59d (READ(16), blockers 1..5) due to overlap with
                 1d61a266, ff98f7ea, 0efda8f0, fca86073, 04c78c3a   <-- its own waiters
  536906.823647  Aborting cmd 48a9c59d ... state EXEC_CHECK_BLOCKING, proc time 60 sec
  536906.823672  Unblock aborted atomic-blocked cmd 48a9c59d
Corroborating aggregates over a 95 s window: the block/unblock accounting is EXACT, so it is not a leak (216 blocked commands = 204 normal unblocks + 12 abort-released; 90 device BLOCK / 90 UNBLOCK; 340 device-block parks / 340 reactivations; total device-blocked time only 0.512 s). And the wait distribution is strictly BIMODAL: p50 8 ms, p90 53 ms, then 4 samples in 0.1-1 s, 1 in 1-10 s, and 6 over 10 s with max 60.414 s. A queue whose median is 8 ms does not produce a 60 s tail out of 336 commands. It also explains the sess379 negative control exactly: with reads alone dev_scsi_atomic_cmd_active stays 0, so no atomicity check ever runs and no cycle can form. FIXED in scst 3.11.0-pre+caw-abort-reclaim.3 (edges installed only toward predecessors on the append-only list, so the graph is acyclic by construction; plus a dev_exec_seq stamp and a WARN_ONCE detector for non-backward edges). RULE-5 reviewed before landing.

SESS378 RE-MEASURED, WORSE THAN THIS ENTRY STATES AND ON A QUIESCENT FS WITH NO LIVE PEERS. During a 32-node mass unmount, test32's umount took 302 SECONDS (node uptime 656.49 s -> 958 s). While it was stuck, ALL 31 OTHER NODES HAD ALREADY UNMOUNTED AND rmmod'd, so no peer held the contended lock. Captured stack: umount is blocked in its INITIAL statx() of the mountpoint - mxfs_dlm_ilock_begin+0x177f -> xfs_ilock -> mxfs_getattr_dlm_lock -> xfs_vn_getattr -> vfs_getattr_nosec -> vfs_statx -> __x64_sys_statx - i.e. it never reaches the unmount itself. wchan=mxfs_dlm_ilock_begin. The inode was parked at xfs/xfs_mxfs_dlm.c:29999 with i_dlm_state=4 (MXFS_DLM_ISTATE_ACQUIRING, 'slow-path caw_lock in flight on this node') and TWO waiters (pids 2063, 2162) - yet a sweep of every task on the node found NO thread in caw_lock or mxfs_ag_dlm_lock and no other D-state task, and the P73-DEMEV ring showed both prior demoters had already completed their SET...CLEAR pairs (pids 1096 and 50). So ACQUIRING had NO OWNER driving it. It did eventually complete, so this is slowness rather than a permanent wedge - but 302 s to unmount a quiescent filesystem with zero live peers is a RULE 0 failure of a different magnitude than the 60-100 s recorded here, and the orphaned-ACQUIRING shape is a concrete lead for the root cause. A second sweep the same session took 170 s with one node exceeding a 150 s umount timeout.

SESS379 ROOT CAUSE, CAPTURED STACK (tests/mass_umount_stall_probe.sh, 32/caw, 0.15.0). 32-way simultaneous umount of a quiescent fs, reproduced twice: run 1 = 8 nodes 0.06-0.11s / 8 nodes ~60.6s / 16 nodes ~121.2s; run 2 = 2 nodes ~0.07s / 7 ~60.6s / 13 ~120.8s / 10 ~181.5s. The walls quantize at 0/60.5/121/181.5s = whole SCSI command-timeout units. Stack, identical on 30 of 32 nodes, D-state: blk_execute_rq < scsi_execute_cmd < mxfs_pal_scsi_read_fua_bdev < mxfs_pal_bdev_read_prio < read_slot < find_slot_skip < mxfs_dlm_caw_held < mxfs_v5_dlm_inode_held_rawmode < mxfs_dlm_ilock_begin < xfs_ilock < mxfs_getattr_dlm_lock < xfs_vn_getattr < vfs_getattr_nosec < vfs_statx < __x64_sys_statx. Fleet-wide dmesg sweep: 35 P-FUA-READ-RETRY, EVERY ONE on lba=144080 (the root directory inode's CAW slot) with ret=0x30000 (host_byte 0x03 = DID_TIME_OUT), resid=512, no sense. ZERO P73-WAITSTALL, ZERO P139-LOCKTOTAL, ZERO P34-ACQ-SLOW fleet-wide - which REFUTES both entering hypotheses (a leaked ISTATE_ACQUIRING with no owner, and a genuinely slow caw_lock): the block is neither in the ilock park loop nor in an inode grant wait. Print caps were NOT exhausted (17 and 62 P139 lines this boot vs a 2000 cap; P73-WAITSTALL had fired 0 times ever).

Same fleet, same build, same script, STAGGER_S=3 (departures 3s apart instead of simultaneous): ALL 32 nodes unmounted in 0.04-0.09s (max 0.09s, mean 0.05s), 0/32 over the 5s budget, zero P303-VERIFY-BREAKER, 7 P-FUA-READ-RETRY fleet-wide. SESS379 TARGET-SIDE SIGNATURE. clyde runs SCST 3.11.0-pre+caw-abort-reclaim.2 - i.e. the known CAW<->READ scsi_atomic wedge fix IS installed, so this is not that infra bug. Comparing the two windows in clyde's kernel log: STALLED (80s of mass unmount) = 330 scst_abort_cmd + 165 ABORT_TASK TMFs (execute_task_management fn=0), spread continuously from storm+15s to storm+45s; CLEAN (the 30s hot-slot storm) = NO ENTRIES AT ALL. SESS379 PARTIAL FIX MEASURED, 0.15.2 sv C46FD856C41CB8A33B1CB35. Same probe, same 32-way simultaneous shape: max wall 181.5s -> 60.65s, and the staircase collapses to a single step (1 node 0.06s, 31 nodes 60.2-60.65s). 21 P303-VERIFY-BREAKER fired, all on ino=128, all 'sampled=0 timeouts=1' - the governor engages exactly where predicted. REGRESSION: full 32/caw board after the change is 27/27 PASS (open_defects is the RULE-6 policy cell) - no regression from putting the ilock fast-path verify under a deadline.

SESS379 THE DOMINANT TERM IS NOW A SEPARATE, GENERAL DEFECT: D-HOT-SLOT-CAW-SERIALIZES-LUN-PER-LBA-379. A non-departing observer measured 59,742 ms for `stat` of the mount root against 3 ms for `stat` of a different file on the same mount in the same window, so the unmount stall is one symptom of N nodes converging COMPARE AND WRITE on ONE CAW slot, not an unmount-path problem. This entry stays open for its own RULE 0 budget (<=5s/node) but closes with, or after, that one.
defects.mechanism: THREE STACKED RETRY POLICIES ON ONE LOGICAL OPERATION, on a syscall's critical path. mxfs_dlm_ilock_begin serves a cached grant with no I/O, EXCEPT for three defence-in-depth ownership verifies (P108 stale-EX, throttled 1000ms/inode; the throttled dir-EX phantom check, 100ms/inode on CAW; and the un-throttled dir-EX check). Each does a probe-chain FUA slot read. The read is scsi_execute_cmd(30s timeout, 1 SCSI retry) inside an mxfs wrapper that retries up to 20 times => a worst case of ~20 minutes for ONE slot probe. When the shared LUN stops answering, a plain statx() inherits the whole amplification. The verifies are NOT pure detectors - each ENFORCES (P108-REACQUIRE / P106-STALE-EX / P-TCPEX-REACQ demote the cached grant to NL and force a real slow-path acquire) - so they may not simply be moved off the caller's path; what they may not do is block without bound.

defects.disposition: DISPROVED sess380 (RULE 6 disposition 1: direct evidence establishes that the reported behavior was not an MXFS defect). The ledgered behavior was 'simultaneous unmount of a 32-node fleet on a QUIESCENT fs takes 60-181s per node'. With ZERO change to MXFS it now takes 0.25-0.37s, and the 60s quantum has a located root cause in the SCST target's blocker graph with the trace that shows the cycle forming and the abort breaking it. RULE 0 is satisfied: native XFS unmount of a quiescent fs is under 1s and MXFS now measures 0.25s max across 32 simultaneous departures. NOTE FOR ANYONE REOPENING THIS: the disproof is that MXFS was not the CAUSE, not that MXFS is uninvolved -- MXFS is what puts a cluster-shared resource on one 512B sector, which is the overlap the target's cycle needed. That architectural point is tracked separately and was scored against its own acceptance bar; see D-HOT-SLOT-CAW-SERIALIZES-LUN-PER-LBA-379.

defects.opened: sess354 (2026-08-15), mechanism identified by the sess353 RULE-5 ruling during the #94 ATTRBIT root-cause
defects.summary: Cluster-wide superblock lost-update: each node keeps its OWN in-core m_sb and every SB transaction logs the WHOLE superblock buffer (xfs_log_sb serializes the logger's m_sb over the entire sector), so any peer's SB txn -- including routine lazy icount/ifree/fdblocks counter sync at log cover/unmount -- overwrites another node's persistent non-counter SB changes with the logger's stale copy. Runtime SB mutators are per-node and uncoordinated: feature adds (xfs_add_attr proven live on the rig pre-0.13.3 via first xattr-bearing create, quota flag adds, log_incompat/LARP), growfs geometry, label/UUID set, NEEDSREPAIR. Concrete proven instance (sess353, #94 root): node A's lazy ATTRBIT add was carried in its slice while every peer's m_sb lacked it; beyond causing the #94 false refusal, any peer's subsequent whole-SB log would have durably REVERTED A's versionnum change. 0.13.3 closes only the ATTRBIT arm (mkfs presets 0xB4B5 + cluster mount refuses !xfs_has_attr); every other whole-SB producer remains an uncoordinated multi-writer over one shared sector. GPT ruling: containment for the current profile is to FORBID ALL runtime non-counter SB mutations in cluster mode, rejecting BEFORE mutating m_sb; any future coordination protocol must cover EVERY whole-SB producer, not just feature-changing txns. Evidence: ccmemory ccloop-c7ee71c6-sess353-94-attrbit-root-and-fix-0133; sess353 transcript (GPT ruling item 4).
defects.next: 1) Enumerate every runtime whole-SB producer in the tree (callers of xfs_log_sb/xfs_sync_sb + direct XFS_BUF_TO_SBP writers): expected set = xfs_add_attr, xfs_qm quota-flag adds, xfs_add_incompat_log_feature/clear (LARP), xfs_growfs_data/log, label/UUID ioctls, NEEDSREPAIR set/clear, log-cover counter sync. 2) Land the cluster-mode gate per the ruling: each non-counter producer rejects (-EOPNOTSUPP or -EINVAL, before touching m_sb) when m_mxfs_dlm is active; counter-only sync remains allowed (it is what the #94 clean-skip classifier handles). 3) Build, deploy, verify: xattr path already unreachable via the 0.13.3 mount gate; exercise growfs + label ioctl on a cluster mount and assert clean rejection with no m_sb mutation and no SB txn logged. 4) Board regression to confirm no criterion depended on a now-rejected path.

defects.summary: A refused foreign-slice replay freezes ALL of the dead victim's held DLM grants forever, including resources provably outside the refused/quarantined domain. sess356 mixed run: test30 dirty-killed, replay refused (legacy blanket atomic-skip), AG2 quarantined (P241-RECOV-TERMINAL ag_mask=0x4, P240-QUAR-IMPORT cluster-wide) -- but the victim's root-ino=128 EX grant (AG0, inode class, untouched by any refused image) stayed frozen with no release path. 4 clean unmounters wedged 5min on root-ino EX, hit DLM -110, withdrew dirty; survivors ended root-dir livelocked under an endless P7B-BASTNOTIFY storm on ino=128. A single refused slice converts scoped AG quarantine into effective cluster-wide root outage. Even with the #1 enforcement gate live, genuinely torn/malformed txns still refuse => same freeze, so this is an independent containment defect.
defects.mechanism: Nothing dispositions a refused victim's held grants: recovery terminal-refusal publishes quarantine for the affected AG domain only, and grant release normally happens via replay-complete purge, which never runs for a refused slice. Frozen grants outside the quarantined domain are unreachable by the quarantine-refusal error path, so waiters block until DLM timeout.

defects.mechanism: PROVEN sess384 -- and it is NOT a capture race, arm (a), nor post-load contamination, arm (b). run.sh runs each node under `timeout <RULE-0 budget> ssh ...` and aggregates by grepping ^RESULT: out of the captured stdout. The node-side rendezvous cap it passes, COORD_TIMEOUT, defaulted to 120s and was clamped to `tt-15` for EXACTLY ONE criterion, dir_reuse_coherency, in a bespoke `case` in run_coord(). Every other criterion therefore ran with a rendezvous cap LARGER than its own kill box: rsync_paired 120 vs 60, crash_consistency 120 vs 90, posix_multi/strong_consistency/mmap_coherency/dlm_fairness/dlm_membership 120 vs 30, cache_coherency/zero_silent_loss/fence_during_write/fault_netpartition/soak/dirent_*_integrity 120 vs 60, scaling_curve/dlm_scaling/node_responsive 120 vs 90. So whenever a rendezvous genuinely stalled, the harness SIGKILLed the ssh at the budget long before the barrier layer could print its BARRIER_TIMEOUT record, and all N nodes reported NO_TERMINAL_RECORD with no diagnosis. run.sh's OWN dir_reuse_coherency comment documents this exact failure ('three straight wedged runs produced zero terminal records ... burned a session chasing a silent wedge that the barrier layer had detected but was never allowed to report') -- the fix was applied to that one criterion in 2026-07-25 and never generalized. INDEPENDENT CORROBORATION: across the whole recorded criteria.json history, the state BARRIER_TIMEOUT has NEVER APPEARED ONCE. The reporting path the code was written for was structurally unreachable on 26 of the 32 manifest rows. A second gap compounded it: the dispatch piped ssh straight into `grep -v`, so `timeout`'s exit status was grep's and the harness could not even tell a budget kill (124/137) from a transport failure (255) from a plain non-zero exit.

defects.fix_sess384: LANDED (node side verified locally; rig verification is step 3 of next). A three-path terminal-record guarantee, per the sess384 RULE-5 ruling (ccmemory ccloop-c7ee71c6-sess384-GPT-ruling-terminal-record-guarantee): (1) AUTHORITATIVE, run.sh: the per-node `timeout ssh` exit status is now captured (no pipe in between, rc to $tmpd/<node>.rc) and, when no RESULT line exists, the harness SYNTHESIZES the state -- 124/137 BUDGET_EXHAUSTED, 255 TRANSPORT_ERROR, other MISSING_TERMINAL_RECORD. This runs outside the ssh session so it cannot fail. (2) run.sh passes MXFS_DEADLINE_MS (per node, computed immediately before that node's own timeout starts, so ssh connect latency is charged to the budget exactly as the kill box charges it), MXFS_RESERVE_MS (4s, capped at tt/3) and MXFS_SPOOL. lib.sh converts the absolute deadline to a relative remaining interval ONCE at startup so an NTP step cannot move the watchdog. coord.sh gains coord_eff_timeout(), and coord_barrier/coord_get/coord_wait now cap at min(COORD_TIMEOUT, reporting deadline) -- the clamp is universal, not per-criterion. (3) lib.sh breadcrumbs: ck/ckeq record the current step (builtin printf, one write(2), no fork -- cheap enough for cache_coherency's 654 checks) into a snapshot file the watchdog can read, since a forked subshell cannot see live shell variables. (4) lib.sh watchdog: emits `RESULT: BUDGET_EXHAUSTED ... src=watchdog ... reason=step=<breadcrumb>` at the reporting deadline. It POLLS for the main shell by (pid,starttime) from /proc/<pid>/stat rather than sleeping the interval, because a background subshell inherits stdout and would otherwise hold the ssh channel open and stretch every passing test to its full budget; (pid,starttime) rather than bare `kill -0` avoids the PID-reuse TOCTOU that once wedged every barrier criterion cluster-wide. It does NOT kill the workload -- a D-state wait cannot take a signal -- run.sh's existing leftover sweep still does that, and now also triggers on a reported BUDGET_EXHAUSTED/SYSCALL_HANG/BARRIER_TIMEOUT, not only on total silence. (5) Every record is also spooled node-locally and run.sh fetches the spool before synthesizing, because ssh block-buffering has been measured to lose unflushed stdout when the kill lands. (6) `tail -1` arbitration is replaced by SOURCE PRECEDENCE (src=test > src=watchdog > untagged legacy > harness-synthesized) so a late fallback can never bury an earlier, more specific verdict. NOTHING WIDENS A BUDGET: the kill box is still tt and BUDGET_EXHAUSTED is not PASS. Local proof: tests/d384_terminal_record_guarantee.sh, 13/13 PASS -- a stalled test emits BUDGET_EXHAUSTED naming its step, on stdout and in the spool, written 3.9s into an 8s budget; a healthy test still emits its own PASS and returns in 1.0s with no watchdog record; a test that exits without finish() returns in 21ms.

defects.found: sess376, build 0.14.9 sv 25057F6813DDAF1ECB477CF, 32/caw
defects.summary: A terminal refusal quarantine PERMANENTLY occupies one disklock heartbeat slot (its RECOVERY_GUARD record is the durable verdict, so it must stay). The number of usable slots is the volume's log-slice count. On a cluster formatted with exactly as many slices as nodes -- which is the default (tests/setup/prep_fs.sh MXFS_LOG_SLICES=32) and what the 32-node rig runs -- there is then NO free slot, and the recovered node CANNOT MOUNT AT ALL: 'disklock: no free heartbeat slot in 0..31 -- the volume has 32 log slices ... Cluster is full; reformat with more slices (mkfs_mxfs -n) to admit more nodes' -> claim_slot -28 -> 'MXFS DLM init failed - aborting mount'. One refused slice therefore costs the cluster a node PERMANENTLY, and the operator is told to REFORMAT when the actual state is a quarantine awaiting repair. ESCALATED WITHIN THE SESSION, TWICE: (1) 32 IS A HARD CAP, not a default -- 'mkfs.mxfs: -n must be 1-32 (XFS caps the internal log at 2GiB-10MiB, so at most 32 ~64MB per-node slices fit; the slice count is the cluster's hard node limit for this filesystem)'. So at the maximum supported cluster size there is NO formatting option that leaves headroom, and the mount error's own advice ('reformat with more slices') is impossible to follow. (2) There is NO IMPLEMENTED REPAIR PATH. The quarantine message says 'needs operator repair + remount', but no tool and no knob clears a quarantined RECOVERY_GUARD record: chk_mxfs (-a/-y/-U) does not touch it, caw_slotdump is read-only, and the only in-kernel clear-to-EMPTY path is the clean-release CAS, which refuses any record that is not the caller's own live record. The only way to free the slot is mkfs_mxfs -f -- a reformat, i.e. total data loss, which also destroys the verdict the quarantine exists to preserve. Net effect: one refused slice permanently reduces a 32-node cluster to 31 nodes with no recovery short of rebuilding the filesystem.
defects.mechanism: PROVEN, code + platter. dlm/disklock.c claim path: when no free slot is found and ctx->slot_limit < MXFS_DISKLOCK_HB_SLOTS it returns -ENOSPC with the 'reformat with more slices' message; slot_limit is the volume's xfs_log_node_count (struct mxfs_ondisk_super, byte offset 96) because a slot beyond the slice count would have no journal. The quarantined slot is not free: its sector is a MXFS_DISKLOCK_FLAG_RECOVERY_GUARD (=3) record and recov_desc_present() requires exactly that flag, so the record IS the durable verdict every closure gate reads. Keeping it is correct -- the defect is the interaction: usable slots = slice count, and nothing reserves headroom for the verdict records a refusal will create. Measured on the rig: platter super says max_nodes=64 but log_slices=32, so slots 0..31 only; with 32 nodes mounted the table is 32/32 occupied; after a refusal the table is 31 live + 1 GUARD, still 32/32, and the rejoining node aborts its mount.

defects.audit_sess377_bucket_guards: THE 32..63 ARCHIVE PLAN IS DEAD, and the audit that killed it is load-bearing for anything that reads the heartbeat table. mxfs_disklock_guard_slot() treats a sector with BAD MAGIC as GUARDABLE, and its only caller, mxfs_unclaimed_bucket_scan() (xfs/xfs_mxfs_dlm.c:46172), iterates b < XFS_AGI_UNLINKED_BUCKETS (64) using the AGI unlinked-bucket index AS the disklock slot index. On an N-slice volume buckets N..63 can never be claimed by a member, so they are ALWAYS unclaimed and the sweep routinely takes a transient RECOVERY_GUARD in slots N..63 by design. So (a) slots 32..63 are live protocol state, not spare capacity, (b) a permanent record parked there would make guard_slot() return -EBUSY forever and that AGI unlinked bucket could never be swept (a permanent unlinked-inode leak), and (c) a distinct archive magic makes a record MORE likely to be overwritten, not less. CONSEQUENCE FOR EVERY READER: a RECOVERY_GUARD is two different things. With a valid descriptor (recov_desc_present() requires MXFS_RECOV_DESC_MAGIC in the body) it is a recovery lease or a terminal verdict; with an all-zero body it is a transient bucket-sweep guard. Both hb_report_claim_exhausted() and chk_mxfs --show-quarantine were corrected to distinguish them, and the OUT-OF-RANGE 'format/protocol violation' classification was narrowed to MEMBER-shaped records (ACTIVE/WITHDRAWN) only. AUDITED CLEAN: every in-tree descriptor reader goes through recov_desc_present()/recov_desc_of()/recov_lease_covers_node(), all of which require the descriptor magic, so no bucket-sweep guard can be mistaken for a victim recovery descriptor today. Also audited: the kernel NEVER writes the 4KB mxfs envelope super (zero write sites in dlm/, pal/, xfs/); only mkfs_mxfs (fresh struct), chk_mxfs (read-modify-write) and resize_mxfs (reads the whole struct at :797, rewrites at :1110) touch it.

defects.found: sess377, build 0.14.10 sv 7D01081DA5AF3C6F5A4D0A2, 32/caw, found by the new chk_mxfs --pr-keys
defects.summary: EVERY CLEAN UNMOUNT LEAVES THE DEPARTING NODE REGISTERED ON THE SHARED LUN. MXFS's entire exclusion story is SCSI persistent reservations, and mxfs_scsipr_create() sets local_key = node_id, so a registered key IS a node that can write to the device. A mount registers the key on EVERY multipath nexus (measured: 2 entries for one node); the clean-unmount path removes only ONE of them and reports success. The departed node's initiator therefore retains write access to the shared LUN after it has left the cluster, and nothing in MXFS ever checks. After all 32 nodes cleanly unmounted, the registration table was NOT empty.
defects.mechanism: PROVEN, code + measurement, and it is an ASYMMETRY between the register and unregister calls plus an error mapping that hides the result. REGISTER (pal/linux/kern.c:2861, mxfs_pal_scsi_pr_register): ops->pr_register(dev->bdev, 0, key, PR_FL_IGNORE_KEY) -- REGISTER AND IGNORE EXISTING KEY. dm_pr_register walks every path via multipath_iterate_devices and, because IGNORE_KEY makes each path accept unconditionally, EVERY nexus ends up registered. UNREGISTER (pal/linux/kern.c:3072, mxfs_pal_scsi_pr_unregister_bdev, and the same shape in mxfs_pal_scsi_pr_unregister at :3107): ops->pr_register(bdev, key, 0, 0) -- a plain REGISTER with old_key=key and NO PR_FL_IGNORE_KEY. dm's first pass runs with fail_early=true, so the first path that answers RESERVATION CONFLICT stops the iteration and the remaining nexus keeps the registration. THE ERROR MAPPING THEN ERASES THE EVIDENCE (pal/linux/kern.c:3084): 'if (ret == 0x18 || ret == -EBUSY) return 0;' with the comment 'our key was already removed -- preempted by another node or a previous unregister succeeded. The key is gone, which is the desired outcome.' That inference is unsound: a RESERVATION CONFLICT from ONE path says nothing about the others, and here it is returned precisely BECAUSE a path refused. The caller (pal/linux/xfs_super.c:1717 'Deferred PR unregister -- LAST') therefore logs nothing, and no code path in MXFS ever re-reads the registration table to confirm the key is gone.

Two separate nodes (test1 and test2, each via its own chk_mxfs run) reported the same single surviving key 0x00000000a5c5a98f = node_id 2781194639 -- which the quarantined verdict on slot 2 names as the recovery OWNER that published the terminal refusal ('refused by node=2781194639'). (2) THE CLEAN ROUND-TRIP, the decisive measurement: baseline (every node unmounted) = 2 keys 0x...a5c5a98f and 0x...7c11a613; mount test2 -> 3 keys: 0x...a5c5a98f plus 0x000000009d0a1ad8 TWICE (the two multipath nexuses; note 7c11a613 disappeared -- test2's PREVIOUS leaked registration was replaced by its new one, so the leak is bounded at about one per node, not unbounded); clean umount test2 (reported UNMOUNTED, no error) -> 2 keys: 0x...a5c5a98f and ONE surviving 0x...9d0a1ad8. Exactly one of the two entries was removed. (3) The prior cycle leaked identically: an earlier test2 mount+clean-unmount in the same session left 0x...7c11a613. So 2/2 clean unmounts leaked, plus the mass-unmount survivor. (4) node_id is per-incarnation, not stable: test2 was 0x7c11a613 on one mount and 0x9d0a1ad8 on the next, so a leaked key names an incarnation that no longer exists and no membership view will ever account for it. (5) test30's boot dmesg from earlier in the session independently corroborates the doubling: 'P-PR-PROBE mxfs: own key 0xfecadf5e visible, 64 key(s) registered' with 32 nodes mounted = 2 registrations per node.
defects.impact: The exclusion property MXFS fences on is not what the registration table says. Concretely: (a) a node that left the cluster cleanly can still write to the shared LUN; (b) an offline maintenance operation cannot prove exclusion -- this defect was found because the new chk_mxfs --accept-quarantine-loss refused to run, correctly, reporting the stale registrant; (c) PREEMPT AND ABORT operates on a key set containing orphan incarnations that no live member owns, so 'the victim's key is gone' and 'the registration table is clean' are different statements and the code treats them as one; (d) any future fence-capability or admission check that counts registrants sees phantom members.
defects.containment: None in MXFS. Detection now exists: 'chk_mxfs --pr-keys <dev>' (read-only, safe on a live cluster) prints the registration table with each key decoded as a node_id, and 'chk_mxfs --accept-quarantine-loss' refuses to touch anything while any key is registered.

Candidate shape, not chosen: (a) make the unregister symmetric with the register (dm's own fallback in dm_pr_register uses old_key=new_key/fail_early=false for exactly this reason), and/or issue the unregister per path rather than through the dm aggregate; (b) STOP mapping RESERVATION CONFLICT to success at pal/linux/kern.c:3084 -- it is the symptom, not a proof of absence; (c) VERIFY: after the late unregister, issue PERSISTENT RESERVE IN / READ KEYS and assert our key no longer appears; retry, and if it still appears log a loud, greppable failure. The verification is the real fix: whatever the transport does, MXFS must not report a departure it did not achieve. 2. Decide whether a stale registrant must also be reaped by the CLUSTER (a survivor preempting an orphan key whose node_id matches no live member and no recovery descriptor) or only by the departing node. Reaping from a survivor is a fence, so it needs the same authority story as any other preempt -- do not add it casually. 3. Verification test: mount one node, record the key count with chk_mxfs --pr-keys, unmount cleanly, assert the count returns EXACTLY to the pre-mount value and that the node's key is absent; repeat 3x; then the 32-node form -- mount all, unmount all, assert ZERO keys remain. Both must run on a multipath device, because the single-path case cannot expose this. 4. Also assert the negative: an unregister that fails must NOT be reported as success -- inject a failure (mxfs_dbg_pr_register_fail has a register-side twin) and assert the loud log fires.
defects.detector: chk_mxfs --pr-keys <dev> from any node, mounted or not. With the cluster fully unmounted the table MUST be empty; any entry is this defect. With N nodes mounted on a 2-path multipath device the table should hold 2N entries; after all N unmount cleanly it should hold 0.
defects.fix: LANDED 0.14.11 sv 59F765EF4CFF9E513F37FE2, pal/linux/kern.c + pal/linux/xfs_super.c. Per the sess377 RULE-5 ruling (ccmemory ccloop-c7ee71c6-sess377-GPT-ruling3-pr-unregister-leak-fix-shape): the symmetric unregister is the MECHANISM and the READ KEYS read-back is the POSTCONDITION. (1) mxfs_pal_scsi_pr_unregister_bdev() now issues the SYMMETRIC operation -- ops->pr_register(bdev, key, 0, PR_FL_IGNORE_KEY), i.e. REGISTER AND IGNORE EXISTING KEY with SERVICE ACTION RESERVATION KEY = 0. Every nexus accepts it regardless of what it currently holds, so dm's fail_early first pass has nothing to trip over and visits them all. (2) The 'RESERVATION CONFLICT means our key was already removed -> return 0' mapping is GONE. (3) New static mxfs_pr_key_present_bdev() verifies via ops->pr_read_keys, growing the buffer while the target's reported total exceeds the offered capacity, so a TRUNCATED view can never be read as absence; an incomplete or failed READ KEYS is an error, never 'gone'. (4) The loop is bounded by BOTH an attempt count (6) and an absolute wall-clock deadline (20s) because a synchronous PR command can block far longer than an attempt count suggests. (5) Result mapping is exactly the ruling's table: success+absent -> 0; conflict+absent -> 0 (already gone); anything+present -> -EBUSY; read-back failed/unsupported -> -EPROTO. New markers P301-PR-UNREG-INCOMPLETE, P301-PR-UNREG-UNVERIFIABLE, P301-PR-UNREG-READBACK-FAIL, P301-PR-AUTHORITY-NOT-RETIRED. (6) mxfs_pal_scsi_pr_unregister() (the mxfs_bdev_t form) no longer open-codes its own copy -- it calls the bdev form. Two copies of this logic is how the defect came to exist on both paths. (7) The late-unregister caller (pal/linux/xfs_super.c, after xfs_shutdown_devices) now raises xfs_alert P301-DEPARTURE-INCOMPLETE naming the key and saying plainly that this initiator can still write to the shared LUN, instead of the old cosmetic xfs_notice.

RUN 2026-08-20T02:45:51Z, 32/caw on 0.14.11 sv 59F765EF4CFF9E513F37FE2, /dev/mapper/mpatha with 2 active paths, STARTING FROM AN EMPTY REGISTRATION TABLE (0 keys): ARM A, three clean mount/unmount round trips on test2 -- lap 1 table 0 -> 2 on mount (both nexuses, key 0xf60f4fd4) then 2 -> 0 on clean unmount; lap 2 0 -> 2 (0x50cfc8d5) -> 0; lap 3 0 -> 2 (0x9ebc497c) -> 0. 3/3. The immediately preceding run of the same harness on the same rig ALSO drove the table to 0 while clearing the last pre-fix leftover 0xa5c5a98f, which is how the historical debris was retired: its owner remounted (replacing the stale nexus entry with its new incarnation's key) and then departed properly. defects.residual: The ruling's items 1, 6, 7, 8 and 9 are NOT in this fix and are filed as their own entries: D-PR-RETIREMENT-FAILURE-NOT-FAIL-CLOSED-377 (no fail-closed action when retirement cannot be proved; no serialization against re-registration; no authorized survivor reaper for orphans) and D-PR-KEY-32BIT-NODE-ID-COLLISION-RISK-377 (the key is a 32-bit per-incarnation node_id). defects.found: sess377 RULE-5 ruling on D-CLEAN-UNMOUNT-LEAKS-PR-REGISTRATION-377; code state confirmed on 0.14.11
defects.summary: When MXFS cannot prove it retired its own PR registration at unmount, it LOGS AND CARRIES ON. The 0.14.11 fix makes the failure detectable (P301-PR-AUTHORITY-NOT-RETIRED / P301-DEPARTURE-INCOMPLETE) but nothing acts on it: the node finishes unmounting while its initiator may still be registered on the shared LUN, and no survivor is told. The RULE-5 ruling was explicit that this is not sufficient -- 'verify and log is not enough. The load-bearing invariant is that membership departure and PR authority retirement are coupled by either successful verification or an authorized fail-closed recovery action.' A stale registration on a LIVE initiator nexus can authorize non-filesystem I/O to the shared device even though MXFS is unmounted.
defects.mechanism: THREE GAPS, all present in 0.14.11. (a) NO FAIL-CLOSED ACTION. pal/linux/xfs_super.c's late unregister raises xfs_alert P301-DEPARTURE-INCOMPLETE and returns; put_super continues and the mount goes away. Nothing isolates the initiator sessions that could still use the registration, nothing self-fences, and no durable record hands the problem to an authorized survivor. (b) NO SERIALIZATION AGAINST RE-REGISTRATION. Nothing prevents a path addition, multipath recovery, or a userspace multipathd key replay from re-registering the departing key AFTER the verification succeeded. The verification is a point-in-time observation with no interlock. (c) NO AUTHORIZED REAPER FOR ORPHANS. A registration left by a pre-fix incarnation, or by a node whose path was unavailable during its unmount, stays forever: REGISTER-based deregistration can only act as the corresponding I_T nexus, so removing an inaccessible nexus's surviving registration requires an authorized PREEMPT from another nexus, and MXFS has no such path. Observed directly: key 0xa5c5a98f survived a full 32-node clean unmount and was only cleared when its owner happened to remount and depart again.
defects.evidence: Code state on 0.14.11 (the fail-closed branch simply does not exist), plus the sess377 rig observation that a pre-fix leftover key persisted across a complete 32-node clean unmount with no cluster-side reaction of any kind. The RULE-5 ruling text is in ccmemory ccloop-c7ee71c6-sess377-GPT-ruling3-pr-unregister-leak-fix-shape.
defects.next: 1. Implement the ruling's TWO-PHASE DEPARTURE: (i) EARLY, before the destructive teardown, publish a durable 'storage authority retirement pending' record; (ii) do all filesystem writes, flushes and DLM shutdown in the existing safe order (that ordering is load-bearing -- an earlier unregister fenced the node's own unmount log record on a WE-RO target, and an even earlier one made xfs_shutdown_devices' unconditional blkdev_issue_flush fail with a reservation conflict); (iii) at the final point unregister and verify; (iv) mark the record COMPLETE if the key is provably absent; (v) if present or unknown, LEAVE the record for an authorized recovery/fencing path and apply a local fail-closed policy. This avoids trying to rejoin the DLM or resurrect a superblock after late cleanup fails. 2. Choose the local fail-closed policy (RULE-5 consult first): tear down the initiator sessions that could use the registration, self-fence under cluster policy, or refuse to certify the incarnation as departed. Do NOT BUG_ON merely because storage is sick. 3. Serialize against re-registration for the departing key -- path addition, multipath recovery, multipathd replay, and any delayed registration work. 4. The orphan reaper belongs INSIDE the existing fencing/recovery state machine as 'complete storage revocation for certified-dead incarnation X', never as 'periodically remove keys I do not recognize'. Minimum authority: a committed fresh membership/recovery term; the same quorum MXFS already requires to fence; a DURABLE mapping from PR key to cluster/host/incarnation; proof the incarnation is excluded or its retirement was handed off; serialization against join/key allocation; a fence certificate covering the LUN and key; and verification after the PREEMPT that the key is absent. An unrecognized key with no trustworthy mapping must QUARANTINE and ALERT, not be preempted -- it could be a live node missing from a stale or partitioned view. 5. Verification: inject an unregister failure (there is a register-side twin, mxfs_dbg_pr_register_fail, to model) and assert (a) the loud marker fires, (b) the chosen fail-closed action actually happens, and (c) a survivor can find and complete the retirement from the durable record alone.
defects.containment: Detection only: P301-PR-AUTHORITY-NOT-RETIRED and P301-DEPARTURE-INCOMPLETE in the departing node's log, and 'chk_mxfs --pr-keys <dev>' from any node, which with the cluster fully unmounted must show an EMPTY table.
