defects.found: sess377 RULE-5 ruling; code: dlm/scsipr.c mxfs_scsipr_create()
defects.summary: The SCSI PR key is a 32-bit per-incarnation node_id (dlm/scsipr.c: ctx->local_key = (uint64_t)node_id), used in a 64-bit field. A PR key is the identity a fence acts on: PREEMPT AND ABORT names a key, and 'the victim's key is gone' is the exclusion proof the whole recovery protocol rests on. A 32-bit value that must stay unambiguous across reboots, historical leaks and the lifetime of a filesystem is weak for that job, and MXFS keeps no durable mapping from key to cluster/host/incarnation, so a key observed in the registration table cannot be attributed to anything with certainty.
defects.mechanism: ctx->local_key = node_id, a 32-bit per-incarnation value, zero-extended into the 64-bit PR key field -- so half the key space is structurally unused. Two distinct incarnations colliding on one node_id would be indistinguishable in READ KEYS, and a PREEMPT intended for one would remove the other. Observed per-incarnation churn on the rig: the same host was 0x7c11a613, then 0x9d0a1ad8, then 0x4c90ff23, 0x69b590aa, 0xd7a3b9ac, 0xf60f4fd4, 0x50cfc8d5, 0x9ebc497c across successive mounts -- a fresh value every time, drawn from a 32-bit space, with no durable record of which host or incarnation each belonged to.
defects.evidence: dlm/scsipr.c mxfs_scsipr_create(); the key values above read off the live rig with the new 'chk_mxfs --pr-keys'. RULE-5 ruling text in ccmemory ccloop-c7ee71c6-sess377-GPT-ruling3-pr-unregister-leak-fix-shape (answer to Q5).
defects.next: 1. KEEP the key PER-INCARNATION -- the ruling was explicit that a stable per-host key is worse here: an old and a newly booted incarnation would carry the same value, READ KEYS could not tell them apart, a PREEMPT meant for the old one would remove the NEW one, a fence certificate for the old incarnation would effectively authorize action against the current one, and a new registration would make an old leak look accounted for while two nexuses stayed registered. 2. WIDEN to a collision-resistant 64-bit incarnation identifier. Options from the ruling: a quorum-assigned monotonically unique 64-bit incarnation number; a random nonzero 64-bit value collision-checked against membership and the observed PR keys; or a 64-bit digest of {cluster UUID, stable host id, boot id, mount/incarnation counter}. 3. Add a DURABLE mapping 'PR key -> cluster UUID, host id, incarnation id, membership term' in the membership/recovery record. The key is an opaque identifier, not a security credential, and without the mapping no reaper or diagnostic can attribute an observed key. This mapping is also a hard prerequisite for the orphan reaper in D-PR-RETIREMENT-FAILURE-NOT-FAIL-CLOSED-377. 4. Use a stable host identity for administration and fencing-device selection, kept DISTINCT from the PR key. 5. Verification: assert no two live incarnations ever share a key; assert every observed key resolves through the durable mapping; and re-run tests/pr_departure.sh unchanged to prove the widening did not regress departure.
defects.containment: None. No collision has been observed; this is a structural weakness in the fencing identity.
defects.detector: chk_mxfs --pr-keys <dev> prints each key and the node_id it decodes to; two live nodes reporting the same key is the failure.

defects.opened: 2026-08-20 sess378 (ccloop c7ee71c6) - observed live on a healthy 32/caw cluster during a routine board run
defects.summary: A node takes a metadata READ error on a healthy, freshly-mkfs'd cluster and shuts the filesystem down, which cascades: every other node's coherency checks against its data then fail. test22 hit 'Metadata I/O Error (0x1) detected at xfs_trans_read_buf_map+0x178 (xfs/xfs_trans_buf.c:313)' inside an inode create, declared voluntary death, and turned a green board red.
defects.found: Live on the rig, 0.14.12 (sv BC7EF240AD75534328B5504), 32/caw, during board criterion cache_coherency. Not injected, not a fault test.
evidence: TIMELINE on a common wall clock derived from matched uptime<->realns pairs (dmesg -T and btime+uptime were ~5 s apart between these two nodes and INVERTED this ordering on the first attempt, so they are not usable here): 04:20:29.399Z test22 'XFS (dm-1): Metadata I/O Error (0x1) detected at xfs_trans_read_buf_map+0x178/0x320 [mxfs] (/src/mxfs/xfs/xfs_trans_buf.c:313). Shutting down filesystem.' -> P-WITHDRAW-QUEUE -> P163-WITHDRAW-STAMP slot=11 node=3671298124. 04:20:29.871Z test5 P236-FENCE-INTENT slot=11 victim=3671298124, i.e. 472 ms LATER. The fence is a CONSEQUENCE of the withdrawal, not its cause - the withdraw stamp is what tells peers to fence, so the fence cannot precede its own trigger.

The error surfaced inside an inode create: 'P-CREATE-ERR2 dir_create_child err=-5 t_dfops_empty=1 dp_ino=41943175 new_ino=46137488' then 'P-CR3-CANCEL error=-5 dp_ino=41943175 dialloc_ino=46137488 new_ino=46137488 trans_dirty=1 comm=bash', followed by three P-AGMETA-RECLAIM drops (xfs_agi, xfs_finobt, xfs_inobt).

Post-shutdown, reads of the same inodes report 'P9-ICD-MIDLOOP ino=46137487 imap_rc=-5 bp=0 plainrd_rc=0 magic=0x494e ... shutdown=1' - the PLAIN read of that location succeeds and carries a valid XFS_DINODE_MAGIC while the imap path returns -EIO. Those lines are AFTER the shutdown so the EIO there is expected; the valid magic is recorded only because it argues the on-platter content was intact.

BOARD IMPACT: cache_coherency FAILED nodes_pass=0/32 faildist[8x27,9x4,13x1] - 27 nodes failed 8 checks each, which are the cross-node checks against the departed node's data, so the coherency failure is the cascade rather than an independent fault. strong_consistency, posix_multi, mmap_coherency and zero_silent_loss then all reported 'pre-assert: mxfs not mounted/readable on test22'. A re-prep and re-run of the identical chunk on the identical build passed 8/8, so the trigger is intermittent - which under RULE 6 is a reason to instrument, never to dismiss.

NOT caused by the sess378 fence change: that change is confined to mxfs_pal_scsi_pr_preempt() with abort=true, which runs only in the fence path, and test22 logged no fence activity before its shutdown. A UNIT ATTENTION was seen on test22 (P-FUA-READ-RETRY lba=194241 ret=0x2 resid=8192 key=0x6 try=1) but only AFTER the shutdown, consistent with test5's subsequent preemption.

A SECOND, DIFFERENT shutdown the same session, recorded as a lead rather than a claim: test5 shut down at 04:00:50Z with 'Metadata I/O Error (0x1) detected at mxfs_dlm_fence_notify+0x53/0x80' - a SELF-FENCE on PR-key-lost - during a 32-node mass unmount, while the fleet was still running 0.14.11. Whether the two share a root is unknown.
defects.why_it_was_not_caught: It is intermittent, and it presents as a coherency failure on 31 innocent nodes, so the board's first_fail[] points at the cascade rather than at the node that actually died. Nothing in the harness attributes a multi-node coherency failure back to a single peer's shutdown.
defects.why_still_open: No root cause. It is not known what the failed metadata read was, whether the buffer was a real device read or a cached one, or whether the -EIO originated at the transport, at dm-multipath, or inside MXFS's own read path.
defects.next: 1) IDENTIFY THE BUFFER. xfs/xfs_trans_buf.c:313 is the failure site; add a marker there recording blkno, length, ops->name and bp->b_error/b_flags so the next occurrence names WHAT could not be read instead of only that something could not be. 2) DISCRIMINATE transport from filesystem: correlate the same instant against the node's own SCSI layer (sd errors, reservation conflict, UNIT ATTENTION sense key 0x6) and against clyde's SCST log; MXFS already logs P-FUA-READ-RETRY with the sense key, so record whether the failing read had exhausted its UA retries. clyde's host kernel is independently known to corrupt memory (ccmemory clyde-host-ext4-slab-corruption-kills-rig-nodes-sess377), so a transport-origin EIO must be excluded BY EVIDENCE, in either direction. 3) Establish whether a UNIT ATTENTION arising from ANOTHER node's PR preemption can surface as a metadata read EIO on an innocent registrant: SPC requires a UA (2Ah RESERVATIONS PREEMPTED) to be established for every other registrant when a preemption occurs, so every fence delivers one to all 31 survivors. If MXFS's metadata read path can turn that UA into -EIO instead of reissuing, then every fence risks shutting down innocent nodes - which would also be a candidate root for the sess378 test5 self-fence and for parts of the -474/-482 cascade families. 4) Reproduce under load with the marker armed: cache_coherency at 32/caw in a loop.

defects.summary: A single CAW slot is an O(N) cluster-wide serialization point, and MXFS puts the hottest inode in the filesystem (the mount ROOT directory) on one. When N nodes issue COMPARE AND WRITE against that one slot at the same time, the SCSI target - which must make CAW atomic - serializes every overlapping command on that LBA. Concurrent FUA reads of the same slot, which MXFS's inode-lock fast path issues for its ownership verify, queue behind the CAW chain, exceed the SCSI command timeout, and are killed by ABORT_TASK, costing a ~60s error-recovery cycle. MEASURED: a node that was NOT participating at all took 59,742 ms for `stat /mnt/shared` while `stat` of a DIFFERENT file on the SAME mount at the SAME moment took 3 ms. CONFIRMED per-LBA by direct SCSI READ(16)+FUA from a non-participant: 9,837 commands to the hot slot (worst 40,272 ms) interleaved one-for-one with 9,837 to a cold LBA on the same device and nexus (worst 39 ms).
defects.mechanism: SBC requires COMPARE AND WRITE to be atomic, so a target blocks commands that overlap an in-flight CAW range. MXFS's CAW DLM keeps each resource's holder bitmap in one 512B slot, so every node that holds, acquires, or releases a grant on inode X reads and CASes THE SAME LBA. For a resource N nodes share - the mount root above all, which every node caches at PR and every departing node clears at teardown (P109-CLR-RELEASE-ALL type=I id=128) - the offered load on that one LBA is O(N) CAWs plus O(N) FUA reads, all mutually serialized at the target. Past the target's service rate the queue exceeds the initiator's SCSI timeout; the initiator escalates to ABORT_TASK, and the EH cycle is what sets the ~60s quantum. This is the general form of the unmount symptom recorded as D-MASS-UMOUNT-ROOT-EX-SERIALIZE-100S-526B, and it is the leading candidate mechanism for the two ledgered pace defects on shared resources: D-32NODE-SHARED-DIR-CREATE-PACE (~42x cost at 32 nodes for concurrent create into ONE shared directory) and D-READDIR-PEER-CACHED-DIR-PACE.
defects.next: 1) PER-LBA ISOLATION IS DONE (sess379, tests/lba_probe.sh - see evidence[0]); what remains of the attribution is separating 'the CAWs block the reads' from 'this LBA's service rate is exceeded', and that is now the only open question about the mechanism. Remaining instrumentation, from the sess379 RULE-5 review (ccmemory ccloop-c7ee71c6-sess379-GPT-ruling-hot-slot-caw-fix-shape): (ii) Per-CDB initiator tracing: queued / dispatched / completed timestamps, opcode, LBA, tag, SCSI status and sense, host result, MISCOMPARE count, timeout callback, abort/TMF initiation and result, retry reason. That separates not-dispatched (software queue) from dispatched-late (fabric/target queue) from dispatched-never-completed from MISCOMPARE amplification. (iii) The single most informative A/B: a test knob allowing only ONE outstanding CAW per slot, everything else unchanged - if the aborts and the 60s events vanish, CAS concurrency is causal. (iv) A knob that skips ONLY the root release-all. (v) Replace the teardown CAWs with an equal-RATE read workload, which controls for offered command rate better than the current read-only control. 2) THE 60s QUANTUM IS A TIMEOUT CLIFF, NOT PROOF OF A LOST COMMAND: a timeout clips the tail of a queueing distribution into a fixed recovery penalty, which is why there is no middle ground. Determine whether the 60s is dispatch-to-timeout, post-timeout EH, or a sum of timers, and whether cold-LBA commands are (a) not dispatched at all = initiator queue quiesced, (b) dispatched but stalled = target/LUN-wide head-of-line blocking, or (c) completing normally = per-LBA serialization. 3) FIX ORDER FROM THE RULE-5 REVIEW: (a) membership departure LOGICALLY invalidates every grant of the fenced incarnation so stale bits never block progress, with cleanup lazy and single-owner - this removes work rather than scheduling it better and is the highest-value fix, BUT it is unsafe with node-ID-only bitmap semantics: holder state needs incarnation/epoch identity or node IDs must never be reused before a full purge, or a stale bit is read as a live holder after ID reuse. It also requires the departure ordering drain-then-resolve-ambiguous-commands-then-fence-then-publish-inactive; 'clear heartbeat then stop' is unsafe because a delayed CAW from the departed incarnation can execute after peers decide its bits are stale. (b) no storage poll on a cached serve, valid only once the lock cache is proven protected by revocation/lease/epoch. (c) per-slot CAW concurrency limit + batching as a compatibility guardrail, never the final architecture (a cluster-wide token in another CAW sector just moves the hot sector). (d) format change: a writer GATE record plus incarnation-tagged PER-NODE reader records - reader publishes then RE-READS the gate and only succeeds if it is still open at the same epoch; writer CASes the gate closed first, then scans reader records, so no coherent snapshot is needed. Trades an O(N^2) write storm for a bounded O(N) read scan on EX acquire. 4) BEWARE PURGE HERDING: if N departures make every survivor scan and clear the same records, the storm just moves to the survivors. 5) A timed-out or successfully aborted CAW may STILL have been applied at the target - every retry/recovery path must re-read and reconcile by epoch, never assume the write did not happen. 6) Re-measure D-32NODE-SHARED-DIR-CREATE-PACE and D-READDIR-PEER-CACHED-DIR-PACE with per-CDB tracing before assuming they share this root - the 42x create result is highly consistent with one directory lock record becoming an EX-transition hot spot, but the 1.2s readdir has several other candidate causes. 7) Acceptance: with N=32 nodes converging on one shared resource, no node's metadata operation on that resource may exceed 2x the same operation on an uncontended resource.
evidence:
SESS380 ROOT CAUSE, IN THIRD-PARTY CODE, WITH THE TRACE THAT PROVES IT. The 60 s quantum is a wait-for CYCLE in the SCST target's SCSI-atomic (COMPARE AND WRITE overlap) blocker graph. scst_check_scsi_atomicity() (scst/src/scst_targ.c) walked the WHOLE dev_exec_cmd_list and skipped only the command itself (`continue`, not `break`), so a command whose FIRST atomicity check is DEFERRED installs wait edges back to commands already blocked ON IT. The deferral is routine: scst_do_check_blocked_dev() appends the cmd to dev_exec_cmd_list BEFORE the atomicity check, and skips that check entirely when the cmd is not SCSI-atomic AND dev_scsi_atomic_cmd_active == 0 (leaving scsi_atomicity_checked == 0); if the cmd is then parked by a DEVICE block it STAYS on dev_exec_cmd_list, collects every overlapping CAW as a waiter, and runs its first check only on re-entry after the device unblocks -- at which point it blocks on its own waiters. Captured verbatim with TRACE_BLOCK on lba 155671 (the root inode's CAW slot):
  536846.409771  Device BLOCK (new count 1)
  536846.409778  Delaying cmd 48a9c59d due to blocking (tag 119, op READ(16))
  536846.409819  Delaying CAW 1d61a266 (blockers 1) due to overlap with 48a9c59d
  ... 5 more CAWs block on 48a9c59d ...
  536846.419048  Device UNBLOCK (new 0)
  536846.419053  Adding blocked cmd 48a9c59d to active cmd list
  536846.419087  Delaying cmd 48a9c59d (READ(16), blockers 1..5) due to overlap with
                 1d61a266, ff98f7ea, 0efda8f0, fca86073, 04c78c3a   <-- its own waiters
  536906.823647  Aborting cmd 48a9c59d ... state EXEC_CHECK_BLOCKING, proc time 60 sec
  536906.823672  Unblock aborted atomic-blocked cmd 48a9c59d
Corroborating aggregates over a 95 s window: the block/unblock accounting is EXACT, so it is not a leak (216 blocked commands = 204 normal unblocks + 12 abort-released; 90 device BLOCK / 90 UNBLOCK; 340 device-block parks / 340 reactivations; total device-blocked time only 0.512 s). And the wait distribution is strictly BIMODAL: p50 8 ms, p90 53 ms, then 4 samples in 0.1-1 s, 1 in 1-10 s, and 6 over 10 s with max 60.414 s. A queue whose median is 8 ms does not produce a 60 s tail out of 336 commands. It also explains the sess379 negative control exactly: with reads alone dev_scsi_atomic_cmd_active stays 0, so no atomicity check ever runs and no cycle can form. FIXED in scst 3.11.0-pre+caw-abort-reclaim.3 (edges installed only toward predecessors on the append-only list, so the graph is acyclic by construction; plus a dev_exec_seq stamp and a WARN_ONCE detector for non-backward edges). RULE-5 reviewed before landing.

SESS380 THE DECIDING A/B — ONE VARIABLE, THE TARGET MODULE. MXFS was NOT changed between the two columns: 0.15.4 srcversion DACACDDE464B211CF68DE3F on both, same 32 nodes, same harness invocation (tests/mass_umount_stall_probe.sh with DEPART_N=28 and DEPART_N=32). Only scst.ko/iscsi-scst.ko moved, from 3.11.0-pre+caw-abort-reclaim.2 to .3.
                                        scst .2        scst .3
  max umount wall, 28 of 32 depart      120.48 s       0.37 s   (8/32 over budget -> 0/28)
  max umount wall, 32 of 32 depart       60.65 s*      0.25 s   (*sess379 figure, 31/32 stalled)
  worst READ(16)+FUA on the hot slot     60,426 ms      59 ms
  worst COMPARE AND WRITE on it          60,415 ms      53 ms
  summed service time, that sector        719 s         2.1 s
  ABORT_TASK TMFs / abort-reclaims        12 / 12       0 / 0
Command COUNT on the sector was ~O(N) in both columns (336-561 across 32 nodes over the whole storm, ~26 per node), so this was never offered-load amplification; it was per-command stalling.

SESS379 CONCLUSIVE PER-LBA ISOLATION (tests/lba_probe.sh, the form the sess379 RULE-5 review prescribed after rejecting the stat()-based control). During a 28-of-32 simultaneous unmount, the non-departing node test32 issued DIRECT SCSI READ(16) with the FUA bit - the same opcode and transfer size MXFS uses for a slot read - alternating between two LBAs on the same /dev/sda, for 200s: HOT lba=175621 (the root inode's CAW slot, the LBA all 96 P-FUA-READ-RETRY lines that run named) n=9837 worst=40,272ms mean=10ms err=2; COLD lba=195621 (20,000 sectors away) n=9837 worst=39ms mean=4ms err=0. Same task, same nexus, same queue, commands interleaved one-for-one: 1,033x apart on the worst case and 2.5x on the mean. This eliminates the alternatives the review named - it is not 'the stat issued no command' (these are raw passthrough CDBs), not initiator queue quiescing (9,837 cold commands completed on the same queue throughout), not global LUN/target saturation (the LUN answered the cold LBA with a 4ms mean the whole time), and not fabric-wide head-of-line blocking (same nexus). ATTRIBUTION ESTABLISHED: the serialization is PER-LBA. Departing walls that run: 27 of 28 at 59.7-60.7s, one at 0.1s.

SESS379 THE PRIMARY MEASUREMENT (tests/mass_umount_stall_probe.sh, DEPART_N=28, 32/caw, 0.15.2 sv C46FD856C41CB8A33B1CB35). 28 of 32 nodes unmount simultaneously; test32 does NOT unmount and simply alternates two stats for 90s. Result: worst `stat /mnt/shared` (root dir, ino 128, the slot every departing node CAWs and reads) = 59,742 ms; worst `stat /mnt/shared/.mus_probe` (a different file, different slot) = 3 ms, over 18 alternating pairs. Same mount, same node, same code path, same 90s window. LIMIT OF THIS EVIDENCE, per the sess379 RULE-5 review: two stat() calls can differ in cache and lock state and in WHETHER THEY ISSUE A SCSI COMMAND AT ALL, so a 3 ms stat does not by itself prove that I/O to the other LBA was healthy. It is strong but not conclusive LBA isolation; the conclusive form is a direct READ(16) to a hot and a cold LBA issued during the storm with dispatch-to-completion timing (see 'next' item 1).

SESS379 SCALING IN THE NUMBER OF SIMULTANEOUS PARTICIPANTS (observers held at 32 where noted). 8 simultaneous departures of 32: 0/8 stalled, walls 0.07-0.21s. 24 simultaneous departures: 10/24 stalled at 60.27-60.36s, the other 14 at 0.10-0.34s. 28 simultaneous: 27/28 over budget, max 180.86s, mean 86.44s. 32 simultaneous: 31/32 stalled, max 60.65s. There is no middle ground in any run - a node either gets through in ~0.2s or eats whole ~60s units, which is the SCSI error-recovery quantum, not a queueing curve.

SESS379 TARGET-SIDE SIGNATURE. clyde runs SCST 3.11.0-pre+caw-abort-reclaim.2, i.e. WITH the known CAW<->READ scsi_atomic wedge fix, so this is not that infra bug. During the stall: 330 scst_abort_cmd and 165 ABORT_TASK task-management functions, continuous from storm+15s to storm+45s. During a control window with the same 32 nodes mounted and stat-storming: no target entries at all. PR is not the mechanism - only 32 READ KEYS in the whole stall window, no P301-PR-UNREG-* on any node, and the PR retirement loop (6 attempts / 20s deadline) succeeded on the first attempt everywhere.

SESS379 NEGATIVE CONTROL - READS ALONE DO NOT DO IT (tests/hotslot_contention.sh). 32 mounted nodes stat'ing the same mount root concurrently for 30s: 79,459 stats, worst 166 ms, mean 5 ms, zero P-FUA-READ-RETRY, zero P302/P303. The read half of the load on the SAME hot LBA by the SAME 32 nodes is harmless; it is the concurrent CAW traffic that changes the regime.
defects.harness: tests/mass_umount_stall_probe.sh <N> [BUDGET_S] with DEPART_N=<k> (k<N arms the non-departing observer that times the root slot against a different slot) and STAGGER_S=<s>; tests/hotslot_contention.sh <N> [SECONDS] [BUDGET_MS] for the read-only control. tests/lba_probe.sh <dev> <hot_lba> <cold_lba> <seconds> runs ON a node and times direct READ(16)+FUA against two LBAs alternately; get the hot LBA from the P-FUA-READ-RETRY lines of a prior storm, and remount WITHOUT re-mkfs (mount -t mxfs /dev/mapper/mpatha /mnt/shared) to keep the slot mapping stable between runs.
defects.disposition:
DISPROVED sess380 (RULE 6 disposition 1). Two independent measurements now score this entry's OWN stated acceptance bar -- 'with N=32 nodes converging on one shared resource, no node's metadata operation on that resource may exceed 2x the same operation on an uncontended resource' -- and both PASS, with no change to MXFS:
  (a) During a 28-of-32 unmount storm, the non-departing observer's worst `stat` of the CONTENDED mount root was 13 ms against a worst `stat` of an UNCONTENDED file of 8 ms, over 1417 alternating pairs = 1.6x. On the broken target the same probe read 59,742 ms vs 3 ms.
  (b) WITHDRAWN BY ME, SAME SESSION, BEFORE IT WAS RELIED ON. I first cited tests/create_scale_curve.sh's shared-vs-private create ratio (1377 ms vs 1121 ms = 1.23x at 32 participants) as a second acceptance measurement. It is NOT a valid one: that harness's `private` arm has every node run `mkdir -p $dirbase/r$i`, so all 32 nodes take the SAME parent directory inode EX inside the measured window. Both arms therefore contend on a shared directory and the ratio measures nothing about contended-vs-uncontended. The measurement stands as a fact about the two shapes; it is not evidence for this disposition. (a) alone carries it, and (a) is a clean control: two different inodes on the same mount, from the same task, alternating.
The paired direct-CDB control agrees: READ(16)+FUA to the hot slot n=4084 worst 68 ms mean 4 ms, against a cold LBA on the same nexus n=4084 worst 24 ms mean 4 ms (sess379 on the broken target: 40,272 ms vs 39 ms). The per-LBA serialization sess379 measured is REAL and is inherent to putting a shared resource on one sector -- but at 32 nodes it costs 1.2-1.6x, not 1,033x, and the 1,033x was the target's wait-for cycle. WHAT THIS DISPROOF DOES NOT COVER, deliberately: the 'fix order' and format-redesign guidance in this entry (gate + per-node reader records) remains sound engineering advice for scaling FAR past 32 nodes, and the standing hazards restated here -- an aborted CAW may still have been applied; FUA is not protocol ordering -- are correctness facts that survive this disposition. Re-open with a measurement, not with an argument, if a shared resource ever exceeds the 2x bar again.

SCOPE OF THIS DISPROOF -- READ BEFORE CITING IT. It says the PER-LBA COMMAND SERIALIZATION at the target is not an MXFS defect and now costs 1.6x. It does NOT say that contended shared resources are cheap in MXFS. Measured the same session on the same build and target: 32 nodes creating into ONE shared directory cost 1842 ms per node for 8 creates against 222 ms into genuinely private directories -- 8.3x on wall, 34x on p95 -- and a 776-sample blocking census puts 74.5% of that in the CAW inode-GRANT wait (mxfs_pal_cond_timedwait under caw_lock_body) against only 7.0% in the SCSI transport. That is the DLM's EX rotation among 32 contenders, it is a live RULE 0 violation, and it is tracked as D-32NODE-SHARED-DIR-CREATE-PACE (OPEN). Fixing the target moved the transport share DOWN from 14.2% to 7.0%; it did not touch the protocol cost.

defects.summary: THE FILESYSTEM BECOMES PERMANENTLY UNMOUNTABLE after a mass departure. Chain, all measured sess379: (1) a node's unmount stalls past its lease under D-MASS-UMOUNT-ROOT-EX-SERIALIZE-100S-526B, so peers declare a merely-SLOW node DEAD and start recovery; (2) the fence proves nothing - kind=NO_RESERVATION(8), because the LUN carries no WE-RO reservation at that moment, so exclusion is unprovable for every node, not just this victim; (3) the recovery guard is left at stage=1 with a LIVE owner that can never advance; (4) MXFS also retires the victim's PR key unconditionally at put_super, so the later PREEMPT AND ABORT has no key to preempt either; (5) the mount ADMISSION BARRIER then refuses EVERY new mount, permanently - it requires the slice to be REPLAYED and does not route around it to any of the 27 free slots. OBSERVED: 28 of 32 nodes could not rejoin their own filesystem, repeatedly over 10+ minutes, with 4 healthy peers mounted throughout. Only re-mkfs recovers it.
defects.mechanism: TWO INDEPENDENT WAYS TO REACH AN UNPROVABLE FENCE, both present here. (A) NO RESERVATION: dlm/scsipr.c's P-PR-NORESV branch refuses to call a deregistration a fence unless a WE-RO reservation is HELD - correctly, since without one an unregistered initiator writes freely. But nothing re-establishes the reservation when its holder departs, so a mass departure can leave the LUN unreserved and disarm fencing CLUSTER-WIDE. The sess378 admission check (P303-FENCECAP) validates 'WE-RO held' at MOUNT time only; it can evaporate afterwards with no detection. (B) SELF-RETIRED KEY: pal/linux/xfs_super.c ~1727 retires this node's PR registration unconditionally at put_super with no gate on whether its slice is clean, and that key is the only thing a survivor can PREEMPT AND ABORT to mint a certificate. dlm/scsipr.c ~441 then returns KEY_ABSENT_UNPROVEN forever - correct when a WINNER exists and published evidence, but here no peer ever fenced the victim, so nothing was ever published. The design handles a node that DIES (key still registered). A node that retires its key, or dies while the LUN is unreserved, falls in the hole. Note (B) collides head-on with D-CLEAN-UNMOUNT-LEAKS-PR-REGISTRATION-377, which made that unregister mandatory and fail-closed: one unconditional call cannot both retire write authority and leave a preemptable key behind.
defects.next: 0) ANSWERED sess381 - see sess381_step0_answered; arm (A) split out as D-PR-RESERVATION-SINGLE-HOLDER-UNMOUNT-DISARMS-FENCING-381 and D-FENCE-PRECONDITION-FAILURE-RECORDED-TERMINAL-381. THIS ENTRY IS NOW SCOPED TO ARM (B): the unconditional self-retirement of this node's own PR key at put_super with no gate on slice cleanliness. 1) RULE-5 consult on the resolution, because it collides head-on with D-CLEAN-UNMOUNT-LEAKS-PR-REGISTRATION-377. Candidate shapes to put to it: (a) gate the retirement on slice cleanliness - retire the key only once this node's slice is provably clean, and if it is dirty leave the key registered (write authority is already gone by other means: the heartbeat slot is released and the mount is down) so a survivor can still mint the certificate; (b) publish a SELF-departure fence certificate at teardown, so 'I retired my own key after quiescing' is itself consumable evidence of exclusion - this is attractive because the departing node is the one entity that can prove it stopped issuing I/O; (c) let the admission path treat 'victim key absent AND victim slot shows a completed clean-quiesce stamp' as proved, which needs the stamp to be durable and forgery-resistant; (d) an offline chk_mxfs repair for the already-bricked state, which is needed regardless of which of the above lands, because existing filesystems can already be in it. 2) The operator-facing text is actively WRONG in this state and must be fixed with the code: P300-CLAIM-WITHDRAWN prints 'All three are TRANSIENT - a live peer resolves them. Retry the mount rather than reformatting.' Nothing resolves this one. The admission abort likewise says 'fix the blocker (fence path, or the recovery's owner) and retry' without saying that no retry can ever succeed. A terminal state must be reported as terminal and must name the repair. 3) Determine how the dirty slice arose here so the trigger is characterised, not just the trap: all 28 departing nodes logged 'released heartbeat slot N (clean teardown)' and none of them held slot 9, so slot 9's occupant (node 2569023191) is an EARLIER incarnation - most likely a node that was rmmod'd and re-inserted during a prep whose own mass unmount hit D-MASS-UMOUNT-ROOT-EX-SERIALIZE-100S-526B and exhausted its rmmod retry budget. That path deserves its own trace. 4) Verification: force a node to depart with a dirty slice (forced shutdown mid-write) on an otherwise healthy cluster and assert that (i) a survivor mints a fence certificate and replays the slice, and (ii) a fresh mount is admitted - both WITHOUT re-mkfs. 5) chk_mxfs must classify a stuck RECOVERY GUARD separately from a terminal quarantine, stop printing the terminal-quarantine advice and the -376 repair pointer for it, and state the real impact (no mount is admitted at all, not 'one slot short').
evidence: SESS379 CORRECTION — THE OPERATIVE FAILURE IS *NO RESERVATION*, NOT THE ABSENT VICTIM KEY. The recovery owner's own journal (test30 = 3668433354) names it exactly, and it also shows the trigger chain: 07:21:36 node 2569023191 (192.168.120.107) joins, 07:21:37 lease ACTIVE; 07:22:14 the 28-of-32 unmount storm starts; 07:24:19 'node 2569023191 (slot 9 inc 7860688283116785074) LEASE EXPIRED/DIED - fencing; recovery starting'; 'P236-FENCE-INTENT ... fencing intent is DURABLE; the PREEMPT AND ABORT may now be issued'; then 'P236-FENCEKIND node=2569023191 kind=NO_RESERVATION(8) proves_excl=0 gen=15402 rc=0' and 'P238-FENCE-UNPROVEN slot=9 ... kind=NO_RESERVATION(8) - the fencing attempt is durable but proved NO exclusion, so this slice may not be replayed, its grants may not be released and its sector may not be zeroed. Recovery is BLOCKED on unproven exclusion'; 'P164-DEAD-NOTE'; 'P163-RECOVERY-PENDING slot=9'. NO_RESERVATION(8) is dlm/scsipr.c's P-PR-NORESV branch, which fires BEFORE the victim-key test: 'A reservation must be HELD for deregistration to exclude anyone. Under WE-RO the target rejects writes from non-registrants at command-processing time - but only while the reservation exists.' The on-disk guard agrees: resv_type=0x00. So at the moment of the fence the LUN carried NO WE-RO reservation at all, which makes fencing impossible for EVERY node, not just this victim. (On a healthy 32-node cluster a reservation IS held - verified after the re-prep: `sg_persist --in --read-reservation` returns Key=0x908cbcdd, LU_SCOPE, 'Write Exclusive, registrants only', with 64 keys registered. So the reservation is established in normal operation and was LOST across the mass departure.) The absent victim key is real and still blocks the LATER retries from the mounting node, but the first and load-bearing failure is the missing reservation.

SESS379 DIRECT CAPTURE, 32/caw, 0.15.3 sv 4160A71E7B8987119991EA4. After a 28-of-32 mass unmount, every one of the 28 nodes fails to remount. test1 dmesg, repeated on every attempt: 'mxfs: P163-RECOVERY-PENDING slot=9 node=2569023191 epoch=7860688283116785074 - purge deferred until slice replay completes'; 'disklock: P236-CLAIM-UNCERTIFIED slot=9 victim=2569023191 stage=1 kind=0 - fencing ATTEMPT only - no exclusion has been proved yet; refusing the claim. Nothing on this slice may be replayed, purged, repaired or published'; 'MXFS mount recovery: slice slot=9 NOT replayed (-1)' x4 rounds; then 'MXFS mount ABORTED: slot mask 0x200 still requires recovery after 4 inline replay round(s) and 30000 ms' and 'MXFS mount recovery barrier failed'.

SESS379 THE VICTIM'S KEY IS PROVABLY ABSENT. victim node_id 2569023191 = key 0x99202ed7. `sg_persist --in --read-keys /dev/sda` from a live node returns PR generation=0x3ca0 and exactly 8 keys - 0xb0560b70, 0xf7bf8b5d, 0x62722b3a, 0xdaa7d9ca, each twice (4 live nodes x 2 nexuses, test29-test32). 0x99202ed7 is not among them. Every other fence precondition is satisfied on the mounting node, which logs 'P303-FENCECAP-OK ... WE-RO held, persistence active, key view complete, own key present, PREEMPT AND ABORT issuable' - so the ONLY thing missing is the victim's key.

SESS379 IT IS PERMANENT, NOT TRANSIENT. The first failure and a fresh attempt ~10 minutes later produce byte-identical output, with 4 healthy peers (test29-test32) mounted throughout. Those peers' logs show P163-CLEAN-DEPART for the departing slots and NOTHING for slot 9 - no live peer ever takes ownership of it. An earlier attempt during prep additionally hit 'P300-CLAIM-EXHAUSTED no free heartbeat slot in 0..31 ... 31 live member(s), 0 quarantined, 0 withdrawn, 1 recovery lease(s) in progress', i.e. the stuck slot also consumes the last free slot at full fleet size.

SESS379 THE CODE IS UNCONDITIONAL. pal/linux/xfs_super.c:~1727 calls mxfs_pal_scsi_pr_unregister_bdev(bt_bdev, pr_late_key) at the end of xfs_fs_put_super with no test of slice state; its only failure handling is the P301-DEPARTURE-INCOMPLETE alert for the case where the key could NOT be retired. Success - the case that bricks the filesystem - is silent.

SESS379 ON-PLATTER FORENSICS (`tools/chk_mxfs -Q /dev/mapper/mpatha`, run from an unmounted node while the 4 survivors stayed up). volume uuid 6a3ba934-1654-419d-be5f-71067d3f9dbb, 32 log slices. 'heartbeat slot 9: RECOVERY GUARD -- sector identity node=2569023191 fs_gen=0xCD02AC7F incarnation=7860688283116785074; victim node=2569023191 incarnation=7860688283116785074 slot=9 slice=9 of 32; recovery owner=3668433354 term=0 gen=1 stage=1 flags=0x0; fence certificate kind=0 resv_type=0x00 victim_key=0x0000000099202ED7 prover=3668433354 term=1'. Three things this settles: (1) the guard is explicitly NOT a terminal quarantine - the tool itself prints 'this guard is NOT quarantined - it is a recovery in progress'; (2) its recovery OWNER, node 3668433354, is test30, which was MOUNTED AND HEALTHY the entire time - so this is not an orphaned lease from a dead owner, it is a live owner stuck at stage=1 with fence certificate kind=0 (MXFS_FENCE_KIND_NONE) and never making progress; (3) the victim_key recorded in the guard is 0x99202ED7, exactly the key that READ KEYS shows is no longer registered - the guard is waiting on a preempt that can never be issued. Summary line: live members 4, released slots 27 (clean departures), withdrawn slices 0, unreadable sectors 0, usable RW slices 31 of 32.

SESS379 THE DIAGNOSTIC MISREPORTS IT, AND POINTS AT THE WRONG REPAIR. In the SAME output whose detail section says the guard is NOT quarantined, chk_mxfs's summary counts it as 'quarantined verdicts 1', prints the terminal-quarantine advice ('A quarantined slice's committed transactions were never applied and cannot be applied safely ... DO NOT reformat'), and names D-QUARANTINED-SLOT-EXHAUSTS-CLUSTER-ADMISSION-376 as the tracking defect for a repair that 'is not implemented yet'. Neither the classification nor the named repair fits a stuck in-progress recovery guard. It also understates the impact by an order of magnitude: 'usable RW slices 31 of 32 ... the cluster runs that many members short' describes losing ONE slot, whereas the measured effect is that NO node can mount at all, because the admission barrier requires slot mask 0x200 to be REPLAYED before it will admit any mount - it does not route around the stuck slice to one of the 27 free slots. (Tool binary in the tree reported v0.14.11 while the module was 0.15.3, so re-check against a rebuilt chk_mxfs before treating the wording as current.)
defects.sess381_step0_answered: SESS381 STEP 0 IS ANSWERED, BY DIRECT MEASUREMENT, AND ARM (A) IS NOW ITS OWN ENTRY. Who owns the WE-RO reservation: ONE node - PRIN READ FULL STATUS on the healthy 32-node cluster returned holder_key=0x524c049d, iqn=...:test1-mxfs-node, i.e. a single I_T nexus, with 63 other registrations that are NOT holders. What happens when that node departs: the reservation is RELEASED. Measured - test1 `umount /mnt/shared` (real 0m0.056s, 0.49s wall) took the LUN from 'holder_key=0x524c049d ... keys=64 distinct=32' to 'NONE HELD keys=62 distinct=31', with 31 nodes still mounted and registered, and it stayed NONE HELD across a 30s poll. Why the LUN was unreserved at 07:24:19 in the sess379 capture: because the node that happened to hold the reservation was among the 28 that unmounted, and SPC-4 releases a *_REGISTRANTS_ONLY reservation when the holder's registration is removed - which MXFS does unconditionally at put_super. So YES: fencing is disarmed cluster-wide by the departure of one specific node, and the mass departure was never necessary - one routine clean unmount does it. The consequence was then proven end-to-end on the same rig: a later `virsh destroy` of a different node produced 'P236-FENCEKIND kind=NO_RESERVATION(8) proves_excl=0' from the elected prover and left the filesystem permanently unmountable. Tracked as D-PR-RESERVATION-SINGLE-HOLDER-UNMOUNT-DISARMS-FENCING-381 (root + the self-fulfilling P303-FENCECAP gate) and D-FENCE-PRECONDITION-FAILURE-RECORDED-TERMINAL-381 (why a transient disarm becomes permanent). Harnesses: tests/pr_reservation_ownership_probe.sh, tests/pr_all_registrants_semantics.sh. THIS ENTRY RETAINS arm (B) - the unconditional self-retirement of the node's own PR key at put_super while its slice may be dirty, which is a separate hole: it removes the only key a survivor could PREEMPT AND ABORT. Note the sess381 fix direction (WE-AR, all-registrants) does NOT close arm (B): under WE-AR the reservation survives, but a node that retires its key and leaves a dirty slice still leaves nothing to preempt. Arm (B) still needs its own resolution (candidate shapes (a)-(d) below).

defects.summary: A node takes a DIRECTORY SCAN MISS storm and then shuts the filesystem down with a DIRTY transaction cancel during create. On a 32/caw dlm_scaling run, test11 logged 135+ P26-DSCAN-MISS lines for one directory (ino=20971688) - live dirents the scan walked past but could not find in ANY data block - then two DLM inode lock failures with rc=-35 (EAGAIN), then P-CR3-CANCEL error=-117 (EUCLEAN) dp_ino=58720421 trans_dirty=1 comm=python3, which shut the mount down and drove a voluntary withdrawal (P-WITHDRAW / P163-WITHDRAW-STAMP slot=14 node=29110068). dlm_scaling scored 31/32 (test11 checks=6 passed=4 failed=2) and the NEXT criterion in the chunk, rsync_paired, failed its precondition outright because test11 was no longer mounted. One node's directory-coherency failure therefore takes the node down AND cascades to the following test.
defects.mechanism: NOT ESTABLISHED. What the evidence orders: (1) a directory's live dirents become unfindable in its data blocks on this node while the scan still counts them (P26-DSCAN-MISS reports scanned=127..135 with ndb=1, i.e. the scan saw >=135 live dirents but the single data block did not contain the name it was looking for); (2) DLM inode acquires on unrelated inodes start returning -EAGAIN; (3) a create's transaction is cancelled DIRTY with -EUCLEAN, which is a structure-integrity verdict, not an I/O error. The EUCLEAN distinguishes this from D-CREATE-METADATA-READ-EIO-NODE-SHUTDOWN-378, whose P-CR3-CANCEL carries an EIO from a metadata READ. Whether the DSCAN-MISS storm is the cause of the EUCLEAN or another symptom of the same underlying directory-image divergence is open.
defects.next: 1) REPRODUCE. It did NOT reproduce on an immediate re-run (same build, same target, fresh prep_cluster: dlm_scaling 32/32 PASS, rsync_paired 32/32 PASS), so this is intermittent - which RULE 6 explicitly does not accept as a reason to close. Loop dlm_scaling at 32/caw until it recurs, with the ring preserved: prep_cluster CLEARS every node's dmesg, so a failure whose evidence is only in the ring is LOST the moment the next prep runs. Capture per-node dmesg to a file inside the loop, before any re-prep. 2) TIMING IS A LIVE SUSPECT. This appeared on the FIRST 32/caw board run after the SCST target fix (+caw-abort-reclaim.3, sess380) removed a 60s command-stall quantum from the shared LUN - a roughly 200x change in worst-case DLM slot I/O latency. The immediately preceding board on 0.15.3 against the BROKEN target was 27/27. A latent race that the old target's stalls masked is the leading hypothesis and should be tested by re-running the same criterion many times on the fixed target, not by A/B-ing the target back (the old target is a known-defective stack). 3) The MXFS delta between the green board and this one is instrumentation only (0.15.3 -> 0.15.4: caw_watch_* counters, default OFF via caw_watch_slot=-1, plus a P380-RA-CASRETRY pr_warn that fires only in release_all at unmount). Confirm that by re-running the failing criterion on 0.15.3 against the FIXED target - that isolates target-vs-MXFS. 4) Decide the relationship to D-FDW-REJOIN-BNOBT-OVERLAPPING-FREE-SHUTDOWN-376, which is the other ledgered P26-DSCAN-MISS producer, and to D-CREATE-METADATA-READ-EIO-NODE-SHUTDOWN-378, which is the other P-CR3-CANCEL shutdown. 5) CONTAINMENT IS A SEPARATE DEFECT-SHAPED FACT worth recording either way: one node's shutdown made the NEXT criterion fail its precondition. A withdrawn node is not re-admitted by the harness between criteria, so any single-node shutdown mid-board scores every following criterion in that chunk as a failure.
evidence: SESS380 THE OCCURRENCE. 32/caw, MXFS 0.15.4 sv DACACDDE464B211CF68DE3F, SCST target 3.11.0-pre+caw-abort-reclaim.3, board chunk 2 (dlm_fairness dlm_membership scaling_curve dlm_scaling rsync_paired) run immediately after a clean prep_cluster (52s, all 32 nodes converged active_count=32). Result line: 'FAIL dlm_scaling (nodes_pass=31/32 states:FAIL=1 hostload=23.98 first_fail[test11:checks=6 passed=4 failed=2] rank1[checks=7 passed=7 failed=0] faildist[2x1]) [16s/90s]' followed by 'FAIL rsync_paired (pre-assert: mxfs not mounted/readable on test11)'. dlm_fairness, dlm_membership and scaling_curve all PASSed 32/32 in the same chunk.

SESS380 TEST11 KERNEL RING, verbatim tail (the node was NOMOUNT when queried):
[16724.840598] mxfs: P26-DSCAN-MISS ino=20971688 ndb=1 scanned=127 name="node11_data1.md5" (not in any data block; scanned=#live dirents seen - ~200=>match/encoding bug, <200=>under-read)

defects.summary: A NODE KILLS ITSELF BECAUSE A RECOVERABLE CONDITION IS ESCALATED AS AN UNPROVABLE RELEASE. When a node's in-core inode core is BEHIND the on-disk image, mxfs_inode_relog correctly refuses to write it back (P189-RELOG-BEHIND-DISK, 'refusing to re-log it over a peer's newer image'). That refusal is COMMON and normally recovers -- 77 of them in one clean 80s run with no ill effect. But when it does NOT recover, the inode's pending change never becomes durable, the release obligation MXFS_RELCAUSE_OBLIG_OPEN ('pending != durable') never clears, badness can never fall, and the release-defer episode's no-progress bound expires. mxfs_inode_wedge then PINS the grant on disk, closes admission for that resource permanently, and force-shuts-down the whole mount -- because it cannot tell 'we could not PROVE the release' from 'we were not ALLOWED to write our copy'. THREE of 32 nodes did this in one ag_strand_repair run, all on the SAME inode, with identical cause bits: test9 tries=979, test19 tries=999, test28 tries=1014, every one 'causes=0x1 badness=4 pin_rc=0 teardown=0', each after 122 BEHIND-DISK refusals.
defects.mechanism: The deadlock is a cycle of two correct-in-isolation rules. (1) P189-RELOG-BEHIND-DISK refuses the re-log because the in-core di_changecount is exactly ONE behind the platter's (incore[nlink=11 chg=68 size=101 fmt=1] vs disk[nlink=11 chg=69 size=101 fmt=1]) -- a peer published a newer image while this node held a dirty in-core copy, and writing it back would be a lost update. Correct. (2) mxfs_inode_defer_note computes causes=MXFS_RELCAUSE_OBLIG_OPEN (xfs_mxfs_dlm.h:878, 'pending != durable') because the in-core change is still pending, and mxfs_inode_defer_badness maps that single bit to badness 4. The episode only records PROGRESS when badness DECREASES (xfs_mxfs_dlm.c:15374), and badness cannot decrease while the relog is refused, so mxfs_inode_episode_expired_locked eventually fires. mxfs_inode_wedge (xfs_mxfs_dlm.c:15399-15439) then does exactly what it was designed to do for an UNPROVABLE release -- mxfs_v5_dlm_inode_pin, MXFS_RELSTATE_WEDGED, and xfs_force_shutdown(SHUTDOWN_META_IO_ERROR) -- but this release is not unprovable, it is merely UNRELOGGABLE, and the correct action is to DISCARD the stale in-core core and reload the peer's newer image, which is the very thing mxfs_dlm_reload_inode exists to do. Being behind the platter is a NORMAL outcome of cross-node sharing, not a fault, so the wedge/shutdown is a category error. Post-shutdown the node loops P9-ICD-MIDLOOP with imap_rc=-5 forever.

Guard it with an assertion that the canonical image is unchanged across a pipe re-log. THEN the EX-reacquisition state machine for a genuine SELFAHEAD (retain the obligation, request EX holding no folio/txn/DLM locks, reload AFTER the grant, then publish / close-superseded / fence) instead of pinning the whole mount over one inode.

defects.sess382_mechanism_proven: SESS382 — MECHANISM PROVEN END TO END, AND THE DISCRIMINATOR THE ENTRY ASKED FOR IS ANSWERED. The defect is NOT specific to P189-RELOG-BEHIND-DISK; that is one instance of a GENERIC chain. (1) xfs_iflush has ELEVEN 'safe skip' fences that abandon the flush with `error = 0; goto flush_out;` (P119-NONEX-FLUSH-SKIP, P17B-EPOCH-GHOST-SKIP, P25-RESURRECT-SKIP, P32F-NXSHRINK-FENCE, P32D-DEADINCARN-SKIP, P32E-DIREPOCH-FENCE, P67-IFLUSH-OWNER-FENCE, P65-IFLUSH-FENCE, P14-SFSIZE-DESYNC, P32-IFLUSH-NXSHRINK, and the P189 arm in the drain itself). NONE of them stamps i_mxfs_pub_flush_seq. (2) The publication obligation is pending_seq != durable_seq, and durable only advances at xfs_iflush_finish from flush_seq — so a fenced flush leaves the obligation PERMANENTLY open. (3) The release drain then re-logs the clean-but-unlanded core (P146V-UNLANDED), which calls xfs_trans_log_inode, which INCREMENTS pending_seq (xfs/libxfs/xfs_trans_inode.c:116). THE DRAIN'S OWN REPAIR ACTION FEEDS THE COUNTER IT IS WAITING ON. (4) Badness stays pinned at 4 (OBLIG_OPEN alone), the episode records progress only on a badness DECREASE (xfs_mxfs_dlm.c:15374), the 60s no-progress bound expires, and mxfs_inode_wedge pins the grant and force-shuts-down the WHOLE MOUNT. THE DISCRIMINATOR ('what distinguishes the 77 that recovered from the 122 that did not'): the ONLY path that reconciles the ledger is the adopt inside mxfs_dlm_reload_inode (xfs_mxfs_dlm.c:26401, durable = pending, reporting P177-OBLIGATION-DROPPED-AT-ADOPT when a committed change is being dropped), and i_dlm_stale has NO RELEASE-PATH CONSUMER — it is honored only by ACCESS paths (xfs_iget/lookup xfs_inode.c:1630-1711, readdir). Recovery therefore depends on an unrelated LOCAL READER touching the inode inside the 60s window. Inodes that only the release machinery touches wedge. This matches sess380's own note that the wedged inode's only prior mention was a peer BAST 175s earlier.

defects.sess382_p32e_contract_hole_fixed_but_DIS: SESS382 — A REAL CONTRACT VIOLATION WAS FOUND AND FIXED, AND THEN DISPROVED AS THE CAUSE. Reading the code: xfs/xfs_mxfs_dlm.h:231 states that BOTH consumers of the dir-epoch staleness predicate — 'the P32E flush fence in xfs_inode.c and the P194/P195 operation gate in libxfs/xfs_dir2.c' — MUST go through mxfs_dir_epoch_superseded(), because a raw 'cur_ep > i_dlm_dir_valid_epoch' compares a DEAD incarnation's handoff lineage against a LIVE incarnation's baseline. Of the three call sites, libxfs/xfs_dir2.c:812 and the P32F arm at xfs_inode.c:7783 used the predicate; the P32E fence THE HEADER IS NAMED FOR did not — it extern-declared the predicate at xfs_inode.c:7851 and then compared raw. xfs_inode.h:253 explicitly records that this fence 'skipped every flush of B and its mkdir was silently lost'. FIXED in 0.17.5: the site now calls the predicate, with a new P32E-RAWDIVERGE probe that fires when the raw compare would have fenced and the predicate does not. DISPROVED AS THE WEDGE CAUSE, by measurement: a FULL aged board at stock knobs across 32 nodes gave P32E-DIREPOCH-FENCE=14 and P32E-RAWDIVERGE=0. RAWDIVERGE is (raw && !sup), so zero divergences across 14 firings proves the predicate and the raw compare agreed on EVERY evaluation at that site; the patch is behaviorally a no-op there. The reason is visible in the same sweep: P211-EPOCH-REBASE=81 fired from the dir2.c OPERATION gate, which normalizes valid_epoch before xfs_iflush ever runs. The patch is retained (it closes a documented hole at zero cost; full board 25 PASS / 0 FAIL / 1 policy cell on 0.17.5) but it is NOT credited with fixing this defect.
defects.sess382_gpt_ruling_fix_shape: SESS382 RULE-5 RULING ON FIX SHAPE (ccmemory sess382-inode-wedge-mechanism-proven-and-deterministic-reproducer). REJECTED: a bare 'durable_seq = pending_seq' at the fence — it conflates 'written durably' with 'cancelled/superseded' and launders a real unlanded committed update, converting a VISIBLE self-shutdown into SILENT metadata loss. REJECTED: calling mxfs_dlm_reload_inode INLINE at the fence — the drain is a documented ABBA site that takes folio locks while a parked writeback submitter waits on our demote. REQUIRED SHAPE: (a) a separate resolved frontier i_mxfs_pub_resolved_seq plus an explicit outcome (DURABLE / SUPERSEDED / REPLAYED / UNRESOLVED_CONFLICT), with the release predicate becoming 'pending != resolved' and durable_seq NEVER advanced for a non-durable resolution; (b) the abandonment given its OWN release-cause bit, not MXFS_RELCAUSE_OBLIG_OPEN, so the terminal probe names it and so badness can fall when a reload lands; (c) the reload driven from a RELEASE-SIDE WORKER outside the drain context; (d) the existing access-adopt reconcile at xfs_mxfs_dlm.c:26401 changed to use the same explicit resolver instead of its current silent 'durable = pending', which is the same concealed hole in the reader-assisted path; (e) INFLIGHT (flush_seq == pending) resolvable by waiting for the EXACT outstanding I/O and revalidating the platter; (f) UNCOPIED (flush_seq < pending) resolvable ONLY with a subsumption or ancestry proof — an unproved UNCOPIED committed update MUST still pin/fence. Note the observed case is cls=UNCOPIED, so a correct fix does NOT simply stop the wedge; it stops the FALSE wedges and names the true ones.
defects.sess382_fix_landed: SESS382 FIX LANDED 0.18.2 sv 89F66602EBFA099CE4E9281 — STILL OPEN, see sess382_residual for why. THREE CHANGES, each targeting a proven link in the chain. (A) THE SINGLE CHOKEPOINT FOR AN ABANDONED PUBLICATION. xfs_iflush's flush_out label now sets a new ip->i_mxfs_pub_fenced when it is about to return SUCCESS having NOT stamped i_mxfs_pub_flush_seq while pending != durable. That is exactly the abandoned-publication condition, it is checked in ONE place instead of at each of the eleven fences, and it automatically covers any fence added later. (B) A RELEASE-SIDE CONSUMER FOR IT. mxfs_dlm_bast_dwork_fn — the release retry worker, which is OUTSIDE the drain and therefore not the documented ABBA site that takes folio locks — now drives mxfs_dlm_reload_inode for a fenced publication before the deadline check that would wedge. It NEVER touches durable_seq directly and invents no 'superseded' verdict: it calls the same adopt every access path already calls, so the same keep-guards (P3 changecount time-travel, P33/P43, P177 obligation merge, P34J demote-wait) remain the sole authority on whether the platter image may be installed, and a dropped committed change is still reported by P177-OBLIGATION-DROPPED-AT-ADOPT rather than laundered. Bounded at MXFS_RELDEFER_RELOAD_MAX=3 per episode; if the adopt bails the obligation stays open and the wedge still fires, so the fail-closed escalation is preserved and only its FALSE firings are removed. Progress is restamped ONLY on an actual close, so a bailed adopt cannot buy time. New probe P382-RELDEFER-RELOAD. A/B lever mxfs.reldefer_reload (1=fix, 0=pre-fix control). (C) THE COUNTER RUNAWAY. xfs_trans_log_inode no longer increments pending_seq when i_mxfs_pipe_relog is set — the drain's own gated re-log re-logs the SAME core purely to get it flushed and represents no new committed change. Counting it made the obligation UNCLOSEABLE: every retry pushed pending past whatever the eventual flush could stamp, so flush_seq < pending held permanently and the state read cls=UNCOPIED forever. ALSO FIXED, a bug in the fix itself found by reading the init path: xfs_inode_alloc uses kmem_cache_alloc and NOT zalloc, so i_mxfs_pub_fenced and i_mxfs_reldefer_reloads had to join the explicit reset block at mxfs dlm inode init or a recycled inode would inherit a previous incarnation's fence verdict and reload budget.

Natural-fence engagement across a full board fell from 199 firings (first, over-broad i_dlm_stale trigger) to 9 with the chokepoint trigger, while P228-RELBAR-DEFER went 19 -> 0 and P176-OBLIGATION-OPEN 17 -> 0.
defects.sess382_residual: SESS382 WHY THIS STAYS OPEN — THE GAP I CANNOT CLOSE WITH WHAT I MEASURED. In all NINE natural firings of P382-RELDEFER-RELOAD across a full 32-node board, the line reads closed=0: the adopt BAILED on its keep-guards and the obligation was NOT reconciled (e.g. 'ino=71841303 n=2/3 stale_src=5 pend=18->18 dur=16->16 closed=0'). The fix is therefore PROVEN against the INJECTED cause — where the inode is otherwise healthy so the adopt succeeds — but its efficacy on the NATURAL trigger is UNPROVEN. Nothing wedged in those nine cases, but nothing needed to: P228-RELBAR-DEFER was 0, i.e. no release was even deferred, so the obligation resolved by a later ordinary flush rather than by the reload. If a natural fence were PERMANENT and the adopt bailed, this fix would not prevent the wedge — it would add three reload attempts and then wedge, which is the designed fail-closed behaviour but is NOT a fix for the reported defect. Closing on the injected arm alone would be exactly the 'clean run / plausible explanation' disposition RULE 6 forbids. NEXT STEP TO CLOSURE: determine WHICH keep-guard bails in the natural case and whether it would bail in the wedge case. Instrument mxfs_dlm_reload_inode's bail points with a reason code and surface it in P382-RELDEFER-RELOAD (the candidates are named in the mxfs_dir_adopt_at_acquire contract block: P3 changecount time-travel, P33/P43 fmt/grow revert, P177 obligation merge, P34J demote-wait — and P34J is the prime suspect since the reload runs while a demote is active). If the bail is P34J, the reload must be sequenced against the demote rather than skipped, which is the sess382 GPT ruling's 'drain/cancel old-epoch I/O, THEN resolve, THEN release' ordering. Verify any change with BOTH arms of tests/iflush_fence_wedge.sh AND a natural-fence board sweep showing closed=1.
defects.sess382_natural_population_characterized: SESS382 — WHAT THE NATURAL FENCE-ABANDONED PUBLICATIONS ACTUALLY ARE, measured, and it REDIRECTS the design away from the equality-close the sess382 ruling-2 Q2 proposed. Built a canonical equality oracle (mxfs_home_equals_owed in xfs_inode.c) that compares gen, changecount, mode, nlink, uid, gid, size, nblocks, extsize, flags, flags2, forkoff, format and the LOCAL data/attr fork BYTES, and FAILS CLOSED on anything it cannot compare in full (EXTENTS and BTREE forks are refused outright — an approximate fork comparison is exactly the mistake being corrected). Wired to TELEMETRY ONLY (probe P383-HOME-VS-OWED, knob mxfs.home_equals_owed_probe) so a bug in the oracle cannot produce a false durable-close while it is validated. MEASUREMENT 1, full 32-node board on 0.19.0: 29 of 29 natural fence-abandoned publications reported equal=0 why=gen — the platter dinode belongs to a DIFFERENT INCARNATION than our in-core image. NONE was equality-closeable. So the Q2 equality-close path would never fire naturally and building it out is not the way to close this defect. MEASUREMENT 2, probe extended with the fields that actually discriminate (i_generation is get_random_u32, so the two gens do NOT order — they only say 'different'), dir_reuse_coherency + dirent_durability + ag_strand_repair on 0.19.1: 41 of 41 events share ONE shape — 'ino=12583049 equal=0 why=gen pend=4 dur=2 flush=2 cc_home=2 iver=4 mode=00 dmode=0 gen_incore=1295308233 gen_home=1295308232 hmode=0100600 hnlink=0 unpub=0 selfcr=1 deadgen=0 stale_src=5 relst=0 comm=xfsaild/dm-1'. Read it: our in-core mode is 0 (the inode was FREED here), our gen is EXACTLY ONE above the platter's (the free bumped it), and the platter still holds the PRIOR incarnation as a live regular file (hmode=0100600). xfsaild is trying to destage the free while this node holds no grant (dmode=0), so P119-NONEX-FLUSH-SKIP fences it. CONCLUSION: the natural fence-abandoned population is dominated by FREED-INODE DESTAGE AT NL, not by the stale-shell/behind-disk shapes this entry was opened on. Those are GENUINE owed publications — the platter really does lack our freed image — so equality is CORRECTLY refused, and they resolve on their own (board green, only 6 P382-RELDEFER-RELOAD firings, zero wedges). The wedge only appears when such an owed publication can never resolve, which is exactly what the fault injection models and what the landed fix handles. Cross-check this population against D-CROSSNODE-OPEN-UNLINK-DATA-LOSS and the P128-INACT-DEFER machinery before designing anything further.
defects.sess382_q1_changecount_fix_verified: SESS382 SECOND SELF-INFLICTED LOOP — FOUND, FIXED, AND VERIFIED (0.19.2 sv CFE42736F91C2B7DA79436E). di_changecount is MXFS's cross-node freshness stamp (compared by P-RELOAD-IDENTICAL, P3-REFUSE-OLDER, P189-RELOG-BEHIND-DISK and the epoch gates), and sess6 deliberately FORCED one bump per CORE-logging transaction so it is a true modification counter. But the release drain's own gated re-log IS a CORE-logging transaction, so every re-log bumped it — the same shape as the pending_seq runaway, on the counter that matters more. Left alone, a re-log storm walks our in-core version past the platter's purely from our own repair attempts, and the inode then looks strictly AHEAD of home, which is exactly the state P34F-RELOAD-SELFAHEAD-SKIP refuses to adopt over: THE REPAIR DEFEATS THE RECOVERY THAT WOULD HAVE RESOLVED IT. FIX (sess382 GPT ruling 2 Q1): xfs_trans_log_inode suppresses BOTH the upstream clean->dirty i_version bump AND the MXFS forced per-CORE-transaction bump when i_mxfs_pipe_relog is set. A re-log is a new PUBLICATION ATTEMPT, not a new logical modification — a repeated publication of version 10 must still carry changecount 10. Safe by construction: the re-log site logs XFS_ILOG_CORE on an otherwise untouched in-core inode and never calls xfs_trans_ichgtime, so the only mutation it would make to the persisted image IS this bump; i_mxfs_pipe_relog has exactly one setter. The XFS_LI_DIRTY transition still runs so the re-log can still be flushed. A/B lever mxfs.relog_holds_version. VERIFIED by the ruling's own experiment — paired A/B on ONE build, knob flipped at runtime, identical injected fault, identical 120 re-logs, reading the in-core logical version out of P383-HOME-VS-OWED: relog_holds_version=0 -> iver runs 4 -> 403 while cc_home stays FROZEN at 3 (about 400 phantom modifications manufactured by our own repair). relog_holds_version=1 -> iver goes 4 -> 5 and STOPS; the delta across 120 re-logs is ZERO, and 5 is exactly the two real touches the test performed. That is the ruling's stated falsifier ('post-fix: both deltas are zero') satisfied. SCOPE NOTE, stated so it is not overread: this fix does NOT by itself prevent the wedge — both arms above still WEDGED because reldefer_reload was 0 in both to force the re-log storm. It removes the FALSE SELFAHEAD, not the wedge. ALSO MEASURED, and it is why a board A/B is the wrong instrument here: dir_reuse_coherency at 32/caw produced P146V-UNLANDED=0 in BOTH arms — that criterion never exercises the drain's re-log at all, so the knob had nothing to suppress and the two arms were indistinguishable (P34F 16 vs 13, P-RELOAD-IDENTICAL 4875 vs 5264, both noise). The re-log path is RARE under ordinary board workloads; only the fault injection drives it hard enough to measure. Full board on 0.19.2: 26 PASS, 1 FLAKY, 0 FAIL, 1 policy cell.
defects.disposition: FIXED AND VERIFIED sess382, MXFS 0.19.4. CAUSE (RULE 4, proven end to end and broader than this entry was opened on): xfs_iflush has ELEVEN 'safe skip' fences that return error=0 WITHOUT stamping i_mxfs_pub_flush_seq. The publication obligation is pending_seq != durable_seq and durable only advances from flush_seq at xfs_iflush_finish, so a fenced flush leaves it permanently open. The release drain then re-logs the clean-but-unlanded core (P146V) on every attempt, and xfs_trans_log_inode incremented pending_seq each time — THE DRAIN'S OWN REPAIR FEEDING THE COUNTER IT WAITS ON (measured: pending 6 -> 730 with flush frozen at 6). Badness stayed pinned at OBLIG_OPEN, the no-progress bound expired, and mxfs_inode_wedge pinned the grant and force-shut-down the WHOLE MOUNT. The reason it usually recovered: the ONLY path that reconciles the ledger is the adopt inside mxfs_dlm_reload_inode, and i_dlm_stale had NO RELEASE-PATH CONSUMER — only access paths honored it — so survival depended on a local reader coincidentally touching the inode inside the bound. PATCH (three changes, each at a proven link): (A) ONE CHOKEPOINT — xfs_iflush's flush_out sets a new i_mxfs_pub_fenced when returning success without having stamped flush_seq while an obligation is open; checked in one place instead of at eleven fences, and it covers any fence added later. (B) A RELEASE-SIDE CONSUMER — mxfs_dlm_bast_dwork_fn (the retry worker, OUTSIDE the drain, so not the documented ABBA folio-lock site) drives the reload the fence asked for, before the deadline check that would wedge, bounded at MXFS_RELDEFER_RELOAD_MAX=3, restamping progress ONLY on an actual obligation close. It never touches durable_seq and invents no verdict: the adopt's existing keep-guards stay the sole authority and a dropped committed change is still reported by P177-OBLIGATION-DROPPED-AT-ADOPT, so a bailed adopt leaves the obligation open and the wedge still fires — the fail-closed escalation is preserved and only its FALSE firings are removed. (C) THE COUNTER RUNAWAYS — xfs_trans_log_inode no longer increments pending_seq, nor bumps i_version/di_changecount, when i_mxfs_pipe_relog marks the drain's own gated re-log; a republication is not a new logical modification. Also fixed a bug in the fix: xfs_inode_alloc is kmem_cache_alloc and NOT zalloc, so both new fields had to join the explicit reset block or a recycled inode inherits a previous incarnation's verdict. VERIFIED TWO WAYS, both paired A/B on ONE build with the lever flipped at runtime. (1) AGAINST THE INJECTED CAUSE. mxfs.iflush_fence_fault_ino makes a chosen inode's flush take exactly the fence shape; tests/iflush_fence_wedge.sh drives it in ~90s. Pre-fix 0.17.6: 721 fence hits, pending 6 -> 730 with flush frozen at 6, P-INODE-WEDGE tries=714 causes=0x1, MOUNT=DOWN — the IDENTICAL signature to test31's natural occurrence, so the injection reproduces the real chain. On 0.18.0: reldefer_reload=1 -> 4 hits, durable 6->10 (reload adopted and reconciled), P177=1, NO WEDGE, MOUNT=UP; reldefer_reload=0 -> 689 hits, durable stuck at 6, WEDGE, MOUNT=DOWN. Repeated on 0.18.1, 0.18.2, 0.19.2. (2) AGAINST THE NATURAL CAUSE — no fault injection, real workload (dirent_durability + ag_strand_repair at 32/caw), 0.19.4, all three levers flipped together, with ONLY the episode observation window shortened (mxfs.reldefer_noprogress_ms 60000->2000; this shortens how long the test waits, it does not alter the fences, obligations or deferrals, and is the method the sess382 GPT ruling explicitly prescribes): PRE-FIX ARM — P119-NONEX-FLUSH-SKIP=67, P176-OBLIGATION-OPEN=8, P228-RELBAR-DEFER=10, P-INODE-WEDGE=1, ag_strand_repair FAIL at 240s/240s with only 18/32 nodes passing, and ALL 32 NODES LEFT NOMOUNT. FIXED ARM — P119=51 (comparable fence rate, same workload), P176=0, P228=0, P-INODE-WEDGE=0, ag_strand_repair PASS at 81s, NO node left unmounted. The obligation never opens, so the wedge precursor never forms. UNCHANGED ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA: full 32/caw board at SHIPPING DEFAULTS green on 0.18.0, 0.18.1, 0.18.2, 0.19.0, 0.19.2 and 0.19.4 — final run 26 PASS, 1 FLAKY, 0 FAIL, 1 policy cell. The FLAKY count improved from 2 to 1 over this work. SCOPE LIMITS, stated rather than hidden: (a) the natural arm required the episode bound shortened 60s->2s to bring the wedge inside a test window — the cause is unmodified but the observation window is not the shipped one; (b) a fence whose adopt keeps bailing still reaches the wedge after 3 attempts, by design (fail-closed), so this removes FALSE wedges, not the escalation itself; (c) a separate finding from this work — ONE wedge took all 32 mounts down and left two nodes un-reprepable — is containment, not this defect, and is recorded against D-WITHDRAWN-NODE-CASCADE-NONCONTAINMENT-474.

defects.summary: ONE node's routine clean unmount disarms SCSI-PR fencing for the ENTIRE cluster, and no node can detect it. MXFS reserves the shared LUN with type 0x05 WRITE EXCLUSIVE - REGISTRANTS ONLY (WE-RO), a SINGLE-HOLDER reservation type: the holder is whichever node reserved first. SPC-4 releases a registrants-only reservation when the holder's registration is removed, and MXFS retires its own registration unconditionally at put_super. Nothing re-reserves. From that moment every fence attempt by every survivor returns kind=NO_RESERVATION(8) proves_excl=0, so the next peer death is unrecoverable and (via D-FENCE-PRECONDITION-FAILURE-RECORDED-TERMINAL-381) permanently bricks the filesystem. No mass departure, no dirty slice, no crash is required - one 0.49-second clean unmount.
defects.mechanism: TWO code facts compose. (1) SINGLE-HOLDER TYPE: dlm/v5_mount.c:4320 (and :4031, dlm/mount.c:1980, :2191) call mxfs_scsipr_reserve(), which issues PROUT RESERVE with PR_TYPE_WR_EX_RO (pal/linux/user.c:1317, kern.c equivalent). Its return value is DISCARDED at all four call sites and a RESERVATION CONFLICT is read as 'another node holds it, fine'. Exactly one I_T nexus in the cluster is therefore the reservation holder. pal/linux/xfs_super.c:~1727 then unregisters that node's key unconditionally at put_super (made mandatory and fail-closed by D-CLEAN-UNMOUNT-LEAKS-PR-REGISTRATION-377), and SPC-4 releases a *_REGISTRANTS_ONLY reservation when its holder's registration is removed. There is no periodic reservation-health check anywhere in the tree, and no survivor re-RESERVEs. (2) THE ADMISSION GATE IS SELF-FULFILLING: mxfs_scsipr_validate_admission() (dlm/scsipr.c:557+, the sess378 P303-FENCECAP gate) refuses the mount unless a WE-RO reservation is HELD - but dlm/v5_mount.c:4320 calls mxfs_scsipr_reserve() on the line immediately BEFORE it, so the gate validates a reservation it just created. It is structurally incapable of observing the disarmed state. Consequence: 31 live nodes each logged P303-FENCECAP-OK at their own mount and every one of them believed fencing was armed for the 30 minutes it was not.
defects.evidence:
SESS381 DIRECT MEASUREMENT, 32/caw, 0.15.10 sv F73F08F0690BB7561EF6930, all 32 nodes mounted. Harness: tests/pr_reservation_ownership_probe.sh (read-only, re-runnable).

  [4] CONSEQUENCE PROVEN END-TO-END. ~30 min later, `virsh destroy test3` (hard kill, key still registered). Death detected at t+66s. Elected prover test32 logged: 'P236-FENCE-INTENT slot=2 victim=1268531449 ... fencing intent is DURABLE; the PREEMPT AND ABORT may now be issued', then 'P236-FENCEKIND node=1268531449 kind=NO_RESERVATION(8) proves_excl=0 gen=2121 rc=0 [prover slot=2 term=1]' and 'P238-FENCE-UNPROVEN slot=2 ... proved NO exclusion ... Recovery is BLOCKED on unproven exclusion'. The other 30 survivors all logged P236-FENCE-ATTEMPT-BUSY (prover=3388166754). This is the SAME NO_RESERVATION(8) sess379 captured after a 28-of-32 mass unmount and could not explain; the minimal trigger is one clean unmount.

Remounting test1 logged 'P-PR-PROBE own key 0x2ecf4e95 visible, 64 key(s) registered' then 'P303-FENCECAP-OK registrants=64 gen=2123 - fencing capability validated at admission: WE-RO held, persistence active, key view complete, own key present, PREEMPT AND ABORT issuable' - while two independent observers read NONE HELD both immediately before and immediately after. The gate passed because test1's own RESERVE, one line earlier, had re-created the reservation; put_super then released it again (post-state: NONE HELD, keys=62).
  [6] FIX PROPERTY PROVEN ON THE REAL TARGET. tests/pr_all_registrants_semantics.sh, same LUN, scratch key from an unmounted node so no MXFS registration was touched: REGISTER 0xdeadbeef -> RESERVE --prout-type=7 -> READ RESERVATION = 'Key=0x0, scope: LU_SCOPE, type: Write Exclusive, all registrants' -> UNREGISTER the holder key -> READ RESERVATION STILL 'Write Exclusive, all registrants', keycount 63->62. WE-AR survives removal of the reserving node's registration; WE-RO does not. Part 2: two distinct nexuses register KA and KB, KA RESERVEs type 7, then KB RESERVEs type 7 -> rc=0 GOOD (not RESERVATION CONFLICT), so every node may reserve and the reservation is self-healing. RELEASE by any registrant works and raises a Unit Attention to the other initiators (observed as 'PR in (Read reservation): Unit attention' on the next PRIN). Target capability: P303-FENCECAP type_mask=0xea01, i.e. REPORT CAPABILITIES resp[4]=0xEA with bit7 set = WR_EX_AR supported (pal/linux/kern.c:3181 documents the bit layout).
  [7] CLEANUP VERIFIED: scratch keys removed, 'RESERVATION: NONE HELD keys=62 distinct=31' - pre-experiment state restored.

defects.found: sess381, 2026-08-20, direct rig measurement while answering step 0 of D-DIRTY-SLICE-DEPARTURE-RETIRES-FENCE-KEY-UNMOUNTABLE-379
defects.disposition:
FIXED AND VERIFIED sess381, 0.16.1 sv 1161F3EF30ADC4DC39E167C, 32/caw.

CAUSE (RULE 4, proven before any patch): MXFS reserved the shared LUN with SPC type 0x05 WRITE EXCLUSIVE - REGISTRANTS ONLY, a SINGLE-HOLDER type, and retires its own registration unconditionally at put_super. SPC releases a *_REGISTRANTS_ONLY reservation when its holder's registration is removed, and nothing in the tree re-reserved. Measured directly, not inferred: PRIN READ FULL STATUS named ONE holder (test1's nexus) out of 64 registrations; one clean `umount` of that node (real 0m0.056s, 0.49s wall) took the LU to 'NONE HELD' with 31 nodes still mounted; it stayed NONE HELD across a 30s poll; and a later `virsh destroy` of a DIFFERENT node then fenced with 'P236-FENCEKIND kind=NO_RESERVATION(8) proves_excl=0', leaving the filesystem permanently unmountable.

FIX (proto-gen 4 -> 5, which excludes mixed-version clusters as layers 1-3 of the gate require):
  1. RESERVE type is now 0x07 WRITE EXCLUSIVE - ALL REGISTRANTS (MXFS_SCSIPR_RESV_TYPE, dlm/scsipr.h). Every registrant is a holder, so the reservation survives until the LAST registration goes.
  2. mxfs_pal_scsi_pr_reserve()/…_preempt() take the type; the preempt CDB now carries the type ACTUALLY IN FORCE (ctx->resv_type_seen) instead of a hardcoded 0x05.
  3. The kernel PAL decided `held` from the reservation KEY. SPC reports that key as ZERO for an all-registrants type (MEASURED: 'Key=0x0'), so the old test would have reported a live WE-AR reservation as 'none held' and failed every fence closed. `held` is now decided by the TYPE.
  4. mxfs_scsipr_reserve()'s return value is no longer discarded at any of the four call sites, and RESERVATION CONFLICT is no longer read as 'someone else holds it, fine' — it is read back and classified (P304-RESV-CONFLICT / -BENIGN), and an incompatible reservation refuses the mount.
  5. The admission gate was self-fulfilling: mxfs_scsipr_reserve() ran on the line before it, so P303-FENCECAP-OK could report 'WE-RO held' on a LUN that had no reservation until that same mount created one (OBSERVED). Mounts now call mxfs_scsipr_observe_reservation() FIRST and log P304-PREOBSERVE — the pre-existing state, before this node touches anything. The gate additionally requires caps.we_ar and refuses a reservation of the wrong type (P303-FENCECAP-NOWEAR / -WRONGTYPE).
  6. Fence path and certificate re-check now accept EITHER Write Exclusive form via mxfs_pr_type_excludes_nonregistrants(), since that — not 'is it the type we would have created' — is the property an exclusion proof rests on.
  7. dlm/scsipr.c refuses a PREEMPT whose SARK equals our own key (P304-PREEMPT-SELFKEY): SPC protects the issuer's own registration from its own PREEMPT, so it fences nobody and would remove our sibling nexus.
  8. pal/linux/user.c built the PROUT CDB as `cdb[2] = (type & 0x0F) << 4`, putting the type in the SCOPE field on every PROUT. Corrected to the low nibble, matching the kernel backend and upstream sd_pr_out_command()'s `cmd[2] = type`.
  9. A NINTH check was found ONLY BY RUNNING THE RIG, and it mattered: dlm/disklock.c:5007 and 5261 (the certificate minter and its verifier) also hardcoded `== WR_EX_RO`. On the first patched build the fence PROVED exclusion and the minter then REFUSED to certify it — 'P236-FENCE-NO-RESV resv_type=0x07' / 'P238-FENCE-UNRECORDED ... exclusion was PROVED but the certificate is not durable ... this slice is BLOCKED' — the worst possible outcome, because the victim key is consumed by then. Both now use the same helper.

FIX PROPERTY PROVEN ON THE TARGET FIRST (tests/pr_all_registrants_semantics.sh, scratch key from an unmounted node): RESERVE type 7 -> 'Key=0x0, LU_SCOPE, Write Exclusive, all registrants'; UNREGISTER the reserving key -> the reservation IS STILL HELD (keys 63->62); a SECOND registrant's RESERVE type 7 -> rc=0 GOOD, not RESERVATION CONFLICT. Target capability confirmed from REPORT CAPABILITIES type_mask=0xea01 (resp[4] bit7 = WR_EX_AR).

VERIFICATION THAT EXERCISES THE CAUSE — tests/fence_lifetime_ab.sh replays the EXACT minimal sequence that bricked the filesystem on 0.15.10. Run TWICE with disjoint node sets:
  run A (unmount test1, kill test3, observe test2) and run B (unmount test7, kill test11, observe test20). Both: RESULT: PASS (all assertions).
    - umount wall 0.476s / 0.505s — the same operation, to the millisecond, that disarmed the cluster before;
    - 'reservation SURVIVED the holder's clean unmount' (keys 64->62, still all-registrants) where 0.15.10 went to NONE HELD;
    - 'P236-FENCEKIND kind=PREEMPT_ABORT_DONE(16) proves_excl=1' where 0.15.10 gave NO_RESERVATION(8) proves_excl=0;
    - 'P236-FENCE-CERTIFIED ... kind=PREEMPT_ABORT_DONE resv=0x07 ... exclusion is PROVED and durable' and 'P238-RECOV-LEASE ... stage=2 ... this slice may now be replayed';
    - the unmounted node REMOUNTED without re-mkfs, where 0.15.10 aborted every mount after 36.4s with four P236-CLAIM-UNCERTIFIED refusals.

BOARD: full 28-row 32/caw board re-run on 0.16.1 — 27 PASS, 0 FAIL, 1 POLICY cell (open_defects, red by RULE 6 design while the ledger is non-empty). Acceptance criteria unchanged.

NOT CLOSED BY THIS, and deliberately so: D-FENCE-PRECONDITION-FAILURE-RECORDED-TERMINAL-381 is untouched. A fence that submits no command is still recorded as a terminal 'exclusion not proved' and still bricks the slice; this fix only removes the most common way of reaching that state. D-DIRTY-SLICE-DEPARTURE-RETIRES-FENCE-KEY-UNMOUNTABLE-379 arm (B) is also untouched: under WE-AR the reservation survives, but a node that retires its key while leaving a dirty slice still leaves nothing for a survivor to PREEMPT AND ABORT.

defects.summary: A fence that NEVER ISSUED A COMMAND is recorded on disk as a terminal 'exclusion not proved', which permanently bricks the filesystem. mxfs_scsipr_fence_node() returns MXFS_FENCE_KIND_NO_RESERVATION (dlm/scsipr.c:437) BEFORE the PROUT PREEMPT AND ABORT at :459 - nothing is consumed, the victim's key is still registered, the attempt is fully retryable. The caller nevertheless publishes it as a durable stage=1 recovery guard, and from then on EVERY mount is refused with P236-CLAIM-UNCERTIFIED, forever, even after the missing precondition is restored. Only re-mkfs recovers. MEASURED: mount aborted after 36s with four identical refusals while 30 healthy peers stayed mounted.
defects.mechanism: dlm/scsipr.c:294 mxfs_scsipr_fence_node() has a pre-command precondition check at :416-438: PRIN READ RESERVATION, and if (ret==-EOPNOTSUPP || !resv.held || resv.type != WR_EX_RO) it logs P-PR-NORESV, sets out->kind=MXFS_FENCE_KIND_NO_RESERVATION and RETURNS 0 - the PROUT PREEMPT AND ABORT at :459 is never reached. No target state changes; the victim key remains registered; a later attempt would have strictly MORE information. But the caller has already published a DURABLE fencing intent (P236-FENCE-INTENT) and now records the outcome in the victim slot's on-disk recovery guard as stage=1 with no certificate. Every subsequent claimant reads that guard and refuses: 'P236-CLAIM-UNCERTIFIED ... fencing ATTEMPT only - no exclusion has been proved yet; refusing the claim. Nothing on this slice may be replayed, purged, repaired or published.' Nothing in the tree ever re-opens a guard in that state, so a TRANSIENT precondition failure is converted into a PERMANENT loss of the filesystem. The state machine has only 'proved' and 'attempted', and is missing the distinction that matters: whether a state-changing command could have reached the target at all.
defects.evidence:
