FIXED AND VERIFIED sess381, 0.17.0 sv 7BE80C7FD64AF310791A322, 32/caw — FOR THE CASE THIS ENTRY DESCRIBES, WHICH IS THE PRE-COMMAND CASE. Read the SCOPE paragraph at the end before treating fencing as sound.

CAUSE (RULE 4): dlm/scsipr.c's precondition check at :416-438 returns MXFS_FENCE_KIND_NO_RESERVATION BEFORE the PROUT PREEMPT AND ABORT at :459 — no command is submitted, nothing is consumed, the victim key stays registered — yet the caller published the outcome as a durable stage=1 recovery guard that nothing in the tree ever re-opened. The retry path did not merely fail; it did not exist: the heartbeat monitor's fire_dead sets ctx->monitored[slot] = false immediately before firing expire_cb, so a death fires expire_cb EXACTLY ONCE, ever, and ctx->blocked[] (which records the refusal) is a purely reporting array that nothing consumes.

FIX — sess381 RULE-5 ruling 2 (ccmemory ccloop-c7ee71c6-sess381-GPT-ruling2-fence-retry-mechanics), its Increment 1, with two of my proposals CORRECTED by that ruling:
  1. THE COMMAND-SUBMISSION BOUNDARY, IN MEMORY: enum mxfs_fence_phase {PRECOMMAND, MAY_HAVE_SUBMITTED, VERIFIED} on struct mxfs_fence_result, set at the two lines that bracket the command — NOT derived from the kind, because a later refactor could detect reservation loss after submission and the reason would then lie.
  2. THE BOUNDARY, DURABLE: MXFS_RECOV_F_FENCE_CMD_MAY_HAVE_RUN (0x8) on the recovery descriptor, written by the new mxfs_disklock_recovery_fence_arm_submit() and not returning until durable. CORRECTION FROM THE RULING: I had proposed the opposite polarity (an F_FENCE_PRECOMMAND bit set at intent and CLEARED before submitting). That needed a mutable bit among sticky ones and had to succeed at clearing on a path that must not fail. MAY_HAVE_RUN is monotonic, is clear on every early return by construction, and its NAME is the contract: it may never be read as proof that submission did happen.
  3. mxfs_scsipr_fence_node() takes an arm_submit callback and calls it on the LAST LINE before the PROUT. If it cannot be made durable the command is NOT issued (P304-FENCE-NOARM) and the result comes back PRECOMMAND — an unrecordable preempt consumes the victim key and is indistinguishable from one that never happened.
  4. A FENCE-RETRY WORKER whose QUEUE IS THE ON-DISK DESCRIPTOR. Fires only for stage==FENCING + MAY_HAVE_RUN clear + prover==us (mxfs_disklock_recovery_fence_retryable()); the in-memory latch is only a wake-up accelerator and every firing re-reads the descriptor before acting, with a 60s descriptor sweep behind it. Backoff 250ms..6s capped with jitter, and it NEVER GIVES UP on an attempt count — abandoning a consumed-nothing attempt is precisely this defect. Thread is created lazily on the first retryable outcome, so a healthy cluster never pays for it.
  5. CORRECTION FROM THE RULING, and it stopped me writing something dangerous: I had considered re-arming the heartbeat monitor (keep the slot monitored, let expire_cb fire again). The ruling calls that ACTIVELY DANGEROUS — expire_cb means 'a live identity became dead, do the one-time retirement', and re-entering it would repeat dead-node retirement, notifications, slice-recovery creation, purge and successor rebasing, and entangle fencing liveness with heartbeat sampling. Driving it from the mount admission path was rejected too: a node that is not yet a member must not become a fencing authority, or repeated mounts become a fencing storm. Certification instead fires an explicit wake-up (P304-FENCE-RETRY-OK -> v5_dispatch_slice_recovery) that does NOT re-enter the death path.
  6. A PER-SLOT SINGLE-PROVER GUARD (ctx->fence_prove_busy, a thin wrapper around v5_pr_fence_prove so all five call sites participate). The fencing-attempt lease is per NODE, so two local threads could both 'resume our own attempt' and both issue a P&A; the second would take RESERVATION CONFLICT and classify as RACE_LOST at MAY_HAVE_SUBMITTED — turning our own success into a slice blocked pending reconciliation. The disklock CAS cannot catch that: both threads hold the same valid lease.
  7. Operator text now states the durable phase and the scheduler state instead of implying terminality: P238-FENCE-PENDING (phase=PRECOMMAND command_may_have_run=no retry=automatic next_retry_ms=N attempt=N) for the retryable case; P238-FENCE-UNPROVEN is now reserved for command_may_have_run=YES.

The opposite case is now REPRESENTABLE for the first time (it was previously conflated with this one) and it is still terminal: an attempt at MAY_HAVE_SUBMITTED is not retried, and mxfs_disklock_recovery_fence_takeover() does not consult MXFS_RECOV_F_FENCE_CMD_MAY_HAVE_RUN before letting a successor issue a fresh P&A. defects.summary: The persistent reservation that ALL of MXFS's fencing rests on is validated at MOUNT TIME ONLY and never again. Nothing in the tree re-reads it periodically, so if it is lost after admission — by a RELEASE or CLEAR from any initiator, an administrative action, a target reset that loses PR state, or a loss of every registration — every mounted node goes on believing fencing is armed, and the first peer death discovers otherwise. sess381 removed the ROUTINE way of reaching that state (D-PR-RESERVATION-SINGLE-HOLDER-UNMOUNT-DISARMS-FENCING-381: a single clean unmount) but not the state itself.
defects.mechanism: mxfs_scsipr_validate_admission() (dlm/scsipr.c) is called exactly once per mount, from dlm/v5_mount.c's CAW admission path. Nothing calls it again. mxfs_scsipr_self_check() runs periodically but checks the KEY TABLE (own key present, registrant count vs live members), not the reservation. mxfs_scsipr_exclusion_holds() does re-read the reservation, but only on the recovery path for a node that is ALREADY fencing a specific victim — i.e. after the death that the missing reservation makes unrecoverable. There is therefore no path on which a healthy cluster learns that its exclusion guarantee has evaporated. Under WE-AR the reservation is released only when the last registration goes, so the failure is far less reachable than the WE-RO case, but PTPL loss on a target restart, an operator's sg_persist --out --clear, or a mass registration loss all still reach it, and the sess378 admission gate is by construction blind to all of them once the mount is up.
defects.evidence:
SESS381 CODE FACT, verifiable by grep: `grep -rn 'validate_admission' --include=*.c .` returns exactly one call site (dlm/v5_mount.c, the mount path). No timer, workqueue, heartbeat hook or monitor tick invokes it or any other reservation read.
SESS381 THE FAILURE MODE WAS OBSERVED LIVE on 0.15.10, before the WE-AR fix removed its routine trigger: 31 nodes stayed mounted for over 30 minutes on a LUN carrying NO reservation at all ('RESERVATION: NONE HELD keys=62 distinct=31' from two independent observers, polled every 5s), each having logged P303-FENCECAP-OK at its own mount, and none of them noticed. The first thing that noticed was the fence of the next node to die — by which point the slice is unrecoverable.
SESS381 RELEASE IS OBSERVABLE AND UNHANDLED: releasing the reservation raises a Unit Attention on other initiators, MEASURED as 'PR in (Read reservation): Unit attention' on the next PRIN from a different node. MXFS's PAL retries UA but nothing treats it as the signal it is.
defects.next: sess381 RULE-5 ruling (ccmemory ccloop-c7ee71c6-sess381-GPT-ruling-we-ar-fencing-lifetime), which is explicit that this must NOT be built as a 32-way poll: 1) Event-driven checks first — at mount, on any unmount anomaly, on a target reset / Unit Attention, and unconditionally in the fencing path itself before a PREEMPT is issued (fence progress must never depend on waiting for a periodic thread). 2) ONE elected PR-health maintainer doing the standing check, plus a slow JITTERED audit by the others, plus cached health with a bounded validity interval. 32 PRINs per heartbeat interval would serialize on the target's PR control path for no benefit. 3) Treat 'no Write Exclusive reservation while registrants are live' as a HIGH-SEVERITY SAFETY EVENT, not routine drift to be silently self-healed: re-reserving restores future exclusion but proves nothing about the interval during which non-registrants could write. Emit an attributable event carrying PR generation, registration count, type, scope and path; repair under serialization by the elected maintainer; revalidate membership and registration state before declaring fencing healthy again. 4) Verification: with the cluster healthy and mounted, clear the reservation out of band (sg_persist --out --release from a registrant, as tests/pr_all_registrants_semantics.sh does) and assert that the cluster DETECTS it and says so, rather than discovering it at the next death; then assert it repairs and that the repair is reported as a safety event, not as normal.

defects.summary: A fencing attempt that MAY have submitted a PREEMPT-family command, but whose outcome was never established, has no reconciliation path: it is recorded terminally, it is never retried, and a successor that takes the attempt lease over issues a FRESH PREEMPT AND ABORT without consulting whether the predecessor's command may still be in flight. Either way the slice can be blocked forever, and the successor path can put two PREEMPT AND ABORTs on the wire against the same victim. sess381 made this state REPRESENTABLE for the first time (before that it was conflated with the pre-command case, which is why it went unnoticed) but did NOT fix it.
defects.mechanism: Three code facts. (1) dlm/v5_mount.c v5_pr_fence_prove_locked's outcome legs: an attempt at phase MXFS_FENCE_PHASE_MAY_HAVE_SUBMITTED takes the P238-FENCE-UNPROVEN branch, is explicitly NOT armed for retry (v5_fence_retry_disarm), and the descriptor keeps MXFS_RECOV_F_FENCE_CMD_MAY_HAVE_RUN set, so mxfs_disklock_recovery_fence_retryable() correctly refuses it forever. That is the deliberate, safe half — but nothing ever reconciles it, so the slice stays unreplayable and every mount is refused. (2) The certificate WRITE failing after a PROVED exclusion (P238-FENCE-UNRECORDED / P236-FENCE-CERTIFY-FAIL) is likewise terminal, with no attempt to re-verify and re-CAS the certificate — the sess381 ruling calls this too pessimistic. (3) dlm/v5_mount.c:~3783 DOES take over a dead prover's fencing attempt (mxfs_disklock_recovery_fence_takeover, gated on v5_node_is_dead) and then calls v5_pr_fence_prove to issue a NEW PREEMPT AND ABORT — WITHOUT reading MXFS_RECOV_F_FENCE_CMD_MAY_HAVE_RUN. The bit exists as of 0.17.0 and this path ignores it, so a successor can issue a second P&A while the predecessor's may still be in flight, and if it instead finds the victim key ABSENT it cannot distinguish 'my predecessor's P&A completed' from 'the victim unregistered cleanly' or 'someone issued a plain PREEMPT without the abort'.
defects.evidence:
SESS381 CODE FACTS, all verifiable by inspection of 0.17.0 sv 7BE80C7FD64AF310791A322: the MAY_HAVE_SUBMITTED leg in v5_pr_fence_prove_locked calls v5_fence_retry_disarm and logs 'command_may_have_run=YES ... this state is NOT retried automatically'; mxfs_disklock_recovery_fence_retryable() returns 0 for any descriptor carrying MXFS_RECOV_F_FENCE_CMD_MAY_HAVE_RUN; and v5_mount.c's P238-FENCE-TAKEOVER block reads the descriptor via mxfs_disklock_recovery_read() and tests only stage, fence_prover_node and v5_node_is_dead — `grep -n 'MAY_HAVE_RUN' dlm/v5_mount.c` shows no use in that path.
SESS381 THE TERMINAL OUTCOME IS THE SAME ONE ALREADY MEASURED: a slice left uncertified produces 'P236-CLAIM-UNCERTIFIED ... refusing the claim' on every subsequent mount and 'MXFS mount ABORTED: slot mask ... still requires recovery', captured live on 0.15.10 (mount wall 36.4s, four identical refusals, 30 healthy peers up). The pre-command route to that state is closed as of 0.17.0; this route is not.
SESS381 THE PRE-EXISTING CODE ALREADY NAMES THE HOLE it cannot fill: the takeover comment says 'it is exactly the crash hole GPT flagged (a P&A that completed before the prover died left its proof only in volatile memory)', and P238-FENCE-UNRECORDED says 'exclusion was PROVED but the certificate is not durable. The victim key is consumed, so no successor can prove it again: this slice is BLOCKED and needs operator action'.
defects.next: sess381 RULE-5 ruling 2, Increment 3 (ccmemory ccloop-c7ee71c6-sess381-GPT-ruling2-fence-retry-mechanics), which flags this as the HIGHEST-RISK part of the whole change set — a mistake here creates overlapping commands or certifies exclusion that was never established. 1) A RECONCILIATION path for MAY_HAVE_RUN, entered instead of resubmission. It must obtain a COHERENT PR snapshot: complete untruncated READ KEYS, READ RESERVATION, own registration present, expected Write Exclusive form, and a stable PR generation across the compound observation. One truncated or changing response is NEVER absence. 2) VICTIM KEY ABSENT proves present exclusion only if MXFS separately prevents the retired incarnation from re-registering — that anti-rejoin property must be made explicit and is currently open as D-FENCED-VICTIM-MAY-REREGISTER. If it holds, certify under a NEW kind whose meaning is 'verified exclusion from a coherent PR state after an earlier command may have executed'; never claim this node completed a P&A it did not observe. 3) VICTIM KEY PRESENT does not prove no old command is in flight. Before a second P&A, establish a bound covering transport timeout, target completion, fabric error recovery, local abort/drain, and the dead prover's inability to submit. Without such a bound, stay in reconciliation rather than assuming an interval is long enough. 4) GATE mxfs_disklock_recovery_fence_takeover() on MXFS_RECOV_F_FENCE_CMD_MAY_HAVE_RUN: a takeover of a bit-set attempt must enter reconciliation, not resubmission. 5) RETRY THE CERTIFICATE WRITE (re-verify, re-CAS under the still-held term) instead of going straight to operator-only on P236-FENCE-CERTIFY-FAIL. 6) Only AFTER this is green, make post-PREEMPT verification mandatory (Increment 4) — landing it earlier creates a new permanent-blocking path. 7) Verification needs adversarial fault injection, not a happy path: kill the prover between the durable arm and the PROUT; kill it after the PROUT but before certify; fail the certificate write; and run each with the victim key both present and absent. tests/fence_precondition_retry.sh is the pattern to extend (it drives a real precondition failure on a live 32-node cluster with no code knob).

defects.summary: Three fail-OPEN arms in the consumers of an on-disk TERMINAL recovery-outcome record, found by finally running the sess333 RULE-5 pre-rig unit checks against the real LUN. (A) mxfs_v5_dlm_recovery_scan_outcomes() is a FOURTH import site that performs NO validation: a crc-valid record with outcome=99 (not TERMINAL_REFUSED) was imported as a real AG-scoped verdict and also fed v5_closure_note_terminal(), which authorizes the selective grant purge. sess334 item B deduped three sites behind mxfs_freplay_import_verdict(); this one was missed. (B) mxfs_disklock_recovery_read_outcome() has NO fs_gen gate and the scan iterates all 64 slots blind, so a PRE-MKFS GHOST sector quarantines the freshly-formatted filesystem. mkfs does not reliably zero the disklock region on this target stack, so surviving GUARD sectors are EXPECTED and hb_gen_foreign is exactly the mechanism meant to make them harmless. (C) an FSWIDE quarantine imported by the registration scan does NOT refuse the mount: the barrier's two unconditional FSWIDE gates both run ~0.5s BEFORE the scan, so the mount ADMITS a zombie whose every operation fails EIO -- precisely what xfs_mxfs_dlm.c:48457 says must never happen. Arm C needs no forgery in principle: any legitimate FSWIDE verdict published between the barrier's sweep and registration -- the late-mount case the scan was BUILT for -- admits the same zombie.

(2) registration scan (v5_mount.c:6916) -- loops 0..63, calls read_outcome, and on rc==0 calls v5_closure_note_terminal(ctx,slot,&oc) + quar_cb(data,slot,&oc) with NO validation at all. (3) shared classifier (xfs_mxfs_dlm.c:47038 -> mxfs_freplay_import_verdict:46941) -- the ONLY validating path; rejects wrong outcome kind, unknown reason, bad domain, empty AG mask, oc->victim_slot != slot. The mount admission barrier builds its cut from get_recovery_pending_slots(), which SKIPS hb_gen_foreign records and stage >= GRANTS_RELEASED records; everything in the cut goes through the validating classifier, so the barrier is correct. The scan is what bypasses it, and it runs AFTER the barrier.
